project.name: Enterprise-Support-Agent
project.objective: Build the Enterprise AI Customer Support Agent as designed in docs/: the orchestration core and all 15 components, implementing the 79 ADPs in docs/decisions/adp/.

plan_approval.reason: User chose the wiring task first (2026-10-31)

approval.reason: Have updated the SPEC.md with all the free tier tools and services.

assumptions.text: Jev (TypeSafe) HTTP contract is assumed, not verified: POST {base_url}/v1/evaluate with {state, questions, version} and Bearer auth, returning {answers: {id: {value, confidence, index}}}. Only core.orchestrator.decisions.JevClient depends on it; verify against TypeSafe's API docs before connecting a real key.
Resolved: the Jev HTTP contract is no longer assumed; see KNOWLEDGE-205fb661 (verified from the TypeSafe API reference, implemented in M1-06b).

decisions.title: Cloud platform: AWS
decisions.text: The system runs on AWS (EKS, KMS, Secrets Manager, S3, RDS Postgres) in US and EU regions; Cedar authorization fits AWS natively. Chosen by the human during SPEC-1 discovery.

decisions.title: LLM provider: Anthropic Claude for mid and frontier tiers
decisions.text: Mid-tier and frontier tiers (CR-D1) use Anthropic Claude models; the third tier is the self-hosted open-weights model per region (RP-D4). The EV judge must come from a different model family (EV-Q3).

decisions.title: Delivery: ordered milestones
decisions.text: All 15 components plus orchestration are in scope; delivery is in ordered milestones, each a set of bounded tasks, defined in the plan.

decisions.title: Success for first production release: launch baseline
decisions.text: No numeric business targets at launch. Success = the EV-D5 release gate passes and the 8 framework scenarios pass end to end; business targets (deflection, CSAT, FCR) are set after one month of production data.

decisions.title: v1 runtime: learning deployment profile (one free VM + free managed services)
decisions.text: This is a learning project, not sold to businesses. The 79 ADPs remain the target design (AWS, US/EU regions, Kubernetes, GPUs). v1 runs on one Oracle Cloud Always Free ARM VM (Docker Compose: Temporal dev server + workers, orchestrator, API, Qdrant or Qdrant Cloud, Jaeger, OpenBao, Ollama) plus free managed services (Vercel frontend, Neon/Supabase Postgres, Qdrant Cloud, Cloudflare R2, Upstash Redis, Grafana Cloud/Langfuse, Hugging Face Spaces for the Streamlit console, GitHub Actions). LLMs: Claude mid/frontier under a hard spend cap, Groq/Gemini free tiers and Ollama for the third tier, judge and screening. Total monthly spend cap: USD 50 (provider spend limits). Every requirement is satisfied in its v1 form per the SPEC.md profile table.
decisions.source: user choice 2026-10-09; cost analysis in session

decisions.title: v1 runtime: learning deployment profile, USD 10/month cap
decisions.text: Same learning deployment profile as DECISION-b4cdefcc (one Oracle Cloud Always Free ARM VM with Docker Compose + free managed services; the 79 ADPs remain the production target), with the total monthly spend cap lowered from USD 50 to USD 10 by the human. Free tiers (Groq / Gemini, or Ollama) serve easy and mid-difficulty turns, the fallback, judge and screening; Claude serves only the hardest turns under a USD 10 console spend limit, falling back to the best free model when the limit is reached.

decisions.title: Module-owned schema
decisions.text: Chosen by Intelligent_developer_123 (2026-10-12): no remaining task may change migrations/, so each task keeps its tables' SQL in its own in-scope module and applies it through the schema_migrations ledger from M0-03 (data.migrate.psql). migrations/ holds only the M0-03 base schema. Every new tenant table still gets forced RLS, a tenant_isolation-style policy, app_owner ownership and explicit grants.

decisions.title: Scope exception: harden M2-05.4 approvals while M2-06.4 is active
decisions.text: Chosen by Intelligent_developer_123 (2026-10-24): fix the HIGH/CRITICAL approval issues found in review of the completed M2-05.4 directly in src/tools/validation/ and tests/tools/validation/ (outside the active task's scope, no replan), with this decision as the authorization. Currency policy until a trusted FX source exists: only USD money actions may run; missing, invalid or non-USD currency is denied. Approver identity for specialists needs a staff identity and a Cedar 'approve' policy (M2-09.4 / policies/); until then approvals can only be granted through a verified-approver interface and fail closed.

decisions.title: Langfuse export through plain OTLP
decisions.text: Chosen by Intelligent_developer_123 (2026-10-28, M5-01.7): traces go to Langfuse through its OTLP HTTP endpoint (Basic auth from LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY / LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY, host LANGFUSE_HOST), with the same PII-scrubbed spans that go to Jaeger. The third-party Langfuse skill and the langfuse SDK are not installed; Langfuse-specific features (prompt management, scores) are not used.

decisions.title: M5-06.7 deployment shape: SSH from the laptop, Neon Postgres, VM public IP
decisions.text: User choices 2026-10-29: (1) Claude runs setup, rollout and checks on the Oracle Always Free ARM VM over SSH from the laptop, each step shown. (2) Postgres (agent, agent_vault, agent_keys) on the Neon free tier, project from the user's notes; role creation (app_owner / app_runtime), FORCE RLS and the extra databases are verified on Neon before migrating. Everything else from deploy/compose.yaml runs on the VM, without its postgres service. (3) The API is reached on the VM's public IP over plain HTTP (OCI security list + VM firewall). Known consequence: the HTTPS web widget on Vercel cannot call a plain-HTTP API (mixed content); API, console and load test work. HTTPS is a later change (Cloudflare tunnel).

knowledge.title: Design source of truth
knowledge.text: Binding design lives in docs/decisions/checkpoint.md (decision log §3, reasoning per component), docs/decisions/adp_groups.yaml (230 decisions grouped into 79 ADPs) and one detailed document per ADP in docs/decisions/adp/. SPEC.md requirements map one-to-one to ADPs.

knowledge.title: Run gates with the project venv on PATH
knowledge.text: On this machine 'python' on PATH resolves to another tool's venv (hermes-agent) without pytest. The project venv is .venv (Python 3.12, pip install -e .[dev]); run Genesis gates as PATH="$PWD/.venv/Scripts:$PATH" genesis gate . <task>. Never install project deps into the hermes venv.

knowledge.title: Approval shorthand
knowledge.text: Intelligent_developer_123 (2026-10-14): when a review is requested and the human replies 'continue', record the independent-review approval with --human Intelligent_developer_123 --reason 'I approve'. Only an actual 'continue' reply from the human counts; never record an approval without one.

knowledge.title: Jev (TypeSafe System One) API contract
knowledge.text: Verified from TypeSafe docs (Quick start + API reference, given by the user 2026-10-15): POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, Bearer auth, body {state: string|object|array, model: 'jev-latest', questions: {id: {type: choice|score|noul, instructions, criteria}}}; choice criteria = {option: description|null} (max 255), score criteria = ordered list (2-10 levels), noul criteria optional {true, false}. Answers: choice {choice, probabilities, confidence}, score {score (weighted, between levels), legend, probabilities, confidence}, noul {noul 0-1, no confidence}; response also has model and usage. Errors: 400/401/413/415/422 = our request or key is wrong; 429/529 = retry with backoff. Implemented in core.orchestrator.decisions (M1-06b).

knowledge.title: Known bug: web dev-server crashes when the API drops mid-stream
knowledge.text: web/dev-server.js proxy: if the upstream API connection errors after the SSE response headers were sent (API restarted while a page is open), the error handler calls response.writeHead(502) -> ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT and Node exits. Fix: in the upstream 'error' handler, writeHead(502) only when !response.headersSent, otherwise response.destroy(). Found 2026-10-21 while running the demo; web/ is outside every remaining task's scope, so it needs a fix task or replan.

knowledge.title: M1-16.4 governance schema and limits
knowledge.text: safety.governance.records.apply_schema (ledger name governance_0001_decisions_archive.sql) adds checks/trace/needs_human columns to decision_records, a retained_two_years CHECK on transcript_legal_archive, and GRANT DELETE to legal_archive for the sweeper (the M0-03 trigger still refuses deletion before retain_until). Callers must run apply_schema on the main database (like knowledge tombstones). Not yet modelled: legal holds, General Counsel dual sign-off for archive reads, S3 Object Lock; require_sign_off() is not yet wired into the statechart, and disclose() is not yet wired into the API reply path.

knowledge.title: M1-17.4 findings: output sanitiser and Base64 screening
knowledge.text: (1) safety.output.checks.sanitise strips <placeholder> text even inside code fences, so a CLI snippet like '--subnet-id <id>' reaches the customer as '--subnet-id '; fix in a task whose scope covers src/safety/output/ (keep stripping real HTML outside code). (2) The pattern injection scorer does not decode Base64: a Base64-only payload passes user-message screening. Containment today comes from Jev picking tools from a closed read-only list (checked() refuses any other choice) and the planner's read-only rule; Prompt Guard (Groq-hosted) or a Base64-decode pass in screening would catch it at the edge. (3) The e2e harness in tests/e2e/test_scenarios_core.py shows the intended dispatch chain; the production dispatch hook still has to be built.

knowledge.title: M2-01.4 conversation memory: schema and limits
knowledge.text: memory.conversation.dialogue.apply_schema (ledger memory_0001_dialogue.sql) adds dialogue_turns (masked text, PK tenant/conversation/seq gives monotonic sequencing and StaleTurn=409), dialogue_summaries and dialogue_pins; needs channels.sessions.apply_schema first (FKs to conversations). Pins are case-wide: a follow-up conversation on the same case sees the earlier conversation's active pins. Case linking (memory.conversation.cases) offers only the principal's open cases (cases has no principal column; ownership comes from conversations.principal_id). Not done: Redis mutex (Postgres PK is the sequencing guard), P2 alert when pins exceed 10% of the dialogue budget (the 10-pin ceiling and pin_overflow flag stand in), wiring into the dispatch/assembler and an LLM summarizer prompt (summarize is injected).

knowledge.title: M2-02.4 long-term facts: schema, deviations and limits
knowledge.text: memory.facts.store.apply_schema (ledger memory_0002_user_facts.sql) adds user_facts with RLS on tenant AND principal (app.current_principal_id), UPDATE granted on valid_to only, and a trigger that refuses any change to a closed row. Statement and embedding are encrypted under the user's data key (data.keys), so KeyStore.shred makes facts unreadable. Deviation from MS-D19: the write path reads masked conversation text, so facts hold PII tokens rather than raw values (raw values stay in the vault); mask() is still applied symmetrically to candidate and neighbours before Jev. Limits: no pgvector in postgres:16-alpine, so nearest neighbours are computed in Python over the user's active facts; activation scoring (recency/importance/relevance, 15% profile slot) and the resolution / 24 h idle trigger are not wired yet; ALLOWED_TOOL_FIELDS is an example allow-list to be replaced by the reviewed tool registry.

knowledge.title: M2-03.4 erasure: inventory, retained stores and limits
knowledge.text: Erasure = data.erasure.ErasureWorkflow (Temporal, activities in memory.lifecycle.inventory, task queue 'erasure'): collect plan -> purge temporal, checkpoints, postgres, vault, keys -> verify every store -> signed receipt in erasure_ledger (subject named by sha256(tenant, principal), HMAC-SHA256 receipt incl. backups_expire_by = +35 days). Schemas: inventory.apply_schema (lifecycle_service role, ledger, erasure delete policy on outbound_event_log; grants re-applied each call, needs all module schemas first) and retention.apply_schema (cases.closed_at trigger, lifecycle policy on user_facts). Retained by design: decision_records (masked, scanned for raw PII: any hit fails the job), tool_audit_records (payload_enc unreadable once keys shredded), transcript_legal_archive (legal carve-out; its vault values are erased). Known limits: legal archive tokens lose their values; a stuck store makes the workflow retry up to 50 times with backoff (by design, but slow); Langfuse traces join the inventory at M5-01; fact TTL uses valid_from as last-confirmed; older versions of a live fact stay until the lineage expires (plain FK in user_facts.replaces); Temporal ticket histories rely on namespace retention for TTL. Test hygiene: tests/erasure terminates leftover ErasureWorkflow runs from interrupted sessions.

knowledge.title: M2-04.4 tool registry and provenance: shape and limits
knowledge.text: tools.registry.Registry: tools registered in code via @registry.tool(tool_id, args, description, risk, stages, min_tier, roles, trusted_outputs, author, reviewed_by), refused when tools.schemas.review fails, the description has digits (Jev rule), stages are empty, or reviewer == author; freeze() stops run-time registration. needs_approval = unreviewed OR high_risk_write/destructive. permitted() = tier >= min_tier AND roles AND stage, and T0 never gets a mutating tool even if misconfigured. shortlist: <=5 skip Jev; else one Jev noul per tool, keep relevance >= 0.50, top 5; Jev down -> [] -> human. pick = DecisionEngine.select_tool (0.80). tools.registry.provenance.check: sensitive args only from USER (exact / same number / >=0.95 similarity in masked user turns) or TOOL_FIELD (allow-listed trusted_outputs path of an earlier call, same scalar value); missing sensitive -> clarifying question; else ProvenanceViolation. Not yet: hosting tools as Temporal activities on per-system task queues (TA-D2), the CI lint that every field declares sensitivity (review() is the runtime gate), approval cards (TA-ADP-03), 'prod' -> 'production' synonym mapping (currently a violation, so the agent asks).

knowledge.title: M2-05.4 action validation: rules, property tests and limits
knowledge.text: tools.validation: verdict = max(static, Jev) over ALLOW < ASK_USER < ASK_SPECIALIST < DENY. Static: financial amount = sum of |financial=True| args as Decimal, per call, >= tenant threshold (tenant_settings.approval_threshold_usd, default 1000) -> ASK_SPECIALIST; >= senior_amount_usd needs a senior_specialist; high-risk/destructive and ANY unreviewed tool (reads too, TA-D16) -> ASK_SPECIALIST; NaN/inf -> DENY; threshold splitting: >=3 prior sub-threshold writes in 24 h and total >= 1500 -> ASK_SPECIALIST (caller passes recent amounts). Jev: choice ALLOW/ASK/DENY + noul serves-request (< 0.85 -> ask) on the masked turn plus masked proposed call; Jev down -> writes ask, reads unchanged. execute() requires an Approval bound to the call hash, approver != handler, role specialist/senior for ASK_SPECIALIST. AC-10 property tests use seeded stdlib random (hypothesis is not a project dependency; adding it needs pyproject.toml, outside this task's scope). Not yet: recent amounts come from the caller (needs amounts in the tool audit log), approval cards over the event stream / HITL queue (HL-ADP-04), DENY feeding the circuit breaker in the turn loop.

knowledge.title: M2-06.4 tool execution: shape and limits
knowledge.text: tools.execution.Executor.run(ToolCall): per-system Breaker (5 transient failures / 60 s -> open 30 s, one trial call), credentials (OBO via Identity.exchange(access_token, system.audience); service account only after Cedar Authorizer.check == allow, else FORBIDDEN before any request), egress client limited to System.hosts and refusing link-local/private/loopback literals, retries for reads and for writes to systems with idempotent_writes (key = checkpoint_id:tool_call_id, same each attempt), max 3, full jitter capped at 15 s, within RetryBudget; 401/403/4xx never retry. Output screened as tool_output (block -> withheld, data {}), spotlighted, offloaded to the object store at tool-output/<tenant>/<case>/<call>.txt when > 4 KB. Tool code reads its client/credential/key via tools.execution.current() so tool functions keep func(arguments). Temporal: one worker per system on 'tools-<system>' sized by System.concurrency; workflows call tools.execution.calls.call_tool (no Temporal retries; failures are non-retryable ApplicationErrors typed by code). Open items: tool-output blobs must join the erasure inventory and get a TTL (keyed by tenant/case for that); egress is enforced in the HTTP client, not yet at the network layer (per-pool firewall / proxy); tools.validation.execute() still calls tool.func directly and must be wired to go through the Executor; system configs (hosts, audiences, secrets from OpenBao) are not defined yet. Full suite once stalled > 10 min under a slow Temporal; reruns took 3m46s.

knowledge.title: M2-05.4 approvals hardened (DECISION-bdad33ce): design and open dependencies
knowledge.text: tools.validation.approvals.ApprovalGate (schema validation_0001_approvals.sql: approval_requests, append-only financial_writes; needs channels.sessions schema): validate -> request (row sealed by SHA-256 binding over tenant, case, conversation, customer, handler, tool, canonical args hash, decision id, tenant_settings.version, level, request id, expires_at; TTL 30 min) -> grant (approver only from verify_approver(credential); tenant match, not handler, customer level = that customer only, specialist/senior levels need the role, are never the customer, and need Cedar approve_action) -> execute (one txn with pg_advisory_xact_lock(tenant:case): fresh decision from tenant limits+version, ledger-only 24 h history, conversation ownership, open case, Cedar on ctx.resource (writes must name one), Jev; consume approval with conditional UPDATE; write financial_writes; commit; then run the tool). USD only: financial calls need currency='USD', otherwise DENY. Previews tokenize every string via safety.pii.tokens.Tokenizer; dry runs only via a reviewed read_only registry tool on the same system with the same args schema. OPEN (blocking real approvals, fail closed today): staff identity provider for verify_approver (default no_staff_identity refuses) and an approve_action policy + ApprovalRequest entity in policies/ (release-gated) -> M2-09.4. Also: Executor (M2-06) must route through ApprovalGate.execute; customer Cedar roles in CallContext are still caller-supplied (no role claims in tokens); a tool that fails after commit keeps its approval consumed and its ledger row (conservative).

knowledge.title: Replan round 5

M2-06.4 and the 22 queued .4 tasks were rejected and re-added unchanged as .5 (0 field differences), after a new task M2-05b (approval hardening, scope src/tools/validation/ + tests) that M2-06.5 now depends on. knowledge.title: M2-07.5 sagas and audit: shape, findings and limits
knowledge.text: tools.audit.AuditLog (schema tools_0001_audit.sql adds audit_id, case_id, call_id, saga_id, step_id, idempotency_key, credential_basis, risk_class, approval_request_id, amount_usd, error_code to the append-only tool_audit_records): plain metadata, personal part (arguments, before/after snapshots, results) sealed under the user's data key as field tool_audit:<audit_id>, so erasure's key shred makes it unreadable. tools.sagas.workflow.SagaWorkflow (sandbox-safe; the package __init__ must stay import-light) + tools.sagas.activities: check_plan (compensations reviewed, same system, idempotent system, args fit; irreversible only last, at most once, with an approval request id that is a UUID; snapshot tool via tools.validation.dry_run_tool), each forward step through ApprovalGate.execute with tool.func -> Executor.run (gated_tool raises irreversible steps to high_risk_write so a specialist must approve), compensations via Executor with call id <saga>:<step>:compensate (same idempotency key every attempt), Temporal retries compensations 3 times then COMPENSATION_FAILED (no further rollback). FOLLOW-UP for the M2-05b code: ApprovalGate crashes (psycopg InvalidTextRepresentation) on a non-UUID request id instead of NotApproved; sagas guard it in check_plan. Limits: the customer's session token is in the saga input (Temporal history), as in ToolCall; no hash chain on the audit (append-only triggers only); compensations bypass the approval gate (they restore state) but are audited.

knowledge.title: M2-07.6 saga hardening (round 6): trust boundaries and open risks
knowledge.text: Trust boundaries after M2-06c + M2-07.6: Temporal workflow input/history for sagas holds only saga_id, tenant_id, session_id (reference), case_id, conversation_id, masked message and steps; no bearer token, principal, handler or roles. Activities resolve the principal with Identity.session_principal (live session row, tenant RLS), roles from Executor.roles_of (trusted directory, default none), handler from SagaActivities(handler_id=AGENT). Every forward step: gate.validate pre-check (DENY stops before any call, snapshots included) -> audited before-snapshot -> gate.execute (re-validates, approvals) -> Executor.run (OBO minted from the session inside the activity). Compensations go through gate.execute too (Cedar on compensation_resource or the step's resource); refusals are non-retryable and stop the rollback (COMPENSATION_FAILED); transient failures retry 3 times. A step activity that fails outright (e.g. audit write) is treated as failed, earlier steps are compensated and the saga ends UNCERTAIN_STEP for a human. Audit covers snapshot/forward/compensate with ok/failed and codes (TRANSIENT, SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE, NOT_APPROVED, INVALID_ARGUMENTS, AUTHENTICATION_EXPIRED, INTERNAL_ERROR); personal payload only when the user is established. Decision-id question: approval decision ids are random per validation (tools.validation.decide), so a fresh decision can never equal the stored one; the binding instead re-checks policy version, level, arguments and context against the stored decision id, which rejects any decision change (tested). OPEN: ApprovalGate trusts CallContext.roles from any caller (sagas pass trusted roles); the generic tools.execution.calls.call_tool / ToolActivities path runs tools without the approval gate; staff identity and the Cedar approve_action policy still missing (M2-09); ApprovalGate crashes on a non-UUID request id (guarded in sagas).

knowledge.title: M2-09a approval policy and lifetime
knowledge.text: policies/support.cedar now permits approve_action on ApprovalRequest (attributes tenant_id, level, handler, customer; schema in support.cedarschema.json, action in the write group so an unreachable engine refuses): Role specialist approves level 'specialist' only; Role senior_specialist approves 'specialist' and 'senior_specialist'; never the handler, never the customer; the generic tenant-boundary forbid applies. Customer-level confirmations are not Cedar-governed (the gate checks the customer). tools.validation.approvals: APPROVAL_TTL is a timedelta (30 min default), ApprovalGate(ttl=...) and request(ttl=...) accept 0 < ttl <= MAX_APPROVAL_TTL (72 h); request ids are parsed as UUIDs (malformed -> NotApproved, never sent to the database). Release note: policies/ is a behaviour path, so this ships in the scheduled release. Still open (for M2-09.7): staff identity and role directory (verify_approver), queues/SLA/72 h cancellation, approval card.

knowledge.title: M2-09a gate hardening: trusted inputs, digest, open items
knowledge.text: ApprovalGate (tools.validation.approvals) after the M2-09a review fixes: tenant and principal must match the server-side conversation record (RLS) or DENY; roles come from roles_of(tenant, principal) when configured (ctx.roles ignored), else legacy ctx.roles; with tool_authz {tool_id: ToolAuthorization(action, resource_type, id_argument, public)} the resource's action and type must equal the tool's rule, its id must equal the tool argument named by id_argument, attrs.tenant_id must equal the tenant, a tool without a rule is denied, public is allowed only for reads; resource_attrs(tenant, type, id) overrides caller attrs. Unconditional: a call with no resource is denied unless its rule is public (reads included); approvals carry a deterministic decision_digest (schema validation_0002_decision_digest.sql) over tenant, case, tool, args, verdict, level, amount, policy version, checked explicitly against the fresh decision at execution (missing digest = refuse); request() recomputes the code-level verdict (limits, ledger, conversation/case, Cedar) and stores the stricter of it and the caller's, with the current policy version. Decision ids stay random (ledger uniqueness). financial_writes = authorized committed attempts (one row per execute, before the external call). OPEN (user chose 'gate only, sagas later'): tools.sagas activities still build CallContext with caller resources and pass ctx.roles; the saga's ApprovalGate is constructed without roles_of / tool_authz / resource_attrs, so the saga path keeps the legacy behaviour; the executor's service-account Cedar check (tools.execution) still uses call.resource; tool->Cedar rules live in the gate config, not the tool registry; no resource_attrs resolver exists yet (needs CRM reads).

knowledge.title: Open issues register (single source; update by superseding)
knowledge.text:
Consolidated 2026-10-25 from KNOWLEDGE-2114e3c6, 82aa3192, c5d19a99, 634b024b, 0bf6e556, 60b69bfa, 60b6dd3c, 630f3cc2, c60fdc50, b0d958bf, d72ef88b, fef4e96a, 97282376. Plan: fix in one end-of-project sweep task (added with a single plan reopen after the last task, when nothing is active or queued), unless an item blocks a task earlier.
SECURITY: S1 saga path uses ApprovalGate legacy mode: caller-supplied ctx.resource and ctx.roles, gate built without roles_of / tool_authz / resource_attrs (src/tools/sagas/activities.py). S2 Executor service-account Cedar check uses caller call.resource, not a tool->Cedar rule (src/tools/execution/__init__.py). S3 generic tools.execution.calls.call_tool / ToolActivities path runs tools without the approval gate (src/tools/execution/). S4 no resource_attrs resolver: resource owner/tenant attributes still come from the caller (needs reviewed CRM read tools). S5 tool->Cedar rules live in gate config, not next to the tool in the registry (src/tools/registry/). S6 screening does not decode Base64; a Base64-only injection passes user-message screening (src/safety/screening/; Prompt Guard via Groq or a decode pass). S7 audit log is append-only but not hash-chained (src/tools/audit.py). S8 ticket workflow (M1-05) inputs/history not audited for sensitive data in Temporal (src/workflows/).
BUGS: B1 output sanitiser strips <placeholder> text inside code fences ('--subnet-id <id>' -> '--subnet-id ') (src/safety/output/checks.py). B2 web/dev-server.js crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT when the API drops mid-stream (writeHead only if !headersSent, else destroy). B3 tests/deploy/test_backbone.py line 4 over 110 chars (lint). B4 app HTTPS on TLS-intercepting machines needs truststore / CA handling (only the demo has it).
NOT YET WIRED: W1 governance require_sign_off() not in the statechart; disclose() not in the API reply path (src/safety/governance/). W2 conversation memory not wired into dispatch / context assembler; summarizer prompt is injected, none written (src/memory/conversation/). W3 facts: activation scoring for the 15% profile slot, the resolution / 24 h idle write trigger, ALLOWED_TOOL_FIELDS is an example list (src/memory/facts/). W4 no CI lint that every tool field declares sensitivity (review() runs at registration). W5 a DENY does not yet feed the turn's circuit breaker (src/core/recovery/ + turn loop). W6 tool-output blobs (tool-output/<tenant>/<case>/) not in the erasure inventory and no TTL (src/memory/lifecycle/). W7 approval cards over the event stream / specialist queue: expected in M2-09.7. W8 Langfuse traces join the erasure inventory: expected in M5-01.
ACCEPTED LIMITS / DESIGN DEBT: L1 no pgvector (nearest facts in Python). L2 legal archive: no legal holds, no General Counsel dual sign-off, Postgres not S3 Object Lock; its tokens lose their values after erasure. L3 no Redis mutex (Postgres PK sequences turns); no P2 alert for pin budget. L4 fact TTL uses valid_from as last-confirmed; old versions of a live fact stay until the lineage expires (plain FK). L5 Temporal ticket history TTL via namespace retention. L6 'prod' -> 'production' synonyms refused (agent asks). L7 non-USD money actions denied until a trusted FX source exists (DECISION-bdad33ce). knowledge.title: M2-09.7 escalation queues and approval desk: shape and limits
knowledge.text: hitl.queues (schema hitl_0001_queues.sql, needs channels.sessions + tools.validation.approvals schemas): staff_directory (tenant, staff_id, roles[], queues[], active; app_owner writes, runtime reads), escalations (tokenized packet jsonb, queue, acuity, approval_request_id UNIQUE, status waiting/claimed/approved/rejected/cancelled, sla_due_at, alerted/promoted/claimed/closed_at; runtime may update only lifecycle columns), escalation_events (append-only by trigger). Packet (pydantic, extra=forbid): provenance, reason, domain (billing/technical/account), summary, last_turns (<=3), pins, citations, tool outputs, diagnostic trace, proposed_action (= tools.validation.preview card) + approval_request_id only for action approvals. Queues.escalate(packet, arguments): conversation must belong to customer+case; for approvals the pending, unexpired, non-customer-level request must match case/conversation/customer/handler, arguments_hash(arguments) must match, and the card's tool_id/level/tokenized arguments/USD amount must equal the request and the real arguments; text tokenized with the PII Tokenizer; Jev score question ACUITY (four levels, unanswered = most urgent); SLA by reason (handoff and low confidence 15 min, approval and reflexion 1 h, significant decision and dependency held 24 h); queue by domain, senior-level approvals to queue_senior. claim(): StaffCredential minted for this item, staffed on the queue, senior queue needs senior_specialist, not handler or customer, status waiting. sweep(tenant): 72 h undecided approvals cancelled (request revoked, customer notified with CANCEL_NOTICE, event action.approval.auto_cancelled), SLA breach -> queue_senior unassigned + alert (once), waiting past half the SLA -> aging alert (once); callbacks run inside the transaction (at least once). hitl.approval: staff_verifier(connect, issuer, public_key): MFA ID token for client support-console, nonce = the item id (escalation id for claim/card, request id for decide), roles from the active directory row. Desk.card/decide: assignee only; approve needs every field (tool_id, amount_usd, arguments.*) confirmed with the card's value, then ApprovalGate.grant (Cedar rights by role and amount); reject needs a RejectReason and the role for the level, revokes the request.

knowledge.title: M2-10.7 hand-off, waiting, cancel arbitration, reply checks, console
knowledge.text: hitl.handoff (schema hitl_0002_handoff.sql, needs hitl.queues + data.events schemas): handoffs (one active owner per conversation by partial unique index; runtime may only set ended_at), reply_overrides and draft_feedback (append-only by trigger; draft_feedback.prompt_example is CHECKed false: CI-D5). wants_human(engine, message, pressed): button, else Jev noul HUMAN_INTENT on masked text, else (Jev down) the ASKS_FOR_HUMAN keywords. Handoffs.request(packet) escalates at once (not for action approvals) and publishes a 'handoff' event {state queued, position, estimate_minutes}. estimate = position (waiting items ahead by acuity then deadline, +1) x SERVICE_MINUTES (10) / active staff on the queue, rounded up; None when unstaffed. mode(): human (active handoffs row) > co_serving (open non-approval escalation not yet picked up) > agent; allowed(mode, tool): co_serving = read_only tools only, human = nothing. pick_up(): staff sign-in for the item, not an approval, Queues.claim unless already claimed by the same person (retry), then the handoffs row + 'specialist_joined' event; returns the packet. reply(): owner only; check_reply warnings (PII via safety.pii find, credentials / high-entropy, 12-word run of an internal passage, links not HTTPS to an allow-listed domain) return Sent(False, warnings) until a Justification is given, then the override is recorded and a 'final' event {text, from: specialist} published. hand_back() ends ownership. feedback(): accepted, or edited / rejected with a DraftFailure code. cancel(principal, escalation_id): the customer only, action approvals only; locks the escalation row then the request row (the same order as Desk.decide, so no client-side deadlock: Desk.decide holds the escalation row while its grant runs on another connection), pending -> revoked + escalation cancelled 'customer_cancelled' + alert to the assignee; approved or consumed -> (False, LATE_CANCEL). This Postgres row-lock arbitration is the v1 form of HL-D8's Temporal signal sequencing: whichever takes the escalation row first wins. console/app.py: Streamlit page over Queues / Desk / Handoffs (services injectable via st.session_state['services']); Approve disabled until every card field is checked, Reject until a reason is chosen, feedback until the code rule holds; server refusals shown with st.error.

knowledge.title: M2-11.7 end-to-end scenarios 3 and 4: what they prove and their glue
knowledge.text: tests/e2e/test_scenarios_actions.py chains PII tokens -> statechart (Postgres checkpointer, Jev triage, injected clock) -> AWAITING_APPROVAL -> ApprovalGate.validate/request (72 h ttl) -> preview card (dry run for the refund, current state for the reset) -> Queues.escalate (contract comparison in tool_outputs) -> SSO-signed specialist claim / card / decide -> APPROVAL_GRANTED resume (revalidate after > 1 h compares the re-read target with the card's current state) -> ApprovalGate.execute -> read-back -> output checks with verified_actions from the read-back only. A correction while an action waits: Jev noul CORRECTS -> Handoffs.cancel -> APPROVAL_DENIED -> new episode for the corrected target. Proven: no ERP call or financial_writes row before a senior approves a 16,000 USD refund; a specialist cannot take it; a promise without a verified action is held (escalate) and a refund the ERP accepted but did not apply is not claimed; a correction revokes the pending reset, only srv-bravo-99 is reset, srv-alpha-12 untouched; after a 2 h wait a changed target goes to ESCALATED_HITL with no side effect, an unchanged one runs; a cancel after the approval returns LATE_CANCEL. Glue in the test (not product code): the slot filler and the correction question are scripted; approval_threshold is set to 0 for the high-risk reset because the statechart waits for approval on amount only; the reset is authorized as Cedar restart_cluster on the instance's Environment. One strict xfail documents register B7 (past-tense success claims pass the output checks).

knowledge.title: M3-01.7 coordinator topology: registry, delegation, limits
knowledge.text: agents.topology: registry(specialists, tool_ids) -> read-only {Role: Specialist} with exactly generalist, billing, technical, account_ops; descriptions are Jev option text (NUMBERS rule), tools must exist in the tool registry; the coordinator has no tools. delegate(engine, registry, Masked) asks one Jev request: choice 'lead' over the registry, plus per domain specialist (not the generalist) noul needs_<role> and after_<role>; lead confidence < 0.50 or JevUnavailable -> Plan(handoff=reason), nothing dispatched; others join at P(yes) >= 0.80, and wait for the lead at P(after) >= 0.80. Budgets fixed up front: COORDINATOR_STEPS 1, lead min(2, left), then each added specialist min(2, left) while STEPS_PER_TURN 6 lasts (so at most three specialists per turn, inside the span of five); no budget -> not dispatched. coordinator(engine, registry, run_tool, checkpointer): LangGraph plan -> Send('first') for the lead and independents (parallel) -> between -> Send('then') for dependents with upstream = the lead's result -> join (outcome delegated / handoff). Each specialist is a compiled subgraph invoked inside the node with the parent config (checkpointed with the case); a step is act(brief, history): findings end it (completed), an action outside the specialist's allow-list blocks it (depth one: no agent-to-agent calls), a tool error is kept as the observation so the next step can retry, and reaching the budget without findings returns status blocked with the last observation. The plan is stored as plain JSON (Plan.as_state) and survives the Postgres checkpointer.

Consolidated 2026-10-25 from KNOWLEDGE-2114e3c6, 82aa3192, c5d19a99, 634b024b, 0bf6e556, 60b69bfa, 60b6dd3c, 630f3cc2, c60fdc50, b0d958bf, d72ef88b, fef4e96a, 97282376; v2 added M2-09.7 items (S9, B5, W9-W13, L10-L11); v3 added M2-10.7 items (B6, W14-W16, L12-L13); v4 added M2-11.7 items (B7, W17-W18, L14); v5 adds M3-01.7 items (W19, L15). Plan (user, 2026-10-25): out-of-scope issues, critical ones too, go here instead of a replan; fix all in one sweep task added with a single plan reopen after the last task (M6-03.7).
SECURITY: S1 saga path uses ApprovalGate legacy mode: caller-supplied ctx.resource and ctx.roles, gate built without roles_of / tool_authz / resource_attrs (src/tools/sagas/activities.py). S2 Executor service-account Cedar check uses caller call.resource, not a tool->Cedar rule (src/tools/execution/__init__.py). S3 generic tools.execution.calls.call_tool / ToolActivities path runs tools without the approval gate (src/tools/execution/). S4 no resource_attrs resolver: resource owner/tenant attributes still come from the caller (needs reviewed CRM read tools). S5 tool->Cedar rules live in gate config, not next to the tool in the registry (src/tools/registry/). S6 screening does not decode Base64; a Base64-only injection passes user-message screening (src/safety/screening/; Prompt Guard via Groq or a decode pass). S7 audit log is append-only but not hash-chained (src/tools/audit.py). S8 ticket workflow (M1-05) inputs/history not audited for sensitive data in Temporal (src/workflows/). S9 ApprovalGate.grant does not pass the request id to verify_approver, so the one-item binding of a staff sign-in (ID token nonce = request id) is enforced by hitl.approval.Desk.decide, not by a direct gate.grant call (src/tools/validation/approvals.py: pass request_id to the verifier).
BUGS: B1 output sanitiser strips <placeholder> text inside code fences ('--subnet-id <id>' -> '--subnet-id ') (src/safety/output/checks.py). B2 web/dev-server.js crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT when the API drops mid-stream (writeHead only if !headersSent, else destroy). B3 tests/deploy/test_backbone.py line 4 over 110 chars (lint). B4 app HTTPS on TLS-intercepting machines needs truststore / CA handling (only the demo has it). B5 ticket workflow waits 48 h for an approval decision (src/workflows/ticket.py approval_timeout_seconds) but HL-D9 / MAX_APPROVAL_TTL / hitl.queues cancel at 72 h. B6 hitl.queues.sweep promotes a claimed hand-off once its SLA passes (for a hand-off the SLA is the time to pick-up) and unassigns it: the conversation's specialist keeps ownership (handoffs row; the one-owner index stops a second take-over) but the item reappears in queue_senior and pages the lead; escalations also have no 'resolved' status for a finished hand-off (src/hitl/queues: skip claimed hand-offs in the promotion, add a resolved status set by hand_back). B7 the output checks only catch future promises ('we will refund', 'will be credited'); a past-tense success claim ('Your refund has been processed.') passes without a verified action (src/safety/output/checks.py PROMISES; strict xfail in tests/e2e/test_scenarios_actions.py flips when fixed).
NOT YET WIRED: W1 governance require_sign_off() not in the statechart; disclose() not in the API reply path (src/safety/governance/). W2 conversation memory not wired into dispatch / context assembler; summarizer prompt is injected, none written (src/memory/conversation/). W3 facts: activation scoring for the 15% profile slot, the resolution / 24 h idle write trigger, ALLOWED_TOOL_FIELDS is an example list (src/memory/facts/). W4 no CI lint that every tool field declares sensitivity (review() runs at registration). W5 a DENY does not yet feed the turn's circuit breaker (src/core/recovery/ + turn loop). W6 tool-output blobs (tool-output/<tenant>/<case>/) not in the erasure inventory and no TTL (src/memory/lifecycle/). W7 approval card delivery to the specialist console / event stream: expected in M2-10 (the card itself is hitl.approval.Desk.card). W8 Langfuse traces join the erasure inventory: expected in M5-01. W9 hitl.queues.Queues.sweep is a function: not yet run on a schedule (Temporal schedule or cron, per tenant). W10 alert (Slack / PagerDuty) and notify (customer inbox, UA-D2) are injected callbacks with no production implementation. W11 nothing emits escalation packets yet: confidence gate hand-offs, reflexion limit, user-requested human and approval-requiring actions must call Queues.escalate (turn loop / M2-10 handoff). W12 escalations / escalation_events (tokenized packet, customer id) not in the erasure inventory or retention (src/memory/lifecycle/). W13 MS-D18 post-wait check: an approval executed more than 1 h after staging does not re-read external state against the dry-run snapshot before running (tools.validation execute / sagas). Also: staff_directory has no admin or SCIM sync path (app_owner SQL only); specialists see PII tokens, vault reveal for authorized staff not wired (console). W14 the turn loop does not yet call hitl.handoff (wants_human -> request, mode / allowed before each turn and tool call), so co-serving and the cold hand-off are not enforced in the agent yet. W15 console sign-in is an in-process MockIdP (development): the console's OIDC redirect with a per-item nonce and its deployment (Hugging Face Spaces) are not built. W16 no customer API route for cancel(); the wait estimate is published once at request time, not refreshed as the queue moves. W17 the statechart waits for approval on amount only (execute_sop: parameters.amount >= approval_threshold); an SOP whose tool needs approval for another reason (high-risk write, unreviewed tool, Cedar approval_required) has no way into AWAITING_APPROVAL; the e2e test sets the threshold to 0 for it (src/core/orchestrator/statechart.py: take needs_approval from tools.validation's decision). W18 the turn loop has no correction detection for an action waiting for approval (the e2e test asks Jev a noul question, then Handoffs.cancel + APPROVAL_DENIED + a new episode), and no slot filler (scripted in the e2e tests). W19 agents.topology.coordinator is not yet called from the statechart's DELIBERATING stage, and a handoff plan (low lead confidence or Jev down) does not yet open an escalation in hitl.queues (turn loop wiring).
ACCEPTED LIMITS / DESIGN DEBT: L1 no pgvector (nearest facts in Python). L2 legal archive: no legal holds, no General Counsel dual sign-off, Postgres not S3 Object Lock; its tokens lose their values after erasure. L3 no Redis mutex (Postgres PK sequences turns); no P2 alert for pin budget; so the 72 h cancel has no mutex to release. L4 fact TTL uses valid_from as last-confirmed; old versions of a live fact stay until the lineage expires (plain FK). L5 Temporal ticket history TTL via namespace retention. L6 'prod' -> 'production' synonyms refused (agent asks). L7 non-USD money actions denied until a trusted FX source exists (DECISION-bdad33ce). L8 hazard scorer is a stub in tests/demo (Llama Guard needs a model pull). L9 SPEC FR-7 says OBO tokens last 24 h; code and UA-D9 say 15 min (doc fix). L10 a business day is counted as 24 h for significant-decision SLAs (no business calendar). L11 queue priority is Jev acuity then SLA deadline; contract tier does not affect it, and promotion to the senior queue keeps the original (breached) deadline. L12 the wait estimate uses a fixed 10-minute service time per specialist, not Erlang A or measured rates. L13 HL-D10's Jev categorisation of free-text feedback is not built: feedback is reason codes only and the edited draft text is not stored. L14 Cedar has no credential-reset action; the e2e reset is authorized as restart_cluster (a production change) on the instance's environment (policies/: add the action when the tool is real). L15 MA-D8's shared turn token budget (16,000 tokens, forced join at 90%) is not enforced: steps are the only ceiling in agents.topology (add with the briefs' token accounting).

knowledge.title: M3-01.7 coordinator topology: registry, delegation, limits (after the security review)
knowledge.text: agents.topology. registry(specialists, tool_registry): exactly generalist, billing, technical, account_ops; Jev descriptions without digits; every allow-listed tool registered and READ_ONLY (writes wait for MA-ADP-04 with the approval gate). delegate(): one Jev request (choice lead + noul needs_<role> / after_<role> per domain specialist); DecisionEngine.checked rejects unknown options, confidence outside [0, 1] or NaN, non-bool nouls and missing answers -> JevUnavailable -> Plan(handoff); lead < 0.50 -> handoff; co-activation and waiting at >= 0.80; budgets fixed up front (coordinator 1, then min(2, left) each within 6, so at most three specialists). Other exceptions propagate (the turn fails, nothing is dispatched). checked_plan() re-validates the plan wherever it is read (dict shape, known distinct roles, lead first and not waiting, int budgets 1..2, bool after_lead, total <= 6, handoff dispatches nobody); a tampered checkpoint plan is refused before any tool runs. Turn input: tenant_id, case_id, session_id, principal_id, masked message (start_turn refuses text in which safety.pii.tokens.find sees personal data before anything is checkpointed, and runs on thread(tenant, case)); the plan node also checks the context and sets a turn_id. Dependents run only after the lead completed (status completed) with its result as upstream; otherwise recorded as skipped. Specialist step: budget re-checked; findings must be str <= 4000 chars with <= 20 str evidence items; actions must be on the allow-list with dict arguments; tools run as run_tool(ToolRequest(tenant, case, session, principal, turn_id, role, step, tool_id, arguments)) with tool_call_id = sha256(turn:role:step:tool) stable across retries; only str (screened) output is accepted, failures reach the model as a code (ToolFailure.code or the class name), never a message; history keeps thought / action / observation only. executor_tool(executor) maps ToolRequest to tools.execution ToolCall (checkpoint_id = turn_id), so the Executor verifies the session's principal and tenant, mints the credential, validates arguments against the schema and screens output. Results merge in role order (merge_results); ledger(results, plan) raises when a role ran twice, outside the plan or over its budget, or the turn passed six.

knowledge.title: M3-02.7 agent contracts, specialist identity and write rules
knowledge.text: agents.contracts. Brief (pydantic, extra=forbid, frozen): task_id, role, case, conversation, masked objective <= 4000, entity_ids, pinned_constraints, evidence_refs, steps 1..2, upstream Result; brief(..., pins=...) copies every pin (pins is required). Result: status completed / blocked / needs_user; blocked <=> a Blocker enum (missing_information, tool_failed, out_of_domain, needs_approval, budget_used_up, read_back_mismatch: no free-text redirects); completed needs findings; every Finding and ProposedAction cites >= 1 evidence id listed in Result.evidence; ExecutedAction.verified is Literal[True]; no customer-facing field. actor(role) = 'specialist.<role>', used as CallContext.handler_id. SpecialistTools(executor, gate, tool_registry, allow_lists, read_backs, resource_of).for_turn(conversation_id, message, solo) -> run_tool(ToolRequest): off the role's allow-list -> Refused NOT_ON_ALLOW_LIST; read_only -> Executor.run (screened content); any other risk or a financial argument -> PROPOSE before the gate is asked; low-risk write while not solo -> PARALLEL_WRITE; no declared ReadBack -> PROPOSE; ApprovalGate.validate (current state: conversation, case open, Cedar on resource_of, limits, Jev) not ALLOW -> PROPOSE; then the write through the Executor (keyed, idempotent), then the ReadBack tool through the Executor (call id + ':read-back'); not band pass or confirm() false -> READ_BACK_MISMATCH; only then an ExecutedAction(verified=True) is recorded. ConversationReader(load).read(tenant, conversation, first, last, topic): int bounds, at most PAGE_TURNS (10) turns, refuses a page with unmasked personal data (SecurityViolation), returns Page(turns, characters) for the caller to charge.

knowledge.title: M3-03.7 merge: numbers in code, conflicts by Jev, one reply
knowledge.text: agents.merge.merge(engine, results, evidence {id: masked text}, draft(claims) -> text, verified_actions) -> Outcome(kind reply | human, text, reason, detail, accepted). claims_from(result): only completed results; findings must be a JSON list of Claim (topic, text, optional finite Decimal value + unit, >= 1 evidence id; extra fields refused); the role is set from the result. Reasons for a person: NOTHING_TO_SAY (no usable claims); NUMERIC_DISCREPANCY (same topic, numbers differ beyond TOLERANCE per unit - percent 0.005, otherwise exact - or different units; detail values {topic: {role: 'value unit'}}; decided before Jev is asked anything); EVIDENCE_AMBIGUITY (non-numeric claims on a topic that differ: Jev score SUPPORT per claim, questions keyed by letters so no digits, each claim against its own cited evidence; a winner needs >= 4 while all others <= 2); JEV_UNAVAILABLE (conflict scoring or the redirect check could not be answered); REDIRECT (Jev noul on the masked draft, P(yes) rounded to 9 places >= 0.20); UNVERIFIED_COMPLETION (completed-action wording - have/has been processed, refunded, credited, applied, reset, ... or is/are now ... - with no verified action). draft() is called once per turn, only after conflicts are settled. Scenario 7 e2e (tests/e2e/test_scenario_multiagent.py) runs agents.topology for technical + billing in parallel, then merge.

Consolidated 2026-10-25 from KNOWLEDGE-2114e3c6, 82aa3192, c5d19a99, 634b024b, 0bf6e556, 60b69bfa, 60b6dd3c, 630f3cc2, c60fdc50, b0d958bf, d72ef88b, fef4e96a, 97282376; v2 added M2-09.7 items (S9, B5, W9-W13, L10-L11); v3 added M2-10.7 items (B6, W14-W16, L12-L13); v4 added M2-11.7 items (B7, W17-W18, L14); v5 added M3-01.7 items (W19, L15); v6 added the M3-01.7 security review's out-of-scope items (S10, S11, W20, and a note on S3); v7 added M3-02.7 items (S12, W21, L16-L17); v8 added M3-03.7 items (W22, L18); v9 added PERF-01 items (B8, L19); v10 marks PERF-01 dropped (L19). Plan (user, 2026-10-25): out-of-scope issues, critical ones too, go here instead of a replan; fix all in one sweep task added with a single plan reopen after the last task (M6-03.7).
SECURITY: S1 saga path uses ApprovalGate legacy mode: caller-supplied ctx.resource and ctx.roles, gate built without roles_of / tool_authz / resource_attrs (src/tools/sagas/activities.py). S2 Executor service-account Cedar check uses caller call.resource, not a tool->Cedar rule (src/tools/execution/__init__.py). S3 generic tools.execution.calls.call_tool / ToolActivities path runs tools without the approval gate (src/tools/execution/). Note for S3: agents.topology.executor_tool also calls Executor.run without the approval gate; it is safe only because a specialist registry refuses non-read-only tools, so M3-02.7 must route specialist writes through ApprovalGate (and S2: executor_tool sends no Cedar resource, so a service-account system denies by default). S4 no resource_attrs resolver: resource owner/tenant attributes still come from the caller (needs reviewed CRM read tools). S5 tool->Cedar rules live in gate config, not next to the tool in the registry (src/tools/registry/). S6 screening does not decode Base64; a Base64-only injection passes user-message screening (src/safety/screening/; Prompt Guard via Groq or a decode pass). S7 audit log is append-only but not hash-chained (src/tools/audit.py). S8 ticket workflow (M1-05) inputs/history not audited for sensitive data in Temporal (src/workflows/). S9 ApprovalGate.grant does not pass the request id to verify_approver, so the one-item binding of a staff sign-in (ID token nonce = request id) is enforced by hitl.approval.Desk.decide, not by a direct gate.grant call (src/tools/validation/approvals.py: pass request_id to the verifier). S10 the LangGraph Postgres checkpoint tables have no tenant row-level security and no integrity seal: someone with database write access could substitute a well-formed plan or state (agents.topology.checked_plan refuses malformed or inflated plans, not a valid substitute); theoretical while the checkpoint database is trusted (core.orchestrator.statechart.postgres_checkpointer: separate role / RLS, or an HMAC over the plan). S11 tools.execution.Executor.run writes no tool audit record (tools.audit is only on the saga path), so specialist tool calls through executor_tool are not audited (src/tools/execution). S12 a specialist's identity does not reach downstream systems or the audit log: on-behalf-of tokens carry act = the one agent identity (channels.identity.service._mint_obo, AGENT), and tool_audit_records has no actor_subrole column (MA-D9, MA-ADP-04 invariant 1); agents.contracts.actor(role) is recorded only as the approval request's handler.
BUGS: B1 output sanitiser strips <placeholder> text inside code fences ('--subnet-id <id>' -> '--subnet-id ') (src/safety/output/checks.py). B2 web/dev-server.js crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT when the API drops mid-stream (writeHead only if !headersSent, else destroy). B3 tests/deploy/test_backbone.py line 4 over 110 chars (lint). B4 app HTTPS on TLS-intercepting machines needs truststore / CA handling (only the demo has it). B5 ticket workflow waits 48 h for an approval decision (src/workflows/ticket.py approval_timeout_seconds) but HL-D9 / MAX_APPROVAL_TTL / hitl.queues cancel at 72 h. B6 hitl.queues.sweep promotes a claimed hand-off once its SLA passes (for a hand-off the SLA is the time to pick-up) and unassigns it: the conversation's specialist keeps ownership (handoffs row; the one-owner index stops a second take-over) but the item reappears in queue_senior and pages the lead; escalations also have no 'resolved' status for a finished hand-off (src/hitl/queues: skip claimed hand-offs in the promotion, add a resolved status set by hand_back). B7 the output checks only catch future promises ('we will refund', 'will be credited'); a past-tense success claim ('Your refund has been processed.') passes without a verified action (src/safety/output/checks.py PROMISES; strict xfail in tests/e2e/test_scenarios_actions.py flips when fixed).
NOT YET B8 tests/tools/validation test_property_no_financial_write_at_or_above_the_threshold_runs_without_a_second_person failed once (2026-10-26) with psycopg AdminShutdown: its Postgres connection was terminated mid-test, most likely by a concurrent Postgres restart from another session; not reproduced since (545/545 green on 2026-10-27). The test and ApprovalGate hold their own connections and do not reconnect. The test also takes ~42 s, unchanged by PERF-01 (its time is not in data.migrate.psql): profile it in the sweep.
WIRED: W1 governance require_sign_off() not in the statechart; disclose() not in the API reply path (src/safety/governance/). W2 conversation memory not wired into dispatch / context assembler; summarizer prompt is injected, none written (src/memory/conversation/). W3 facts: activation scoring for the 15% profile slot, the resolution / 24 h idle write trigger, ALLOWED_TOOL_FIELDS is an example list (src/memory/facts/). W4 no CI lint that every tool field declares sensitivity (review() runs at registration). W5 a DENY does not yet feed the turn's circuit breaker (src/core/recovery/ + turn loop). W6 tool-output blobs (tool-output/<tenant>/<case>/) not in the erasure inventory and no TTL (src/memory/lifecycle/). W7 approval card delivery to the specialist console / event stream: expected in M2-10 (the card itself is hitl.approval.Desk.card). W8 Langfuse traces join the erasure inventory: expected in M5-01. W9 hitl.queues.Queues.sweep is a function: not yet run on a schedule (Temporal schedule or cron, per tenant). W10 alert (Slack / PagerDuty) and notify (customer inbox, UA-D2) are injected callbacks with no production implementation. W11 nothing emits escalation packets yet: confidence gate hand-offs, reflexion limit, user-requested human and approval-requiring actions must call Queues.escalate (turn loop / M2-10 handoff). W12 escalations / escalation_events (tokenized packet, customer id) not in the erasure inventory or retention (src/memory/lifecycle/). W13 MS-D18 post-wait check: an approval executed more than 1 h after staging does not re-read external state against the dry-run snapshot before running (tools.validation execute / sagas). Also: staff_directory has no admin or SCIM sync path (app_owner SQL only); specialists see PII tokens, vault reveal for authorized staff not wired (console). W14 the turn loop does not yet call hitl.handoff (wants_human -> request, mode / allowed before each turn and tool call), so co-serving and the cold hand-off are not enforced in the agent yet. W15 console sign-in is an in-process MockIdP (development): the console's OIDC redirect with a per-item nonce and its deployment (Hugging Face Spaces) are not built. W16 no customer API route for cancel(); the wait estimate is published once at request time, not refreshed as the queue moves. W17 the statechart waits for approval on amount only (execute_sop: parameters.amount >= approval_threshold); an SOP whose tool needs approval for another reason (high-risk write, unreviewed tool, Cedar approval_required) has no way into AWAITING_APPROVAL; the e2e test sets the threshold to 0 for it (src/core/orchestrator/statechart.py: take needs_approval from tools.validation's decision). W18 the turn loop has no correction detection for an action waiting for approval (the e2e test asks Jev a noul question, then Handoffs.cancel + APPROVAL_DENIED + a new episode), and no slot filler (scripted in the e2e tests). W19 agents.topology.coordinator is not yet called from the statechart's DELIBERATING stage, and a handoff plan (low lead confidence or Jev down) does not yet open an escalation in hitl.queues (turn loop wiring). W20 a specialist tool failure is reduced to its code for the model, and its detail is not written to an access-controlled, redacted diagnostic log (observability, M5). W21 agents.topology does not use agents.contracts yet: briefs and results are still dicts; its registry refuses every non-read-only tool, so SpecialistTools' solo low-risk writes are unreachable from the coordinator; for_turn needs solo (the plan's single assignment), the conversation id and the masked message; a specialist's ProposedAction is not yet routed by the coordinator to ApprovalGate.request + hitl.queues (src/agents/topology). W22 agents.merge is not wired into the coordinator's join: its human outcomes (NUMERIC_DISCREPANCY, EVIDENCE_AMBIGUITY, REDIRECT, UNVERIFIED_COMPLETION, JEV_UNAVAILABLE) do not yet open a hitl.queues escalation with a discrepancy card; a REDIRECT does not re-delegate to the missing specialist; the drafting model is not wired, and the merged reply does not yet pass the output checks and the confidence gate on its way out.
ACCEPTED LIMITS / DESIGN DEBT: L1 no pgvector (nearest facts in Python). L2 legal archive: no legal holds, no General Counsel dual sign-off, Postgres not S3 Object Lock; its tokens lose their values after erasure. L3 no Redis mutex (Postgres PK sequences turns); no P2 alert for pin budget; so the 72 h cancel has no mutex to release. L4 fact TTL uses valid_from as last-confirmed; old versions of a live fact stay until the lineage expires (plain FK). L5 Temporal ticket history TTL via namespace retention. L6 'prod' -> 'production' synonyms refused (agent asks). L7 non-USD money actions denied until a trusted FX source exists (DECISION-bdad33ce). L8 hazard scorer is a stub in tests/demo (Llama Guard needs a model pull). L9 SPEC FR-7 says OBO tokens last 24 h; code and UA-D9 say 15 min (doc fix). L10 a business day is counted as 24 h for significant-decision SLAs (no business calendar). L11 queue priority is Jev acuity then SLA deadline; contract tier does not affect it, and promotion to the senior queue keeps the original (breached) deadline. L12 the wait estimate uses a fixed 10-minute service time per specialist, not Erlang A or measured rates. L13 HL-D10's Jev categorisation of free-text feedback is not built: feedback is reason codes only and the edited draft text is not stored. L14 Cedar has no credential-reset action; the e2e reset is authorized as restart_cluster (a production change) on the instance's environment (policies/: add the action when the tool is real). L15 MA-D8's shared turn token budget (16,000 tokens, forced join at 90%) is not enforced: steps are the only ceiling in agents.topology (add with the briefs' token accounting). L16 'solo' means the only specialist dispatched in the turn (a dependent running alone after the lead does not count); SpecialistTools validates with the gate and then writes through the executor, two steps without a shared lock (the gate re-decides on current state; a change in between is caught by the read-back, not prevented). L17 ConversationReader is not registered as a tool and its characters are not charged to a shared turn budget (with L15). L18 specialist claims travel as a JSON list in a result's findings until agents.topology carries agents.contracts (W21); the merge's completed-action check is a phrase list, like the output checks' (B7). L19 PERF-01 (one reused psycopg connection per database in data.migrate.psql, for test speed) was dropped by the user on 2026-10-27: task rejected, src/data/migrate.py reverted to one docker exec psql per query; the reverted change is kept as a patch outside the repo. Tests stay slow; revisit in the sweep if speed matters.

knowledge.title: M4-01.7 admission control: limits, degradation, one turn per conversation
knowledge.text: reliability.admission. Admission(store, limits, clock, fallback).admit(tenant, user, conversation, turn_id) -> Verdict(mode, retry_after, active_turn_id, message; status 202 / 409 / 429). Counters: fixed one-minute windows, keys rpm:user:<tenant>:<user>:<minute>, rpm:tenant:<tenant>:<minute>, tpm:tenant:<tenant>:<minute>, each written with INCRBY + EXPIRE 120 in one Upstash /multi-exec transaction; load = max(user/10, tenant/120, tokens/60000) (Limits configurable); load <= 1 FULL, <= 1.5 KB_ONLY, above THROTTLED with retry_after = ceil(seconds left in the minute), at least 1. Requests are counted before the lock check. Lock: lock:conv:<tenant>:<conversation> = turn_id via SET NX EX 60; busy -> BUSY with the holder and STILL_WORKING; keep_alive / hold_for_approval (72 h = hitl.queues.CANCEL_AFTER) / finish only by the holder (Lua compare-and-expire / compare-and-delete). record_usage(tenant, {prompt_tokens, completion_tokens}) accepts only non-negative ints and adds their sum. Upstash: REST client over httpx (Bearer token; errors, HTTP failures and error replies -> StoreUnavailable); on StoreUnavailable each operation falls back to Local (in-process, locked, expiring dict) with a warning. degraded_answer(retrieve, generate, question): top three passages, KB_DISCLAIMER, prompt forbids account claims; model failure -> the snippets as they are; no passages -> no model call.

knowledge.title: M4-02.7 bursts: coalescing, incident mode, latency budgets
knowledge.text: reliability.bursts. SingleFlight(clock, window 0.2 s).run(tenant, action, arguments, call, read_only): writes refused (ValueError); key = sha256 of JSON [tenant, action, arguments with strings casefolded and whitespace-collapsed]; a caller arriving while a flight with that key is in progress and started <= 200 ms ago waits on its Future and gets its result or re-raised exception; the flight is removed when it finishes. Incidents (in-process, one active Incident(brief masked, status_answer, tenants or None for all, declared_by)); incident_answer(engine, incidents, tenant, Masked message): no incident for the tenant -> None; Jev noul INCIDENT_QUESTION on {incident, message}; JevUnavailable -> None; P(yes) rounded >= 0.80 -> the status answer if safety.output.checks.check delivers it (its sanitised text), else None. BUDGETS: faq 5 s / hard 8 s / fallback top_snippet; diagnostic 20 / 28 / summarise_findings; multi_specialist 45 / 60 / human_co_pilot; per-step allocations that must sum within the target (Budget validates). Deadline(route, clock): status_due() for the 1 s first status, fits(optional step, then=required steps after it), timeout(step) = min(allocation, time to the hard ceiling), expired().
