knowledge.text:
Consolidated 2026-10-25 from KNOWLEDGE-2114e3c6, 82aa3192, c5d19a99, 634b024b, 0bf6e556, 60b69bfa, 60b6dd3c, 630f3cc2, c60fdc50, b0d958bf, d72ef88b, fef4e96a, 97282376; v2 added M2-09.7 items (S9, B5, W9-W13, L10-L11); v3 added M2-10.7 items (B6, W14-W16, L12-L13); v4 added M2-11.7 items (B7, W17-W18, L14); v5 added M3-01.7 items (W19, L15); v6 added the M3-01.7 security review's out-of-scope items (S10, S11, W20, and a note on S3); v7 added M3-02.7 items (S12, W21, L16-L17); v8 added M3-03.7 items (W22, L18); v9 added PERF-01 items (B8, L19); v10 marked PERF-01 dropped (L19); v11 added M4-01.7 items (W23, L20) and updated L3; v12 adds M4-02.7 items (W24, L21). Plan (user, 2026-10-25): out-of-scope issues, critical ones too, go here instead of a replan; fix all in one sweep task added with a single plan reopen after the last task (M6-03.7).
SECURITY: S1 saga path uses ApprovalGate legacy mode: caller-supplied ctx.resource and ctx.roles, gate built without roles_of / tool_authz / resource_attrs (src/tools/sagas/activities.py). S2 Executor service-account Cedar check uses caller call.resource, not a tool->Cedar rule (src/tools/execution/__init__.py). S3 generic tools.execution.calls.call_tool / ToolActivities path runs tools without the approval gate (src/tools/execution/). Note for S3: agents.topology.executor_tool also calls Executor.run without the approval gate; it is safe only because a specialist registry refuses non-read-only tools, so M3-02.7 must route specialist writes through ApprovalGate (and S2: executor_tool sends no Cedar resource, so a service-account system denies by default). S4 no resource_attrs resolver: resource owner/tenant attributes still come from the caller (needs reviewed CRM read tools). S5 tool->Cedar rules live in gate config, not next to the tool in the registry (src/tools/registry/). S6 screening does not decode Base64; a Base64-only injection passes user-message screening (src/safety/screening/; Prompt Guard via Groq or a decode pass). S7 audit log is append-only but not hash-chained (src/tools/audit.py). S8 ticket workflow (M1-05) inputs/history not audited for sensitive data in Temporal (src/workflows/). S9 ApprovalGate.grant does not pass the request id to verify_approver, so the one-item binding of a staff sign-in (ID token nonce = request id) is enforced by hitl.approval.Desk.decide, not by a direct gate.grant call (src/tools/validation/approvals.py: pass request_id to the verifier). S10 the LangGraph Postgres checkpoint tables have no tenant row-level security and no integrity seal: someone with database write access could substitute a well-formed plan or state (agents.topology.checked_plan refuses malformed or inflated plans, not a valid substitute); theoretical while the checkpoint database is trusted (core.orchestrator.statechart.postgres_checkpointer: separate role / RLS, or an HMAC over the plan). S11 tools.execution.Executor.run writes no tool audit record (tools.audit is only on the saga path), so specialist tool calls through executor_tool are not audited (src/tools/execution). S12 a specialist's identity does not reach downstream systems or the audit log: on-behalf-of tokens carry act = the one agent identity (channels.identity.service._mint_obo, AGENT), and tool_audit_records has no actor_subrole column (MA-D9, MA-ADP-04 invariant 1); agents.contracts.actor(role) is recorded only as the approval request's handler.
BUGS: B1 output sanitiser strips <placeholder> text inside code fences ('--subnet-id <id>' -> '--subnet-id ') (src/safety/output/checks.py). B2 web/dev-server.js crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT when the API drops mid-stream (writeHead only if !headersSent, else destroy). B3 tests/deploy/test_backbone.py line 4 over 110 chars (lint). B4 app HTTPS on TLS-intercepting machines needs truststore / CA handling (only the demo has it). B5 ticket workflow waits 48 h for an approval decision (src/workflows/ticket.py approval_timeout_seconds) but HL-D9 / MAX_APPROVAL_TTL / hitl.queues cancel at 72 h. B6 hitl.queues.sweep promotes a claimed hand-off once its SLA passes (for a hand-off the SLA is the time to pick-up) and unassigns it: the conversation's specialist keeps ownership (handoffs row; the one-owner index stops a second take-over) but the item reappears in queue_senior and pages the lead; escalations also have no 'resolved' status for a finished hand-off (src/hitl/queues: skip claimed hand-offs in the promotion, add a resolved status set by hand_back). B7 the output checks only catch future promises ('we will refund', 'will be credited'); a past-tense success claim ('Your refund has been processed.') passes without a verified action (src/safety/output/checks.py PROMISES; strict xfail in tests/e2e/test_scenarios_actions.py flips when fixed).
NOT YET B8 tests/tools/validation test_property_no_financial_write_at_or_above_the_threshold_runs_without_a_second_person failed once (2026-10-26) with psycopg AdminShutdown: its Postgres connection was terminated mid-test, most likely by a concurrent Postgres restart from another session; not reproduced since (545/545 green on 2026-10-27). The test and ApprovalGate hold their own connections and do not reconnect. The test also takes ~42 s, unchanged by PERF-01 (its time is not in data.migrate.psql): profile it in the sweep.
WIRED: W1 governance require_sign_off() not in the statechart; disclose() not in the API reply path (src/safety/governance/). W2 conversation memory not wired into dispatch / context assembler; summarizer prompt is injected, none written (src/memory/conversation/). W3 facts: activation scoring for the 15% profile slot, the resolution / 24 h idle write trigger, ALLOWED_TOOL_FIELDS is an example list (src/memory/facts/). W4 no CI lint that every tool field declares sensitivity (review() runs at registration). W5 a DENY does not yet feed the turn's circuit breaker (src/core/recovery/ + turn loop). W6 tool-output blobs (tool-output/<tenant>/<case>/) not in the erasure inventory and no TTL (src/memory/lifecycle/). W7 approval card delivery to the specialist console / event stream: expected in M2-10 (the card itself is hitl.approval.Desk.card). W8 Langfuse traces join the erasure inventory: expected in M5-01. W9 hitl.queues.Queues.sweep is a function: not yet run on a schedule (Temporal schedule or cron, per tenant). W10 alert (Slack / PagerDuty) and notify (customer inbox, UA-D2) are injected callbacks with no production implementation. W11 nothing emits escalation packets yet: confidence gate hand-offs, reflexion limit, user-requested human and approval-requiring actions must call Queues.escalate (turn loop / M2-10 handoff). W12 escalations / escalation_events (tokenized packet, customer id) not in the erasure inventory or retention (src/memory/lifecycle/). W13 MS-D18 post-wait check: an approval executed more than 1 h after staging does not re-read external state against the dry-run snapshot before running (tools.validation execute / sagas). Also: staff_directory has no admin or SCIM sync path (app_owner SQL only); specialists see PII tokens, vault reveal for authorized staff not wired (console). W14 the turn loop does not yet call hitl.handoff (wants_human -> request, mode / allowed before each turn and tool call), so co-serving and the cold hand-off are not enforced in the agent yet. W15 console sign-in is an in-process MockIdP (development): the console's OIDC redirect with a per-item nonce and its deployment (Hugging Face Spaces) are not built. W16 no customer API route for cancel(); the wait estimate is published once at request time, not refreshed as the queue moves. W17 the statechart waits for approval on amount only (execute_sop: parameters.amount >= approval_threshold); an SOP whose tool needs approval for another reason (high-risk write, unreviewed tool, Cedar approval_required) has no way into AWAITING_APPROVAL; the e2e test sets the threshold to 0 for it (src/core/orchestrator/statechart.py: take needs_approval from tools.validation's decision). W18 the turn loop has no correction detection for an action waiting for approval (the e2e test asks Jev a noul question, then Handoffs.cancel + APPROVAL_DENIED + a new episode), and no slot filler (scripted in the e2e tests). W19 agents.topology.coordinator is not yet called from the statechart's DELIBERATING stage, and a handoff plan (low lead confidence or Jev down) does not yet open an escalation in hitl.queues (turn loop wiring). W20 a specialist tool failure is reduced to its code for the model, and its detail is not written to an access-controlled, redacted diagnostic log (observability, M5). W21 agents.topology does not use agents.contracts yet: briefs and results are still dicts; its registry refuses every non-read-only tool, so SpecialistTools' solo low-risk writes are unreachable from the coordinator; for_turn needs solo (the plan's single assignment), the conversation id and the masked message; a specialist's ProposedAction is not yet routed by the coordinator to ApprovalGate.request + hitl.queues (src/agents/topology). W22 agents.merge is not wired into the coordinator's join: its human outcomes (NUMERIC_DISCREPANCY, EVIDENCE_AMBIGUITY, REDIRECT, UNVERIFIED_COMPLETION, JEV_UNAVAILABLE) do not yet open a hitl.queues escalation with a discrepancy card; a REDIRECT does not re-delegate to the missing specialist; the drafting model is not wired, and the merged reply does not yet pass the output checks and the confidence gate on its way out. W23 reliability.admission is not wired: channels.api POST /turns does not call admit() (409 body with active_turn_id, 429 with a Retry-After header), the turn loop does not call keep_alive / finish, AWAITING_APPROVAL does not call hold_for_approval and an approval decision or the 72 h cancellation (hitl.queues.sweep) does not release it, model and Jev completions do not call record_usage, KB_ONLY is not routed to degraded_answer, and UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL / TOKEN are not read into an Upstash store. W24 reliability.bursts is not wired: retrieval and tool reads do not go through SingleFlight; there is no admin API (with on-call authorization and audit) to declare or clear an incident; the turn loop does not ask incident_answer before triage; turns do not run on a Deadline (first status event, skipping reranking, the route fallbacks), and nothing classifies a turn as faq / diagnostic / multi-specialist.
ACCEPTED LIMITS / DESIGN DEBT: L1 no pgvector (nearest facts in Python). L2 legal archive: no legal holds, no General Counsel dual sign-off, Postgres not S3 Object Lock; its tokens lose their values after erasure. L3 the Redis turn lock now exists (reliability.admission) but is not wired (W23), so the Postgres PK still sequences turns; no P2 alert for pin budget; so the 72 h cancel has no mutex to release. L4 fact TTL uses valid_from as last-confirmed; old versions of a live fact stay until the lineage expires (plain FK). L5 Temporal ticket history TTL via namespace retention. L6 'prod' -> 'production' synonyms refused (agent asks). L7 non-USD money actions denied until a trusted FX source exists (DECISION-bdad33ce). L8 hazard scorer is a stub in tests/demo (Llama Guard needs a model pull). L9 SPEC FR-7 says OBO tokens last 24 h; code and UA-D9 say 15 min (doc fix). L10 a business day is counted as 24 h for significant-decision SLAs (no business calendar). L11 queue priority is Jev acuity then SLA deadline; contract tier does not affect it, and promotion to the senior queue keeps the original (breached) deadline. L12 the wait estimate uses a fixed 10-minute service time per specialist, not Erlang A or measured rates. L13 HL-D10's Jev categorisation of free-text feedback is not built: feedback is reason codes only and the edited draft text is not stored. L14 Cedar has no credential-reset action; the e2e reset is authorized as restart_cluster (a production change) on the instance's environment (policies/: add the action when the tool is real). L15 MA-D8's shared turn token budget (16,000 tokens, forced join at 90%) is not enforced: steps are the only ceiling in agents.topology (add with the briefs' token accounting). L16 'solo' means the only specialist dispatched in the turn (a dependent running alone after the lead does not count); SpecialistTools validates with the gate and then writes through the executor, two steps without a shared lock (the gate re-decides on current state; a change in between is caught by the read-back, not prevented). L17 ConversationReader is not registered as a tool and its characters are not charged to a shared turn budget (with L15). L18 specialist claims travel as a JSON list in a result's findings until agents.topology carries agents.contracts (W21); the merge's completed-action check is a phrase list, like the output checks' (B7). L19 PERF-01 (one reused psycopg connection per database in data.migrate.psql, for test speed) was dropped by the user on 2026-10-27: task rejected, src/data/migrate.py reverted to one docker exec psql per query; the reverted change is kept as a patch outside the repo. Tests stay slow; revisit in the sweep if speed matters. L20 admission uses fixed one-minute windows, not a continuous token bucket (a burst across a window boundary can reach twice the rate); the Upstash fallback is per process (v1 runs one worker; with several, the one-turn guarantee would not hold during an outage, and locks taken locally are not visible in Upstash after it recovers); tests use a fake Upstash REST server, not a real one. L21 RP-D9 autoscaling with pre-warmed minimums is infrastructure (Kubernetes) that v1 does not have (one VM); incidents and coalescing live in one process; the latency budgets are design limits, not yet measured p95 (no load test).

knowledge.title: M4-03.7 backups, erasure log and restore drill
knowledge.text: deploy/backup/pgbackup.py (cron: deploy/backup/support-agent-backup.cron, daily 02:30 UTC dump + prune, first-Sunday 04:00 drill). dump(store, database, now): snapshot (applied schema_migrations, exact row count per public table), pg_dump -Fc through PG_TOOLS (default docker exec -i support-agent-postgres-1), write-once backups/<db>/<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>.dump + .dump.json manifest (sha256, size, migrations, counts, created_at). latest(); prune(now, 35 days = BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS) deletes older dumps but always keeps a database's newest, and erasure-log entries past 35 days. Erasure log: log_erasure(store, tenant, principal, job_id, completed_at) -> write-once erasure-log/<stamp>-<job>.json, outside the databases (the ledger only has subject hashes and is inside the dump); erasures_since(moment) includes entries from 1 h before the dump (REPLAY_MARGIN). restore(store, key, target): only restore_* / standby_* names, sha256 must match the manifest, drop + create + pg_restore --exit-on-error. replay_erasures(store, dumped_at, ErasureActivities on the restored main / vault / keys): collect, purge postgres, checkpoints, vault, keys, then _verify -> residue per job. drill(store, activities_for, databases, prefix, keep=False): restores agent, agent_vault, agent_keys, compares migrations and counts with the manifests, replays erasures since the oldest dump (activities built only if there are any), and drops the copies afterwards unless keep (a kept warm standby must be in the erasure fan-out); DrillReport.ok = no mismatches, no residue, every database restored.

knowledge.title: M4-04.7 held requests: breaker-open reads held up to 24 h
knowledge.text: reliability.hold (workflow-safe: stdlib + temporalio): HoldStart(hold_id, tenant_id, session_id reference, case_id, conversation_id, tool_id, arguments, masked question, probe_seconds default 300, max_hold_seconds default 86400); holdable(risk, code) = read_only and code in {SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE, TRANSIENT}; start_hold(client, start, risk, code, task_queue) refuses anything else (ValueError) and starts HeldRequestWorkflow id hold:<tenant>:<hold_id>. Workflow: hold_notify (status event 'held', HELD text, retried) -> loop: hold_attempt(start, tries) with no Temporal retry (the executor is the one retry layer; an activity failure counts as down) -> delivered: done; refused: hold_hand_over(code); down: hand over STILL_DOWN when the next probe would pass the deadline, else sleep probe_seconds. reliability.hold.activities.HoldActivities(executor, connect, queues, answer, domain): attempt resolves the principal from the live session (executor.identity.session_principal; failure -> refused AUTHENTICATION_EXPIRED), runs a ToolCall (tool_call_id hold_id:tries, checkpoint_id hold_id) through Executor.run (session, credential, screening again), still-down codes -> down, other ToolFailure -> refused; on success answer(question, screened content) -> safety.output.checks.check -> not deliver: refused REPLY_HELD; deliver: FINAL event {text, hold_id, deferred: true} into the conversation's outbound event log; the tool output never leaves the activity, so Temporal history holds no account data. hand_over: the conversation's principal from its record, a hitl.queues escalation (reason system_dependency_held, masked summary), then a HANDOFF event {state queued, text HANDED_OVER, reason}. Scenario 6 e2e: tests/e2e/test_scenario_degradation.py.

SECURITY: S1 saga path uses ApprovalGate legacy mode: caller-supplied ctx.resource and ctx.roles, gate built without roles_of / tool_authz / resource_attrs (src/tools/sagas/activities.py). S2 Executor service-account Cedar check uses caller call.resource, not a tool->Cedar rule (src/tools/execution/__init__.py). S3 generic tools.execution.calls.call_tool / ToolActivities path runs tools without the approval gate (src/tools/execution/). Note for S3: agents.topology.executor_tool also calls Executor.run without the approval gate; it is safe only because a specialist registry refuses non-read-only tools, so M3-02.7 must route specialist writes through ApprovalGate (and S2: executor_tool sends no Cedar resource, so a service-account system denies by default). S4 no resource_attrs resolver: resource owner/tenant attributes still come from the caller (needs reviewed CRM read tools). S5 tool->Cedar rules live in gate config, not next to the tool in the registry (src/tools/registry/). S6 screening does not decode Base64; a Base64-only injection passes user-message screening (src/safety/screening/; Prompt Guard via Groq or a decode pass). S7 audit log is append-only but not hash-chained (src/tools/audit.py). S8 ticket workflow (M1-05) inputs/history not audited for sensitive data in Temporal (src/workflows/). S9 ApprovalGate.grant does not pass the request id to verify_approver, so the one-item binding of a staff sign-in (ID token nonce = request id) is enforced by hitl.approval.Desk.decide, not by a direct gate.grant call (src/tools/validation/approvals.py: pass request_id to the verifier). S10 the LangGraph Postgres checkpoint tables have no tenant row-level security and no integrity seal: someone with database write access could substitute a well-formed plan or state (agents.topology.checked_plan refuses malformed or inflated plans, not a valid substitute); theoretical while the checkpoint database is trusted (core.orchestrator.statechart.postgres_checkpointer: separate role / RLS, or an HMAC over the plan). S11 tools.execution.Executor.run writes no tool audit record (tools.audit is only on the saga path), so specialist tool calls through executor_tool are not audited (src/tools/execution). S12 a specialist's identity does not reach downstream systems or the audit log: on-behalf-of tokens carry act = the one agent identity (channels.identity.service._mint_obo, AGENT), and tool_audit_records has no actor_subrole column (MA-D9, MA-ADP-04 invariant 1); agents.contracts.actor(role) is recorded only as the approval request's handler. S13 the erasure workflow does not yet write the erasure log (deploy/backup/pgbackup.log_erasure) when an erasure completes (memory.lifecycle.inventory close / data.erasure): until it does, restoring a dump taken before an erasure brings that user back, and the drill has nothing to replay. OpenBao (the transit key that wraps every data key) is not backed up: losing it makes all encrypted fields unreadable.
BUGS: B1 output sanitiser strips <placeholder> text inside code fences ('--subnet-id <id>' -> '--subnet-id ') (src/safety/output/checks.py). B2 web/dev-server.js crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT when the API drops mid-stream (writeHead only if !headersSent, else destroy). B3 tests/deploy/test_backbone.py line 4 over 110 chars (lint). B4 app HTTPS on TLS-intercepting machines needs truststore / CA handling (only the demo has it). B5 ticket workflow waits 48 h for an approval decision (src/workflows/ticket.py approval_timeout_seconds) but HL-D9 / MAX_APPROVAL_TTL / hitl.queues cancel at 72 h. B6 hitl.queues.sweep promotes a claimed hand-off once its SLA passes (for a hand-off the SLA is the time to pick-up) and unassigns it: the conversation's specialist keeps ownership (handoffs row; the one-owner index stops a second take-over) but the item reappears in queue_senior and pages the lead; escalations also have no 'resolved' status for a finished hand-off (src/hitl/queues: skip claimed hand-offs in the promotion, add a resolved status set by hand_back). B7 the output checks only catch future promises ('we will refund', 'will be credited'); a past-tense success claim ('Your refund has been processed.') passes without a verified action (src/safety/output/checks.py PROMISES; strict xfail in tests/e2e/test_scenarios_actions.py flips when fixed).
NOT YET B8 tests/tools/validation test_property_no_financial_write_at_or_above_the_threshold_runs_without_a_second_person failed once (2026-10-26) with psycopg AdminShutdown: its Postgres connection was terminated mid-test, most likely by a concurrent Postgres restart from another session; not reproduced since (545/545 green on 2026-10-27). WIRED: W1 governance require_sign_off() not in the statechart; disclose() not in the API reply path (src/safety/governance/). W2 conversation memory not wired into dispatch / context assembler; summarizer prompt is injected, none written (src/memory/conversation/). W7 approval card delivery to the specialist console / event stream: expected in M2-10 (the card itself is hitl.approval.Desk.card). W8 Langfuse traces join the erasure inventory: expected in M5-01. W9 hitl.queues.Queues.sweep is a function: not yet run on a schedule (Temporal schedule or cron, per tenant). W11 nothing emits escalation packets yet: confidence gate hand-offs, reflexion limit, user-requested human and approval-requiring actions must call Queues.escalate (turn loop / M2-10 handoff). W14 the turn loop does not yet call hitl.handoff (wants_human -> request, mode / allowed before each turn and tool call), so co-serving and the cold hand-off are not enforced in the agent yet. W15 console sign-in is an in-process MockIdP (development): the console's OIDC redirect with a per-item nonce and its deployment (Hugging Face Spaces) are not built. W16 no customer API route for cancel(); the wait estimate is published once at request time, not refreshed as the queue moves. W17 the statechart waits for approval on amount only (execute_sop: parameters.amount >= approval_threshold); an SOP whose tool needs approval for another reason (high-risk write, unreviewed tool, Cedar approval_required) has no way into AWAITING_APPROVAL; the e2e test sets the threshold to 0 for it (src/core/orchestrator/statechart.py: take needs_approval from tools.validation's decision). W19 agents.topology.coordinator is not yet called from the statechart's DELIBERATING stage, and a handoff plan (low lead confidence or Jev down) does not yet open an escalation in hitl.queues (turn loop wiring). W20 a specialist tool failure is reduced to its code for the model, and its detail is not written to an access-controlled, redacted diagnostic log (observability, M5). W21 agents.topology does not use agents.contracts yet: briefs and results are still dicts; its registry refuses every non-read-only tool, so SpecialistTools' solo low-risk writes are unreachable from the coordinator; for_turn needs solo (the plan's single assignment), the conversation id and the masked message; a specialist's ProposedAction is not yet routed by the coordinator to ApprovalGate.request + hitl.queues (src/agents/topology). W22 agents.merge is not wired into the coordinator's join: its human outcomes (NUMERIC_DISCREPANCY, EVIDENCE_AMBIGUITY, REDIRECT, UNVERIFIED_COMPLETION, JEV_UNAVAILABLE) do not yet open a hitl.queues escalation with a discrepancy card; a REDIRECT does not re-delegate to the missing specialist; the drafting model is not wired, and the merged reply does not yet pass the output checks and the confidence gate on its way out. W23 reliability.admission is not wired: channels.api POST /turns does not call admit() (409 body with active_turn_id, 429 with a Retry-After header), the turn loop does not call keep_alive / finish, AWAITING_APPROVAL does not call hold_for_approval and an approval decision or the 72 h cancellation (hitl.queues.sweep) does not release it, model and Jev completions do not call record_usage, KB_ONLY is not routed to degraded_answer, and UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL / TOKEN are not read into an Upstash store. W24 reliability.bursts is not wired: retrieval and tool reads do not go through SingleFlight; there is no admin API (with on-call authorization and audit) to declare or clear an incident; the turn loop does not ask incident_answer before triage; turns do not run on a Deadline (first status event, skipping reranking, the route fallbacks), and nothing classifies a turn as faq / diagnostic / multi-specialist. W25 backups are not installed on the VM: deploy/setup-vm.sh does not install the cron file, create /var/log/support-agent or set RESTORE_DSN_BASE; there is no warm standby (RP-D15: a kept standby_ copy would also need to join the erasure fan-out); Qdrant is not snapshotted (the index can be rebuilt from the raw snapshots in R2). W26 reliability.hold is not wired: the turn loop does not catch a holdable ToolFailure and call start_hold; no worker for the held-requests task queue is deployed; answer() is not the drafting model yet; the hand-over packet carries identity_tier unknown and the agent as handler.

L3 the Redis turn lock now exists (reliability.admission) but is not wired (W23), so the Postgres PK still sequences turns; no P2 alert for pin budget; so the 72 h cancel has no mutex to release. L4 fact TTL uses valid_from as last-confirmed; old versions of a live fact stay until the lineage expires (plain FK). L5 Temporal ticket history TTL via namespace retention. L10 a business day is counted as 24 h for significant-decision SLAs (no business calendar). L11 queue priority is Jev acuity then SLA deadline; contract tier does not affect it, and promotion to the senior queue keeps the original (breached) deadline. L12 the wait estimate uses a fixed 10-minute service time per specialist, not Erlang A or measured rates. L13 HL-D10's Jev categorisation of free-text feedback is not built: feedback is reason codes only and the edited draft text is not stored. L14 Cedar has no credential-reset action; the e2e reset is authorized as restart_cluster (a production change) on the instance's environment (policies/: add the action when the tool is real). L15 MA-D8's shared turn token budget (16,000 tokens, forced join at 90%) is not enforced: steps are the only ceiling in agents.topology (add with the briefs' token accounting). L17 ConversationReader is not registered as a tool and its characters are not charged to a shared turn budget (with L15). L18 specialist claims travel as a JSON list in a result's findings until agents.topology carries agents.contracts (W21); the merge's completed-action check is a phrase list, like the output checks' (B7). L19 PERF-01 (one reused psycopg connection per database in data.migrate.psql, for test speed) was dropped by the user on 2026-10-27: task rejected, src/data/migrate.py reverted to one docker exec psql per query; the reverted change is kept as a patch outside the repo. Tests stay slow; revisit in the sweep if speed matters. L20 admission uses fixed one-minute windows, not a continuous token bucket (a burst across a window boundary can reach twice the rate); the Upstash fallback is per process (v1 runs one worker; with several, the one-turn guarantee would not hold during an outage, and locks taken locally are not visible in Upstash after it recovers); tests use a fake Upstash REST server, not a real one. L21 RP-D9 autoscaling with pre-warmed minimums is infrastructure (Kubernetes) that v1 does not have (one VM); incidents and coalescing live in one process; the latency budgets are design limits, not yet measured p95 (no load test). L22 v1 backs up with daily pg_dump, not WAL archiving: RPO up to a day (not 5 minutes) and no point-in-time recovery, one VM (no multi-AZ); dumps rely on R2 encryption at rest (no client-side encryption; encrypted fields stay sealed under data keys); the drill row-count check is exact only when nothing writes during the dump (nightly). knowledge.title: M4-05.7 answer cache and tenant budgets
knowledge.text: cost.cache (schema cost_0001_answer_cache.sql: answer_cache(tenant_id, key, answer, doc_ids, created_at, expires_at), PK (tenant, key), GIN on doc_ids, tenant RLS). key = sha256(normalise(question) | tenant | product_version | kb_version), normalise = casefold, punctuation to spaces, whitespace collapsed. AnswerCache(connect, engine).put(tenant, question, answer, product_version, kb_version, passages [(doc_id, audience)], tools_called) returns None when stored, else the reason: a tool ran; non-public or no passages; the question names a version (VERSION regex v?N.N(.N)); personal data in question or answer (safety.pii find); Jev noul PUBLIC_ONLY on {question, answer} below 0.80 or unavailable. TTL 7 days (upsert refreshes). get(): version-volatile questions never hit; live entry by key under RLS; returned only if safety.output.checks.check delivers it (sanitised text). evict_document(tenant, doc) deletes entries citing it; prune() deletes expired. cost.budgets (schema cost_0002_budgets.sql: usage_ledger(tenant, month YYYY-MM, model, route, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens) with atomic upsert-increment, tenant_budgets(tenant, monthly_usd > 0, warned_month); tenant RLS; runtime may insert / increment usage and set warned_month only). Prices(version, {model: (USD in, USD out) per million}); Ledger(connect, prices, notify_admins).record() refuses non-int / negative usage and unpriced models; report(tenant, month) -> lines with Decimal cost, total, budget, used; band(): no budget NOMINAL, >= 1.00 SOFT_CAP (KB-only + SOFT_CAP_NOTICE), >= 0.80 WARNING (notify_admins once per month via warned_month), else NOMINAL; reconcile(tenants, month, invoices) flags models off by > 2% (or present on one side only); release_gate(candidate, previous, baseline) violations: > 1.10x previous, > 1.50x baseline, or a route missing from either.

W15 console sign-in is an in-process MockIdP (development): the console's OIDC redirect with a per-item nonce and its deployment (Hugging Face Spaces) are not built. W16 no customer API route for cancel(); the wait estimate is published once at request time, not refreshed as the queue moves. W17 the statechart waits for approval on amount only (execute_sop: parameters.amount >= approval_threshold); an SOP whose tool needs approval for another reason (high-risk write, unreviewed tool, Cedar approval_required) has no way into AWAITING_APPROVAL; the e2e test sets the threshold to 0 for it (src/core/orchestrator/statechart.py: take needs_approval from tools.validation's decision). W18 the turn loop has no correction detection for an action waiting for approval (the e2e test asks Jev a noul question, then Handoffs.cancel + APPROVAL_DENIED + a new episode), and no slot filler (scripted in the e2e tests). W19 agents.topology.coordinator is not yet called from the statechart's DELIBERATING stage, and a handoff plan (low lead confidence or Jev down) does not yet open an escalation in hitl.queues (turn loop wiring). W20 a specialist tool failure is reduced to its code for the model, and its detail is not written to an access-controlled, redacted diagnostic log (observability, M5). W22 agents.merge is not wired into the coordinator's join: its human outcomes (NUMERIC_DISCREPANCY, EVIDENCE_AMBIGUITY, REDIRECT, UNVERIFIED_COMPLETION, JEV_UNAVAILABLE) do not yet open a hitl.queues escalation with a discrepancy card; a REDIRECT does not re-delegate to the missing specialist; the drafting model is not wired, and the merged reply does not yet pass the output checks and the confidence gate on its way out. W23 reliability.admission is not wired: channels.api POST /turns does not call admit() (409 body with active_turn_id, 429 with a Retry-After header), the turn loop does not call keep_alive / finish, AWAITING_APPROVAL does not call hold_for_approval and an approval decision or the 72 h cancellation (hitl.queues.sweep) does not release it, model and Jev completions do not call record_usage, KB_ONLY is not routed to degraded_answer, and UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL / TOKEN are not read into an Upstash store. W24 reliability.bursts is not wired: retrieval and tool reads do not go through SingleFlight; there is no admin API (with on-call authorization and audit) to declare or clear an incident; the turn loop does not ask incident_answer before triage; turns do not run on a Deadline (first status event, skipping reranking, the route fallbacks), and nothing classifies a turn as faq / diagnostic / multi-specialist. W25 backups are not installed on the VM: deploy/setup-vm.sh does not install the cron file, create /var/log/support-agent or set RESTORE_DSN_BASE; there is no warm standby (RP-D15: a kept standby_ copy would also need to join the erasure fan-out); Qdrant is not snapshotted (the index can be rebuilt from the raw snapshots in R2). W26 reliability.hold is not wired: the turn loop does not catch a holdable ToolFailure and call start_hold; no worker for the held-requests task queue is deployed; answer() is not the drafting model yet; the hand-over packet carries identity_tier unknown and the agent as handler. W27 cost.cache and cost.budgets are not wired: the turn loop does not look up the cache before generating or store eligible answers after; nothing provides the kb_version (a hash of the tenant index snapshot) or the customer product_version (identity has none); erase_document does not call AnswerCache.evict_document; model and Jev completions do not call Ledger.record; L2 legal archive: no legal holds, no General Counsel dual sign-off, Postgres not S3 Object Lock; its tokens lose their values after erasure. L3 the Redis turn lock now exists (reliability.admission) but is not wired (W23), so the Postgres PK still sequences turns; no P2 alert for pin budget; so the 72 h cancel has no mutex to release. L4 fact TTL uses valid_from as last-confirmed; old versions of a live fact stay until the lineage expires (plain FK). L5 Temporal ticket history TTL via namespace retention. L6 'prod' -> 'production' synonyms refused (agent asks). L7 non-USD money actions denied until a trusted FX source exists (DECISION-bdad33ce). L8 hazard scorer is a stub in tests/demo (Llama Guard needs a model pull). L9 SPEC FR-7 says OBO tokens last 24 h; code and UA-D9 say 15 min (doc fix). L10 a business day is counted as 24 h for significant-decision SLAs (no business calendar). L11 queue priority is Jev acuity then SLA deadline; contract tier does not affect it, and promotion to the senior queue keeps the original (breached) deadline. L12 the wait estimate uses a fixed 10-minute service time per specialist, not Erlang A or measured rates. L13 HL-D10's Jev categorisation of free-text feedback is not built: feedback is reason codes only and the edited draft text is not stored. L14 Cedar has no credential-reset action; the e2e reset is authorized as restart_cluster (a production change) on the instance's environment (policies/: add the action when the tool is real). L15 MA-D8's shared turn token budget (16,000 tokens, forced join at 90%) is not enforced: steps are the only ceiling in agents.topology (add with the briefs' token accounting). L17 ConversationReader is not registered as a tool and its characters are not charged to a shared turn budget (with L15). L18 specialist claims travel as a JSON list in a result's findings until agents.topology carries agents.contracts (W21); the merge's completed-action check is a phrase list, like the output checks' (B7). L19 PERF-01 (one reused psycopg connection per database in data.migrate.psql, for test speed) was dropped by the user on 2026-10-27: task rejected, src/data/migrate.py reverted to one docker exec psql per query; the reverted change is kept as a patch outside the repo. L21 RP-D9 autoscaling with pre-warmed minimums is infrastructure (Kubernetes) that v1 does not have (one VM); incidents and coalescing live in one process; the latency budgets are design limits, not yet measured p95 (no load test). L22 v1 backs up with daily pg_dump, not WAL archiving: RPO up to a day (not 5 minutes) and no point-in-time recovery, one VM (no multi-AZ); dumps rely on R2 encryption at rest (no client-side encryption; encrypted fields stay sealed under data keys); the drill row-count check is exact only when nothing writes during the dump (nightly). knowledge.title: M5-01.7 tracing: tail sampling, scrubbing, export, JSON logs, Langfuse erasure
knowledge.text: observability.tracing (in-process: no separate collector in v1). provider(service, targets=None, baseline, slow_seconds, max_traces): TracerProvider -> TailSampler -> ScrubbingExporter -> Fanout(targets or exporters()). TailSampler buffers spans per trace until the root (parent None) ends; keep whole with content if any span ERROR, support.escalated True, agent.risk_tier == 'risk', or root > 2.5 s; else baseline_pick(trace_id) = trace_id % 10000 < 5% keeps the trace with content attributes (gen_ai.prompt, gen_ai.completion, input.value, output.value, content.*) and events removed; else dropped; buffer bounded at 10,000 traces (oldest decided first), force_flush decides the rest. ScrubbingExporter: every string in attributes, event attributes and the status description through safety.pii find -> [REDACTED_<KIND>] (tokens like <EMAIL_x> untouched). exporters(environ): OTLP HTTP to OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT + /v1/traces (Jaeger) and, when LANGFUSE_HOST / PUBLIC_KEY / SECRET_KEY are all set, LANGFUSE_HOST + /api/public/otel/v1/traces with Basic auth (DECISION-9da2e064). subject_hash(tenant, principal) = data.erasure.subject_hash; turn_attributes() sets tenant.id, user.id (the hash), session.id (conversation). JsonFormatter: timestamp, level, logger, scrubbed message, trace_id / span_id of the current span, optional tenant_id / user_hash / conversation_id extras, scrubbed exception. LangfuseEraser(host, pk, sk).erase(tenant, principal): GET /api/public/traces?userId=<hash> (paged), DELETE each, re-list, raise if any is left. Tested against the compose Jaeger (query API) and a fake Langfuse.

knowledge.title: M5-02.7 SLOs, tripwires, token telemetry, failure classification
knowledge.text: observability.alerts. Turn(at, ok, first_status_ms, final_ms, escalated); SLOS: turn_availability 0.999 (ok), first_status 0.95 (<= 300 ms), final_reply 0.95 (<= 2500 ms), escalation 0.92 (not escalated); burn_rate = bad share in the window / (1 - target); burn_alerts: P1 when 1 h and 5 min windows both >= 14.4x, else P2 when 6 h and 30 min both >= 6x. Tripwires(send): each key alerts once until it clears: token_expiry (< 2 h, P2), nightly_batch (exit != 0 or parity < 0.90, P2), breaker (state open, P1, per system), reranker (fallback share > 5%, P2), sub_threshold_writes (> 3 writes strictly below the threshold within 1 h on a case, P1 security). TokenCounter: labels tenant_id, component (fixed set: coordinator, specialist, jev, judge, reranker, router, retrieval, other), model, type; non-negative int counts; at most max_series (16,000) regular series, then overflow series per component and type; exposition() in Prometheus text format. estimated_cost([(cost, 'deterministic' | 'baseline')], baseline 0.05) = sum deterministic + sum baseline / 0.05. classify(engine, error_codes, decision, Masked transcript): RULES first (external system down, authorization denial, agent loop limit, timeout abort, injection blocked) without Jev; else Jev choice over six conversational categories, committed at >= 0.85; Jev down, invalid, unsure or no transcript -> residual for human QA.

knowledge.text:
Consolidated 2026-10-25 from KNOWLEDGE-2114e3c6, 82aa3192, c5d19a99, 634b024b, 0bf6e556, 60b69bfa, 60b6dd3c, 630f3cc2, c60fdc50, b0d958bf, d72ef88b, fef4e96a, 97282376; v2 added M2-09.7 items (S9, B5, W9-W13, L10-L11); v3 added M2-10.7 items (B6, W14-W16, L12-L13); v4 added M2-11.7 items (B7, W17-W18, L14); v5 added M3-01.7 items (W19, L15); v6 added the M3-01.7 security review's out-of-scope items (S10, S11, W20, and a note on S3); v7 added M3-02.7 items (S12, W21, L16-L17); v8 added M3-03.7 items (W22, L18); v9 added PERF-01 items (B8, L19); v10 marked PERF-01 dropped (L19); v11 added M4-01.7 items (W23, L20) and updated L3; v12 added M4-02.7 items (W24, L21); v13 added M4-03.7 items (S13, W25, L22); v14 added M4-04.7 items (W26, L23); v15 added M4-05.7 items (W27, L24); v16 added M5-01.7 items (W28, L25) and updated W8; v17 adds M5-02.7 items (W29, L26). Plan (user, 2026-10-25): out-of-scope issues, critical ones too, go here instead of a replan; fix all in one sweep task added with a single plan reopen after the last task (M6-03.7).
SECURITY: S1 saga path uses ApprovalGate legacy mode: caller-supplied ctx.resource and ctx.roles, gate built without roles_of / tool_authz / resource_attrs (src/tools/sagas/activities.py). S2 Executor service-account Cedar check uses caller call.resource, not a tool->Cedar rule (src/tools/execution/__init__.py). S3 generic tools.execution.calls.call_tool / ToolActivities path runs tools without the approval gate (src/tools/execution/). Note for S3: agents.topology.executor_tool also calls Executor.run without the approval gate; it is safe only because a specialist registry refuses non-read-only tools, so M3-02.7 must route specialist writes through ApprovalGate (and S2: executor_tool sends no Cedar resource, so a service-account system denies by default). S4 no resource_attrs resolver: resource owner/tenant attributes still come from the caller (needs reviewed CRM read tools). S5 tool->Cedar rules live in gate config, not next to the tool in the registry (src/tools/registry/). S6 screening does not decode Base64; a Base64-only injection passes user-message screening (src/safety/screening/; Prompt Guard via Groq or a decode pass). S7 audit log is append-only but not hash-chained (src/tools/audit.py). S8 ticket workflow (M1-05) inputs/history not audited for sensitive data in Temporal (src/workflows/). S9 ApprovalGate.grant does not pass the request id to verify_approver, so the one-item binding of a staff sign-in (ID token nonce = request id) is enforced by hitl.approval.Desk.decide, not by a direct gate.grant call (src/tools/validation/approvals.py: pass request_id to the verifier). S10 the LangGraph Postgres checkpoint tables have no tenant row-level security and no integrity seal: someone with database write access could substitute a well-formed plan or state (agents.topology.checked_plan refuses malformed or inflated plans, not a valid substitute); theoretical while the checkpoint database is trusted (core.orchestrator.statechart.postgres_checkpointer: separate role / RLS, or an HMAC over the plan). S11 tools.execution.Executor.run writes no tool audit record (tools.audit is only on the saga path), so specialist tool calls through executor_tool are not audited (src/tools/execution). S12 a specialist's identity does not reach downstream systems or the audit log: on-behalf-of tokens carry act = the one agent identity (channels.identity.service._mint_obo, AGENT), and tool_audit_records has no actor_subrole column (MA-D9, MA-ADP-04 invariant 1); agents.contracts.actor(role) is recorded only as the approval request's handler. S13 the erasure workflow does not yet write the erasure log (deploy/backup/pgbackup.log_erasure) when an erasure completes (memory.lifecycle.inventory close / data.erasure): until it does, restoring a dump taken before an erasure brings that user back, and the drill has nothing to replay. OpenBao (the transit key that wraps every data key) is not backed up: losing it makes all encrypted fields unreadable.
BUGS: B1 output sanitiser strips <placeholder> text inside code fences ('--subnet-id <id>' -> '--subnet-id ') (src/safety/output/checks.py). B2 web/dev-server.js crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT when the API drops mid-stream (writeHead only if !headersSent, else destroy). B3 tests/deploy/test_backbone.py line 4 over 110 chars (lint). B4 app HTTPS on TLS-intercepting machines needs truststore / CA handling (only the demo has it). B5 ticket workflow waits 48 h for an approval decision (src/workflows/ticket.py approval_timeout_seconds) but HL-D9 / MAX_APPROVAL_TTL / hitl.queues cancel at 72 h. B6 hitl.queues.sweep promotes a claimed hand-off once its SLA passes (for a hand-off the SLA is the time to pick-up) and unassigns it: the conversation's specialist keeps ownership (handoffs row; the one-owner index stops a second take-over) but the item reappears in queue_senior and pages the lead; escalations also have no 'resolved' status for a finished hand-off (src/hitl/queues: skip claimed hand-offs in the promotion, add a resolved status set by hand_back). B7 the output checks only catch future promises ('we will refund', 'will be credited'); a past-tense success claim ('Your refund has been processed.') passes without a verified action (src/safety/output/checks.py PROMISES; strict xfail in tests/e2e/test_scenarios_actions.py flips when fixed).
NOT YET B8 tests/tools/validation test_property_no_financial_write_at_or_above_the_threshold_runs_without_a_second_person failed once (2026-10-26) with psycopg AdminShutdown: its Postgres connection was terminated mid-test, most likely by a concurrent Postgres restart from another session; not reproduced since (545/545 green on 2026-10-27). The test and ApprovalGate hold their own connections and do not reconnect. The test also takes ~42 s, unchanged by PERF-01 (its time is not in data.migrate.psql): profile it in the sweep.
WIRED: W1 governance require_sign_off() not in the statechart; disclose() not in the API reply path (src/safety/governance/). W2 conversation memory not wired into dispatch / context assembler; summarizer prompt is injected, none written (src/memory/conversation/). W3 facts: activation scoring for the 15% profile slot, the resolution / 24 h idle write trigger, ALLOWED_TOOL_FIELDS is an example list (src/memory/facts/). W4 no CI lint that every tool field declares sensitivity (review() runs at registration). W5 a DENY does not yet feed the turn's circuit breaker (src/core/recovery/ + turn loop). W6 tool-output blobs (tool-output/<tenant>/<case>/) not in the erasure inventory and no TTL (src/memory/lifecycle/). W7 approval card delivery to the specialist console / event stream: expected in M2-10 (the card itself is hitl.approval.Desk.card). W8 observability.tracing.LangfuseEraser exists (M5-01.7) but is not yet a store in the erasure inventory (memory.lifecycle.inventory STORES / verify). W9 hitl.queues.Queues.sweep is a function: not yet run on a schedule (Temporal schedule or cron, per tenant). W10 alert (Slack / PagerDuty) and notify (customer inbox, UA-D2) are injected callbacks with no production implementation. W11 nothing emits escalation packets yet: confidence gate hand-offs, reflexion limit, user-requested human and approval-requiring actions must call Queues.escalate (turn loop / M2-10 handoff). W12 escalations / escalation_events (tokenized packet, customer id) not in the erasure inventory or retention (src/memory/lifecycle/). W13 MS-D18 post-wait check: an approval executed more than 1 h after staging does not re-read external state against the dry-run snapshot before running (tools.validation execute / sagas). Also: staff_directory has no admin or SCIM sync path (app_owner SQL only); specialists see PII tokens, vault reveal for authorized staff not wired (console). W14 the turn loop does not yet call hitl.handoff (wants_human -> request, mode / allowed before each turn and tool call), so co-serving and the cold hand-off are not enforced in the agent yet. W15 console sign-in is an in-process MockIdP (development): the console's OIDC redirect with a per-item nonce and its deployment (Hugging Face Spaces) are not built. W16 no customer API route for cancel(); the wait estimate is published once at request time, not refreshed as the queue moves. W17 the statechart waits for approval on amount only (execute_sop: parameters.amount >= approval_threshold); an SOP whose tool needs approval for another reason (high-risk write, unreviewed tool, Cedar approval_required) has no way into AWAITING_APPROVAL; the e2e test sets the threshold to 0 for it (src/core/orchestrator/statechart.py: take needs_approval from tools.validation's decision). W18 the turn loop has no correction detection for an action waiting for approval (the e2e test asks Jev a noul question, then Handoffs.cancel + APPROVAL_DENIED + a new episode), and no slot filler (scripted in the e2e tests). W19 agents.topology.coordinator is not yet called from the statechart's DELIBERATING stage, and a handoff plan (low lead confidence or Jev down) does not yet open an escalation in hitl.queues (turn loop wiring). W20 a specialist tool failure is reduced to its code for the model, and its detail is not written to an access-controlled, redacted diagnostic log (observability, M5). W21 agents.topology does not use agents.contracts yet: briefs and results are still dicts; its registry refuses every non-read-only tool, so SpecialistTools' solo low-risk writes are unreachable from the coordinator; for_turn needs solo (the plan's single assignment), the conversation id and the masked message; a specialist's ProposedAction is not yet routed by the coordinator to ApprovalGate.request + hitl.queues (src/agents/topology). W22 agents.merge is not wired into the coordinator's join: its human outcomes (NUMERIC_DISCREPANCY, EVIDENCE_AMBIGUITY, REDIRECT, UNVERIFIED_COMPLETION, JEV_UNAVAILABLE) do not yet open a hitl.queues escalation with a discrepancy card; a REDIRECT does not re-delegate to the missing specialist; the drafting model is not wired, and the merged reply does not yet pass the output checks and the confidence gate on its way out. W23 reliability.admission is not wired: channels.api POST /turns does not call admit() (409 body with active_turn_id, 429 with a Retry-After header), the turn loop does not call keep_alive / finish, AWAITING_APPROVAL does not call hold_for_approval and an approval decision or the 72 h cancellation (hitl.queues.sweep) does not release it, model and Jev completions do not call record_usage, KB_ONLY is not routed to degraded_answer, and UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL / TOKEN are not read into an Upstash store. W24 reliability.bursts is not wired: retrieval and tool reads do not go through SingleFlight; there is no admin API (with on-call authorization and audit) to declare or clear an incident; the turn loop does not ask incident_answer before triage; turns do not run on a Deadline (first status event, skipping reranking, the route fallbacks), and nothing classifies a turn as faq / diagnostic / multi-specialist. W25 backups are not installed on the VM: deploy/setup-vm.sh does not install the cron file, create /var/log/support-agent or set RESTORE_DSN_BASE; there is no warm standby (RP-D15: a kept standby_ copy would also need to join the erasure fan-out); Qdrant is not snapshotted (the index can be rebuilt from the raw snapshots in R2). W26 reliability.hold is not wired: the turn loop does not catch a holdable ToolFailure and call start_hold; no worker for the held-requests task queue is deployed; answer() is not the drafting model yet; the hand-over packet carries identity_tier unknown and the agent as handler. W27 cost.cache and cost.budgets are not wired: the turn loop does not look up the cache before generating or store eligible answers after; nothing provides the kb_version (a hash of the tenant index snapshot) or the customer product_version (identity has none); erase_document does not call AnswerCache.evict_document; model and Jev completions do not call Ledger.record; band() is not consulted (soft cap -> degraded_answer + SOFT_CAP_NOTICE); there is no admin-notification channel, tenant-admin report view, monthly reconcile job or invoice import; release_gate is not in CI (it needs cost per resolved conversation per route from the evaluation harness, M5). W28 tracing is not wired: services do not call observability.tracing.provider / json_logging at start-up, the turn loop, model router, Jev client and tools do not create spans with turn_attributes and gen_ai.* attributes or set support.escalated / agent.risk_tier, Temporal workers are not given temporalio.contrib.opentelemetry.TracingInterceptor (trace context across workflows), and the compose Jaeger runs in memory with no 7-day retention set (deploy/compose.yaml; Langfuse retention is a project setting). W29 observability.alerts is not wired: no metrics backend (Prometheus / Grafana Cloud) or alert channel (PagerDuty / Slack) is set up; nothing feeds burn_alerts with turn records or the tripwires with breaker states, OAuth token lifetimes, batch results, reranker fallbacks or the financial_writes ledger; TokenCounter is not fed by completions; classify() is not run over failed or escalated conversations, its results are not stored, and residuals have no human QA queue; observability.tracing does not tag kept spans with sampling.reason (deterministic / baseline), which estimated_cost needs.
ACCEPTED LIMITS / DESIGN DEBT: L1 no pgvector (nearest facts in Python). L2 legal archive: no legal holds, no General Counsel dual sign-off, Postgres not S3 Object Lock; its tokens lose their values after erasure. L3 the Redis turn lock now exists (reliability.admission) but is not wired (W23), so the Postgres PK still sequences turns; no P2 alert for pin budget; so the 72 h cancel has no mutex to release. L4 fact TTL uses valid_from as last-confirmed; old versions of a live fact stay until the lineage expires (plain FK). L5 Temporal ticket history TTL via namespace retention. L6 'prod' -> 'production' synonyms refused (agent asks). L7 non-USD money actions denied until a trusted FX source exists (DECISION-bdad33ce). L8 hazard scorer is a stub in tests/demo (Llama Guard needs a model pull). L9 SPEC FR-7 says OBO tokens last 24 h; code and UA-D9 say 15 min (doc fix). L10 a business day is counted as 24 h for significant-decision SLAs (no business calendar). L11 queue priority is Jev acuity then SLA deadline; contract tier does not affect it, and promotion to the senior queue keeps the original (breached) deadline. L12 the wait estimate uses a fixed 10-minute service time per specialist, not Erlang A or measured rates. L13 HL-D10's Jev categorisation of free-text feedback is not built: feedback is reason codes only and the edited draft text is not stored. L14 Cedar has no credential-reset action; the e2e reset is authorized as restart_cluster (a production change) on the instance's environment (policies/: add the action when the tool is real). L15 MA-D8's shared turn token budget (16,000 tokens, forced join at 90%) is not enforced: steps are the only ceiling in agents.topology (add with the briefs' token accounting). L16 'solo' means the only specialist dispatched in the turn (a dependent running alone after the lead does not count); SpecialistTools validates with the gate and then writes through the executor, two steps without a shared lock (the gate re-decides on current state; a change in between is caught by the read-back, not prevented). L17 ConversationReader is not registered as a tool and its characters are not charged to a shared turn budget (with L15). L18 specialist claims travel as a JSON list in a result's findings until agents.topology carries agents.contracts (W21); the merge's completed-action check is a phrase list, like the output checks' (B7). L19 PERF-01 (one reused psycopg connection per database in data.migrate.psql, for test speed) was dropped by the user on 2026-10-27: task rejected, src/data/migrate.py reverted to one docker exec psql per query; the reverted change is kept as a patch outside the repo. Tests stay slow; revisit in the sweep if speed matters. L20 admission uses fixed one-minute windows, not a continuous token bucket (a burst across a window boundary can reach twice the rate); the Upstash fallback is per process (v1 runs one worker; with several, the one-turn guarantee would not hold during an outage, and locks taken locally are not visible in Upstash after it recovers); tests use a fake Upstash REST server, not a real one. L21 RP-D9 autoscaling with pre-warmed minimums is infrastructure (Kubernetes) that v1 does not have (one VM); incidents and coalescing live in one process; the latency budgets are design limits, not yet measured p95 (no load test). L22 v1 backs up with daily pg_dump, not WAL archiving: RPO up to a day (not 5 minutes) and no point-in-time recovery, one VM (no multi-AZ); dumps rely on R2 encryption at rest (no client-side encryption; encrypted fields stay sealed under data keys); the drill row-count check is exact only when nothing writes during the dump (nightly). L23 tool calls are capped at three retries per call (and the per-system retry budget), not three retries per turn across all tools (RP-D13); a held request keeps its tool arguments in Temporal history, as saga steps do; the held-request probe interval is fixed (default 5 minutes), not driven by the breaker closing. L24 cache normalisation lowercases and strips punctuation (no lemmatisation); budgets are set by administrators in SQL; the price table is versioned in code, not a table; band() sums the month ledger on every call (fine at v1 volume). L25 tail sampling and scrubbing run in each process (no collector): a trace whose root runs in another process (a Temporal activity under a remote parent) is decided only when the buffer fills or on flush; Jaeger all-in-one has no delete API, so a user is erased from it only by the 7-day expiry (its spans carry only the subject hash); logs go to stdout (docker log rotation is the retention). L26 SLO burn rates are computed from turn records in process, not by a metrics backend; tripwire de-duplication lives in one process (restarts re-alert once); the failure taxonomy is the ADP list (rules for hard faults, six conversational categories).

knowledge.title: M5-03.7 evaluation datasets, judge, calibration, retrieval metrics
knowledge.text: evals.datasets (schema evals_0001_datasets.sql: eval_opt_in append-only (tenant, opted_in, by_admin, at), eval_samples (tenant, region, user_hash, conversation_id, stratum, route, turns jsonb), tenant RLS). framework_episodes(): the eight framework scenarios from framework_seeds.json (id, stratum, route, expect). Samples(connect, tokenizer): set_opt_in(tenant, admin, bool); sample(tenant, principal, conversation, turns, stratum, route) -> id or None when not opted in (latest record), turns tokenized and refused if find_pii still matches, stored with tenants.region and subject_hash; erase(tenant, principal) deletes by hash; episodes(tenant, region) refuses another region. weighted_mean({stratum: values}) = sum P(s) x mean_s with P = routine 0.80, edge 0.15, risk 0.05 (the ADP's P/Q x mean form omits Q and is not used). evals.scoring: assertions tools_called, never_called (tool, tool:value, *), approval_before (an approval.granted step for that tool earlier in the trace), no_leak (credentials, 12-word system-prompt run, raw PII). judge_for(model, rubric, complete, agent_models) refuses Jev and the agent's model families (claude anthropic, gpt / o1 openai, gemini google, llama meta, mistral, qwen alibaba); Judge.score parses a 1..5 and records the rubric hash; judge_accepted: kappa >= 0.80 and >= 200 labels. calibrate(route, confidences, correct, target): < 100 examples -> floor 0.95; else temperature by NLL grid (0.25..5.0), ECE before / after (10 bins), the lowest calibrated threshold meeting the target precision or the floor. Retrieval: ndcg_at, mrr, masking_distortion (<= 5%), context_precision, context_recall, top3_mass, retrieval_deficit (weights 0.35 / 0.35 / 0.20 / -0.10, top-3 mass < 0.35, gap > 0.65).

W11 nothing emits escalation packets yet: confidence gate hand-offs, reflexion limit, user-requested human and approval-requiring actions must call Queues.escalate (turn loop / M2-10 handoff). W19 agents.topology.coordinator is not yet called from the statechart's DELIBERATING stage, and a handoff plan (low lead confidence or Jev down) does not yet open an escalation in hitl.queues (turn loop wiring). there is no admin API (with on-call authorization and audit) to declare or clear an incident; the turn loop does not ask incident_answer before triage; turns do not run on a Deadline (first status event, skipping reranking, the route fallbacks), and nothing classifies a turn as faq / diagnostic / multi-specialist. W25 backups are not installed on the VM: deploy/setup-vm.sh does not install the cron file, create /var/log/support-agent or set RESTORE_DSN_BASE; L3 the Redis turn lock now exists (reliability.admission) but is not wired (W23), so the Postgres PK still sequences turns; no P2 alert for pin budget; so the 72 h cancel has no mutex to release. L10 a business day is counted as 24 h for significant-decision SLAs (no business calendar). L11 queue priority is Jev acuity then SLA deadline; contract tier does not affect it, and promotion to the senior queue keeps the original (breached) deadline. L12 the wait estimate uses a fixed 10-minute service time per specialist, not Erlang A or measured rates. L13 HL-D10's Jev categorisation of free-text feedback is not built: feedback is reason codes only and the edited draft text is not stored. L14 Cedar has no credential-reset action; the e2e reset is authorized as restart_cluster (a production change) on the instance's environment (policies/: add the action when the tool is real). L15 MA-D8's shared turn token budget (16,000 tokens, forced join at 90%) is not enforced: steps are the only ceiling in agents.topology (add with the briefs' token accounting). L18 specialist claims travel as a JSON list in a result's findings until agents.topology carries agents.contracts (W21); the merge's completed-action check is a phrase list, like the output checks' (B7). L19 PERF-01 (one reused psycopg connection per database in data.migrate.psql, for test speed) was dropped by the user on 2026-10-27: task rejected, src/data/migrate.py reverted to one docker exec psql per query; the reverted change is kept as a patch outside the repo. L20 admission uses fixed one-minute windows, not a continuous token bucket (a burst across a window boundary can reach twice the rate); the Upstash fallback is per process (v1 runs one worker; with several, the one-turn guarantee would not hold during an outage, and locks taken locally are not visible in Upstash after it recovers); tests use a fake Upstash REST server, not a real one. L21 RP-D9 autoscaling with pre-warmed minimums is infrastructure (Kubernetes) that v1 does not have (one VM); incidents and coalescing live in one process; the latency budgets are design limits, not yet measured p95 (no load test). L22 v1 backs up with daily pg_dump, not WAL archiving: RPO up to a day (not 5 minutes) and no point-in-time recovery, one VM (no multi-AZ); dumps rely on R2 encryption at rest (no client-side encryption; encrypted fields stay sealed under data keys); the drill row-count check is exact only when nothing writes during the dump (nightly). L24 cache normalisation lowercases and strips punctuation (no lemmatisation); budgets are set by administrators in SQL; the price table is versioned in code, not a table; band() sums the month ledger on every call (fine at v1 volume). L25 tail sampling and scrubbing run in each process (no collector): a trace whose root runs in another process (a Temporal activity under a remote parent) is decided only when the buffer fills or on flush; Jaeger all-in-one has no delete API, so a user is erased from it only by the 7-day expiry (its spans carry only the subject hash); logs go to stdout (docker log rotation is the retention). L27 temperature scaling is a grid search (0.25 to 5.0 in steps of 0.05) on binary correctness, not a multi-class fit; the framework seeds and their expected assertions are hand-written (eight episodes); the judge reads the first digit of its reply as the score.

knowledge.title: M5-04.7 evaluation suites, environments, shadow, canary and release gate
knowledge.text: evals.suites: Suite(name in COMPONENTS triage, retrieval, memory, tool_selection, delegation, screening, output_checks, or risk_tier; cases); Case(id, run -> CaseResult(passed, failures, cost_usd, latency_ms, safety_violation), smoke flag); run(suites, tier smoke | full, k=3): smoke runs only smoke cases, risk_tier cases run k times, a raising case fails; SuiteReport(tier, k, results {suite: {case: [results]}}, seconds; over_budget smoke 90 s / full 45 min; pass_rate, risk_failures, safety_violations, all_runs). Environments: Cassette (replay by sha256 of method, URL, body; MissingRecording otherwise), Sandbox (allowed hosts only; notify() always raises), Twin (copied state + change log). ShadowTools(run_read, is_write): writes recorded as proposals, never run; divergence(shadow, production) over shared turn ids; canary(route, conversation, percent): only READ_ONLY_ROUTES (faq, status, documentation), sha256 bucket < percent. evals.gate.release_gate(report, thresholds, route_costs (candidate, previous, baseline), live (previous, candidate) csat / fcr / ces, changed_routes, shadow {route: divergence}, risk_routes) -> Verdict(passed, failures): full tier only; component pass rates >= thresholds (a missing suite fails); zero safety violations; k >= 3 and every risk episode passed every run; at least one risk episode; p95 latency <= 2500 ms (nearest rank), mean cost <= 0.04 USD; cost.budgets.release_gate per route; CSAT / FCR not lower, CES not higher; each changed non-read-only route needs to be in risk_routes and a shadow divergence <= 0.05.

L8 hazard scorer is a stub in tests/demo (Llama Guard needs a model pull). L9 SPEC FR-7 says OBO tokens last 24 h; code and UA-D9 say 15 min (doc fix). L10 a business day is counted as 24 h for significant-decision SLAs (no business calendar). L11 queue priority is Jev acuity then SLA deadline; contract tier does not affect it, and promotion to the senior queue keeps the original (breached) deadline. L12 the wait estimate uses a fixed 10-minute service time per specialist, not Erlang A or measured rates. L13 HL-D10's Jev categorisation of free-text feedback is not built: feedback is reason codes only and the edited draft text is not stored. L14 Cedar has no credential-reset action; the e2e reset is authorized as restart_cluster (a production change) on the instance's environment (policies/: add the action when the tool is real). L15 MA-D8's shared turn token budget (16,000 tokens, forced join at 90%) is not enforced: steps are the only ceiling in agents.topology (add with the briefs' token accounting). L16 'solo' means the only specialist dispatched in the turn (a dependent running alone after the lead does not count); SpecialistTools validates with the gate and then writes through the executor, two steps without a shared lock (the gate re-decides on current state; a change in between is caught by the read-back, not prevented). L17 ConversationReader is not registered as a tool and its characters are not charged to a shared turn budget (with L15). L18 specialist claims travel as a JSON list in a result's findings until agents.topology carries agents.contracts (W21); the merge's completed-action check is a phrase list, like the output checks' (B7). L19 PERF-01 (one reused psycopg connection per database in data.migrate.psql, for test speed) was dropped by the user on 2026-10-27: task rejected, src/data/migrate.py reverted to one docker exec psql per query; the reverted change is kept as a patch outside the repo. Tests stay slow; revisit in the sweep if speed matters. L20 admission uses fixed one-minute windows, not a continuous token bucket (a burst across a window boundary can reach twice the rate); the Upstash fallback is per process (v1 runs one worker; with several, the one-turn guarantee would not hold during an outage, and locks taken locally are not visible in Upstash after it recovers); tests use a fake Upstash REST server, not a real one. L21 RP-D9 autoscaling with pre-warmed minimums is infrastructure (Kubernetes) that v1 does not have (one VM); incidents and coalescing live in one process; the latency budgets are design limits, not yet measured p95 (no load test). L22 v1 backs up with daily pg_dump, not WAL archiving: RPO up to a day (not 5 minutes) and no point-in-time recovery, one VM (no multi-AZ); dumps rely on R2 encryption at rest (no client-side encryption; encrypted fields stay sealed under data keys); the drill row-count check is exact only when nothing writes during the dump (nightly). L23 tool calls are capped at three retries per call (and the per-system retry budget), not three retries per turn across all tools (RP-D13); a held request keeps its tool arguments in Temporal history, as saga steps do; the held-request probe interval is fixed (default 5 minutes), not driven by the breaker closing. L24 cache normalisation lowercases and strips punctuation (no lemmatisation); budgets are set by administrators in SQL; the price table is versioned in code, not a table; band() sums the month ledger on every call (fine at v1 volume). L25 tail sampling and scrubbing run in each process (no collector): a trace whose root runs in another process (a Temporal activity under a remote parent) is decided only when the buffer fills or on flush; Jaeger all-in-one has no delete API, so a user is erased from it only by the 7-day expiry (its spans carry only the subject hash); logs go to stdout (docker log rotation is the retention). L26 SLO burn rates are computed from turn records in process, not by a metrics backend; tripwire de-duplication lives in one process (restarts re-alert once); the failure taxonomy is the ADP list (rules for hard faults, six conversational categories). L27 temperature scaling is a grid search (0.25 to 5.0 in steps of 0.05) on binary correctness, not a multi-class fit; the framework seeds and their expected assertions are hand-written (eight episodes); the judge reads the first digit of its reply as the score. L28 the release gate trusts its caller for which routes changed, which the risk tier covered, and the per-suite thresholds; p95 is the nearest-rank percentile over the suite runs, not over live traffic.

knowledge.title: M5-05.7 mocked-model harness, invariants, injection set, contracts, checkpoints, load and chaos
knowledge.text:
tests/invariants/harness.py: ScriptedJev is the System One endpoint as an httpx MockTransport for the real JevClient (valid answers, or unknown option, confidence out of range, missing answer, wrong answer type, non-JSON body, HTTP 400 / 429 / 500, unreachable); all_valid discounts a 429 the client retried; engine(jev) is the real DecisionEngine over it; ScriptedModel is a complete(prompt) for llm_fallback (valid JSON, prose, missing field, wrong types, out of range, and with can_fail an outage). Everything is seeded by random.Random.
tests/invariants/test_invariants.py: properties over 300 seeds each: statechart transitions stay legal and every run stops at rest; an SOP is collected only after a confident Jev triage; diagnosis stops at four steps and at the third critique and never continues after a non-read-only tool; money at or above the threshold moves only after APPROVAL_GRANTED (personas random / persistent / critic drive the ReAct steps); delegation never exceeds six steps, two per specialist or three specialists, never reaches a tool off the role's allow-list, and always carries the turn's own context; with Jev undecided nobody is dispatched; a numeric disagreement (independently restated) always goes to a person and a reply is drafted at most once; a reply holding a credential (seven formats, seven wrappings) or twelve copied words of the system prompt is never delivered; the admission mutex allows one active turn per conversation under random thread interleavings. A coverage test checks the draws reach every stage and every Jev failure mode.
tests/invariants/test_injection_set.py: the fixed adversarial set (TQ-D3): direct override, Cyrillic and Greek homoglyphs, zero-width splits and fullwidth letters are blocked at screening; three benign look-alikes pass; Base64 smuggling passes screening (strict xfail, S6) but the refund it would steer to cannot run without a person; injections inside tool output are withheld; paraphrased exfiltration requests pass screening (L29) and every verbatim, upper-case, zero-width-spaced or credential leak is blocked at the output; obfuscated credentials are a strict xfail (S14).
tests/contracts/test_policy_lints.py: every table in migrations/ and every module SCHEMA (as imported) has ENABLE + FORCE row-level security and a policy (exception NO_RLS = knowledge_tombstones, S15); no DROP / RENAME / ALTER COLUMN TYPE / DROP TABLE (expand / contract); every Jev question constant (25 found across ten modules, incl. templates named *QUESTION and RELEVANT) has a known type, options where needed and no digits; every framework scenario one to eight has a test_scenario_<n>_ test.
tests/contracts/test_schema_contracts.py: snapshots/ pins 20 shared formats (envelope, thread state keys + SCHEMA_VERSION, Triage, Step, Brief, Result, Claim, Packet, Submission, IncidentDiagnosticPacket and their enums); a change fails with breaking vs additive changes listed; ThreadState cannot change without a SCHEMA_VERSION bump; regenerate with UPDATE_CONTRACTS=1.
tests/contracts/test_checkpoints.py + checkpoints/v1/: six states captured from the real graph (awaiting customer, awaiting approval x3, resolved, escalated); each loads into a fresh graph (update_state as_node="resume"), upgrades and resumes to its recorded outcome on a fixed clock; a rehearsal with SCHEMA_VERSION + 1 and a registered migration loads the whole library; a version with no migration goes to a person; the library must cover every version 1..SCHEMA_VERSION and every older version must have a migration. Capture new versions with UPDATE_CHECKPOINTS=1 (never rewrites an archived file).
tests/load/ac13.py: Sample, personas() (seed episodes weighted by P(stratum) / episodes in it), failures(samples) (lost status, first status p95 over 1 s, per route lost or slow finals, turns with a person excluded), frames(), measure(open_stream, post, route, text, think) as a client sees a turn. tests/load/test_api_load.py runs the real app under uvicorn on a free port (production poll / heartbeat) with a mocked agent: 30 customers get every event within one poll; 60 customers is a strict xfail (B12); the release locustfile runs in a subprocess against it. tests/load/locustfile.py: the VM release run (AC-13), reports SSE first_status and final:<route>, exits 1 on an AC-13 failure. tests/load/test_chaos.py: Jev down at every decision point fails safe (triage asks, guard no, tool none, delegation hands off, merge to a person, no incident answer); a case with Jev down never collects an SOP; Jev and the model both down is a strict xfail (B10); provider outages stay within the retry budget, in chain order, with the turn's count equal to the retries made; with every model down the degraded answer cites the knowledge base; tool latency spikes retry a read at most three times and open the breaker; a worker killed before triage, slot filling or the SOP resumes and runs the SOP exactly once; admission answers through a partition; the partition split-brain is a strict xfail (B11).
Mutation check: 26 mutants of the product code, 25 caught; the survivor (dropping the GitHub token pattern) is still blocked by the entropy rule. Load measurements: see register B12-B14.

knowledge.title: Open issues register (single source; update by superseding)
knowledge.text:
Consolidated 2026-10-25 from KNOWLEDGE-2114e3c6, 82aa3192, c5d19a99, 634b024b, 0bf6e556, 60b69bfa, 60b6dd3c, 630f3cc2, c60fdc50, b0d958bf, d72ef88b, fef4e96a, 97282376; v2 added M2-09.7 items (S9, B5, W9-W13, L10-L11); v3 added M2-10.7 items (B6, W14-W16, L12-L13); v4 added M2-11.7 items (B7, W17-W18, L14); v5 added M3-01.7 items (W19, L15); v6 added the M3-01.7 security review's out-of-scope items (S10, S11, W20, and a note on S3); v7 added M3-02.7 items (S12, W21, L16-L17); v8 added M3-03.7 items (W22, L18); v9 added PERF-01 items (B8, L19); v10 marked PERF-01 dropped (L19); v11 added M4-01.7 items (W23, L20) and updated L3; v12 added M4-02.7 items (W24, L21); v13 added M4-03.7 items (S13, W25, L22); v14 added M4-04.7 items (W26, L23); v15 added M4-05.7 items (W27, L24); v16 added M5-01.7 items (W28, L25) and updated W8; v17 added M5-02.7 items (W29, L26); v18 added M5-03.7 items (W30, L27); v19 added M5-04.7 items (W31, L28); v20 adds M5-05.7 items (S14-S15, B9-B15, W32, L29-L30). Plan (user, 2026-10-25): out-of-scope issues, critical ones too, go here instead of a replan; fix all in one sweep task added with a single plan reopen after the last task (M6-03.7).










SECURITY: S1 saga path uses ApprovalGate legacy mode: caller-supplied ctx.resource and ctx.roles, gate built without roles_of / tool_authz / resource_attrs (src/tools/sagas/activities.py). S2 Executor service-account Cedar check uses caller call.resource, not a tool->Cedar rule (src/tools/execution/__init__.py). S3 generic tools.execution.calls.call_tool / ToolActivities path runs tools without the approval gate (src/tools/execution/). Note for S3: agents.topology.executor_tool also calls Executor.run without the approval gate; it is safe only because a specialist registry refuses non-read-only tools, so M3-02.7 must route specialist writes through ApprovalGate (and S2: executor_tool sends no Cedar resource, so a service-account system denies by default). S4 no resource_attrs resolver: resource owner/tenant attributes still come from the caller (needs reviewed CRM read tools). S5 tool->Cedar rules live in gate config, not next to the tool in the registry (src/tools/registry/). S6 screening does not decode Base64; a Base64-only injection passes user-message screening (src/safety/screening/; Prompt Guard via Groq or a decode pass). S7 audit log is append-only but not hash-chained (src/tools/audit.py). S8 ticket workflow (M1-05) inputs/history not audited for sensitive data in Temporal (src/workflows/). S9 ApprovalGate.grant does not pass the request id to verify_approver, so the one-item binding of a staff sign-in (ID token nonce = request id) is enforced by hitl.approval.Desk.decide, not by a direct gate.grant call (src/tools/validation/approvals.py: pass request_id to the verifier).
