S10 the LangGraph Postgres checkpoint tables have no tenant row-level security and no integrity seal: someone with database write access could substitute a well-formed plan or state (agents.topology.checked_plan refuses malformed or inflated plans, not a valid substitute); theoretical while the checkpoint database is trusted (core.orchestrator.statechart.postgres_checkpointer: separate role / RLS, or an HMAC over the plan). S11 tools.execution.Executor.run writes no tool audit record (tools.audit is only on the saga path), so specialist tool calls through executor_tool are not audited (src/tools/execution). S12 a specialist's identity does not reach downstream systems or the audit log: on-behalf-of tokens carry act = the one agent identity (channels.identity.service._mint_obo, AGENT), and tool_audit_records has no actor_subrole column (MA-D9, MA-ADP-04 invariant 1); agents.contracts.actor(role) is recorded only as the approval request's handler.



 S13 the erasure workflow does not yet write the erasure log (deploy/backup/pgbackup.log_erasure) when an erasure completes (memory.lifecycle.inventory close / data.erasure): until it does, restoring a dump taken before an erasure brings that user back, and the drill has nothing to replay. OpenBao (the transit key that wraps every data key) is not backed up: losing it makes all encrypted fields unreadable. S14 the output checks match credentials on the raw text, so an invisible or spacing character inside one hides it: a key with a zero-width space or word joiner inside, or with its characters spaced out, is delivered (src/safety/output/checks.py: NFKC and strip format characters, collapse single-character spacing, before matching; strict xfail tests/invariants/test_injection_set.py). S15 knowledge_tombstones holds per-tenant rows (scope = the tenant id) with no row-level security: app_runtime can read every tenant's tombstoned document ids and reasons (src/knowledge/ingest/pipeline.py; listed in NO_RLS in tests/contracts/test_policy_lints.py, which fails once it is fixed).






BUGS: B1 output sanitiser strips <placeholder> text inside code fences ('--subnet-id <id>' -> '--subnet-id ') (src/safety/output/checks.py). B2 web/dev-server.js crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT when the API drops mid-stream (writeHead only if !headersSent, else destroy). B3 tests/deploy/test_backbone.py line 4 over 110 chars (lint). B4 app HTTPS on TLS-intercepting machines needs truststore / CA handling (only the demo has it). B5 ticket workflow waits 48 h for an approval decision (src/workflows/ticket.py approval_timeout_seconds) but HL-D9 / MAX_APPROVAL_TTL / hitl.queues cancel at 72 h. B6 hitl.queues.sweep promotes a claimed hand-off once its SLA passes (for a hand-off the SLA is the time to pick-up) and unassigns it: the conversation's specialist keeps ownership (handoffs row; the one-owner index stops a second take-over) but the item reappears in queue_senior and pages the lead; escalations also have no 'resolved' status for a finished hand-off (src/hitl/queues: skip claimed hand-offs in the promotion, add a resolved status set by hand_back). B7 the output checks only catch future promises ('we will refund', 'will be credited'); a past-tense success claim ('Your refund has been processed.') passes without a verified action (src/safety/output/checks.py PROMISES; strict xfail in tests/e2e/test_scenarios_actions.py flips when fixed). B9 the output checks' PEM private-key header pattern sits behind \b, which cannot match before '-----' after a space, a line break or punctuation, so that pattern never fires; a full key block is still blocked by the entropy rule on its body (src/safety/output/checks.py CREDENTIALS; strict xfail tests/invariants/test_invariants.py). B10 triage's llm_fallback catches only parse errors (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError): a provider outage (AllProvidersFailed, a connection error) escapes triage, so Jev and the fallback model both down crashes the turn instead of asking the customer (src/core/orchestrator/triage.py; strict xfail tests/load/test_chaos.py). B11 admission's local fallback cannot see a lock held in Upstash: during a partition a second turn on a busy conversation is admitted, even with one worker (worse than L20 says; src/reliability/admission: fail closed to BUSY for a conversation the shared store cannot confirm, or keep a local mirror of held locks; strict xfail tests/load/test_chaos.py). B12 CRITICAL channels.api streams events from a sync generator, which holds one of the server's 40 worker threads (anyio's default limiter) for the life of each open stream, and the sync POST handler needs the same pool. Measured by tests/load/test_api_load.py (mocked agent, compose Postgres): 5 and 30 concurrent customers are fine; at 60, 47 of 60 status events were lost, 58 final replies never arrived and the first status p50 was 7.2 s; at 100, first status p95 8.8 s and FAQ final p95 13.2 s. AC-13 cannot pass at release load (src/channels/api/app.py: an async stream with async psycopg or LISTEN / NOTIFY; strict xfail at 60 users). B13 the stream places its cursor when its generator first runs, not when the client connects: events published in between are never delivered (seen under B12's load; the web client connects the same way) (src/channels/api/app.py: take the cursor before returning the response, or return the event id with the POST for Last-Event-ID). B14 the stream polls the outbox once a second (create_app poll_seconds=1.0), which uses the whole 1 s first-status budget: first status p95 0.91 to 1.05 s at 5 to 30 customers with no agent load (poll every 0.2 s, or LISTEN / NOTIFY). B15 tests/evals/gate/test_gate.py (M5-04.7) and tests/hitl/gate/test_gate.py share a module name in test folders without __init__.py, so a single pytest run over the whole suite fails at collection (import file mismatch): CI runs python -m pytest -q and breaks; the batched local runs hid it (rename tests/evals/gate/test_gate.py to test_release_gate.py).










NOT YET B8 tests/tools/validation test_property_no_financial_write_at_or_above_the_threshold_runs_without_a_second_person failed once (2026-10-26) with psycopg AdminShutdown: its Postgres connection was terminated mid-test, most likely by a concurrent Postgres restart from another session; not reproduced since (545/545 green on 2026-10-27). The test and ApprovalGate hold their own connections and do not reconnect. The test also takes ~42 s, unchanged by PERF-01 (its time is not in data.migrate.psql): profile it in the sweep.









WIRED: W1 governance require_sign_off() not in the statechart; disclose() not in the API reply path (src/safety/governance/). W2 conversation memory not wired into dispatch / context assembler; summarizer prompt is injected, none written (src/memory/conversation/). W3 facts: activation scoring for the 15% profile slot, the resolution / 24 h idle write trigger, ALLOWED_TOOL_FIELDS is an example list (src/memory/facts/). W4 no CI lint that every tool field declares sensitivity (review() runs at registration). W5 a DENY does not yet feed the turn's circuit breaker (src/core/recovery/ + turn loop). W6 tool-output blobs (tool-output/<tenant>/<case>/) not in the erasure inventory and no TTL (src/memory/lifecycle/). W7 approval card delivery to the specialist console / event stream: expected in M2-10 (the card itself is hitl.approval.Desk.card). W8 observability.tracing.LangfuseEraser exists (M5-01.7) but is not yet a store in the erasure inventory (memory.lifecycle.inventory STORES / verify). W9 hitl.queues.Queues.sweep is a function: not yet run on a schedule (Temporal schedule or cron, per tenant). W10 alert (Slack / PagerDuty) and notify (customer inbox, UA-D2) are injected callbacks with no production implementation. W11 nothing emits escalation packets yet: confidence gate hand-offs, reflexion limit, user-requested human and approval-requiring actions must call Queues.escalate (turn loop / M2-10 handoff). W12 escalations / escalation_events (tokenized packet, customer id) not in the erasure inventory or retention (src/memory/lifecycle/). W13 MS-D18 post-wait check: an approval executed more than 1 h after staging does not re-read external state against the dry-run snapshot before running (tools.validation execute / sagas). Also: staff_directory has no admin or SCIM sync path (app_owner SQL only); specialists see PII tokens, vault reveal for authorized staff not wired (console). W14 the turn loop does not yet call hitl.handoff (wants_human -> request, mode / allowed before each turn and tool call), so co-serving and the cold hand-off are not enforced in the agent yet. W15 console sign-in is an in-process MockIdP (development): the console's OIDC redirect with a per-item nonce and its deployment (Hugging Face Spaces) are not built. W16 no customer API route for cancel(); the wait estimate is published once at request time, not refreshed as the queue moves. W17 the statechart waits for approval on amount only (execute_sop: parameters.amount >= approval_threshold); an SOP whose tool needs approval for another reason (high-risk write, unreviewed tool, Cedar approval_required) has no way into AWAITING_APPROVAL; the e2e test sets the threshold to 0 for it (src/core/orchestrator/statechart.py: take needs_approval from tools.validation's decision). W18 the turn loop has no correction detection for an action waiting for approval (the e2e test asks Jev a noul question, then Handoffs.cancel + APPROVAL_DENIED + a new episode), and no slot filler (scripted in the e2e tests). W19 agents.topology.coordinator is not yet called from the statechart's DELIBERATING stage, and a handoff plan (low lead confidence or Jev down) does not yet open an escalation in hitl.queues (turn loop wiring). W20 a specialist tool failure is reduced to its code for the model, and its detail is not written to an access-controlled, redacted diagnostic log (observability, M5). W21 agents.topology does not use agents.contracts yet: briefs and results are still dicts; its registry refuses every non-read-only tool, so SpecialistTools' solo low-risk writes are unreachable from the coordinator; for_turn needs solo (the plan's single assignment), the conversation id and the masked message; a specialist's ProposedAction is not yet routed by the coordinator to ApprovalGate.request + hitl.queues (src/agents/topology). W22 agents.merge is not wired into the coordinator's join: its human outcomes (NUMERIC_DISCREPANCY, EVIDENCE_AMBIGUITY, REDIRECT, UNVERIFIED_COMPLETION, JEV_UNAVAILABLE) do not yet open a hitl.queues escalation with a discrepancy card; a REDIRECT does not re-delegate to the missing specialist; the drafting model is not wired, and the merged reply does not yet pass the output checks and the confidence gate on its way out.

 W23 reliability.admission is not wired: channels.api POST /turns does not call admit() (409 body with active_turn_id, 429 with a Retry-After header), the turn loop does not call keep_alive / finish, AWAITING_APPROVAL does not call hold_for_approval and an approval decision or the 72 h cancellation (hitl.queues.sweep) does not release it, model and Jev completions do not call record_usage, KB_ONLY is not routed to degraded_answer, and UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL / TOKEN are not read into an Upstash store.
 W24 reliability.bursts is not wired: retrieval and tool reads do not go through SingleFlight; there is no admin API (with on-call authorization and audit) to declare or clear an incident; the turn loop does not ask incident_answer before triage; turns do not run on a Deadline (first status event, skipping reranking, the route fallbacks), and nothing classifies a turn as faq / diagnostic / multi-specialist.
 W25 backups are not installed on the VM: deploy/setup-vm.sh does not install the cron file, create /var/log/support-agent or set RESTORE_DSN_BASE; there is no warm standby (RP-D15: a kept standby_ copy would also need to join the erasure fan-out); Qdrant is not snapshotted (the index can be rebuilt from the raw snapshots in R2).
 W26 reliability.hold is not wired: the turn loop does not catch a holdable ToolFailure and call start_hold; no worker for the held-requests task queue is deployed; answer() is not the drafting model yet; the hand-over packet carries identity_tier unknown and the agent as handler.
 W27 cost.cache and cost.budgets are not wired: the turn loop does not look up the cache before generating or store eligible answers after; nothing provides the kb_version (a hash of the tenant index snapshot) or the customer product_version (identity has none); erase_document does not call AnswerCache.evict_document; model and Jev completions do not call Ledger.record; band() is not consulted (soft cap -> degraded_answer + SOFT_CAP_NOTICE); there is no admin-notification channel, tenant-admin report view, monthly reconcile job or invoice import; release_gate is not in CI (it needs cost per resolved conversation per route from the evaluation harness, M5).
 W28 tracing is not wired: services do not call observability.tracing.provider / json_logging at start-up, the turn loop, model router, Jev client and tools do not create spans with turn_attributes and gen_ai.* attributes or set support.escalated / agent.risk_tier, Temporal workers are not given temporalio.contrib.opentelemetry.TracingInterceptor (trace context across workflows), and the compose Jaeger runs in memory with no 7-day retention set (deploy/compose.yaml; Langfuse retention is a project setting).
 W29 observability.alerts is not wired: no metrics backend (Prometheus / Grafana Cloud) or alert channel (PagerDuty / Slack) is set up; nothing feeds burn_alerts with turn records or the tripwires with breaker states, OAuth token lifetimes, batch results, reranker fallbacks or the financial_writes ledger; TokenCounter is not fed by completions; classify() is not run over failed or escalated conversations, its results are not stored, and residuals have no human QA queue; observability.tracing does not tag kept spans with sampling.reason (deterministic / baseline), which estimated_cost needs.
 W30 evaluation data is not wired: eval_samples is not a store in the erasure inventory; there is no back-office route to set the evaluation opt-in, and no job that harvests opted-in production conversations; no judge model or key is configured (it must be another family than the agent: the agent runs Claude / Groq Llama / Gemini, so e.g. OpenAI or Mistral); the per-route labelled validation sets and the 200 human-labelled conversations for judge acceptance are not collected; nothing feeds retrieval_deficit with live reranker scores, re-asks, feedback and citation clicks.
 W31 the evaluation suites are not in CI: no GitHub Actions job runs the smoke tier per commit or the full tier nightly and before a release; the component suites are not yet populated with real cases for every component (the tests carry examples), and the framework seed episodes are not run through the agent; shadow mode and canary routing are not wired into the live runtime or the API; live CSAT, FCR and CES are not collected (feedback signals come in M6-01). W32 the release load test (tests/load/locustfile.py, AC-13) has not run on the VM (needs M5-06's deploy) and no release job runs it or gates on its exit code; chaos runs in process only (no staging cluster or Chaos Mesh, L21).
ACCEPTED LIMITS / DESIGN DEBT: L1 no pgvector (nearest facts in Python). L2 legal archive: no legal holds, no General Counsel dual sign-off, Postgres not S3 Object Lock; its tokens lose their values after erasure. L3 the Redis turn lock now exists (reliability.admission) but is not wired (W23), so the Postgres PK still sequences turns; no P2 alert for pin budget; so the 72 h cancel has no mutex to release. L4 fact TTL uses valid_from as last-confirmed; old versions of a live fact stay until the lineage expires (plain FK). L5 Temporal ticket history TTL via namespace retention. L6 'prod' -> 'production' synonyms refused (agent asks). L7 non-USD money actions denied until a trusted FX source exists (DECISION-bdad33ce). L8 hazard scorer is a stub in tests/demo (Llama Guard needs a model pull). L9 SPEC FR-7 says OBO tokens last 24 h; code and UA-D9 say 15 min (doc fix). L10 a business day is counted as 24 h for significant-decision SLAs (no business calendar). L11 queue priority is Jev acuity then SLA deadline; contract tier does not affect it, and promotion to the senior queue keeps the original (breached) deadline. L12 the wait estimate uses a fixed 10-minute service time per specialist, not Erlang A or measured rates. L13 HL-D10's Jev categorisation of free-text feedback is not built: feedback is reason codes only and the edited draft text is not stored. L14 Cedar has no credential-reset action; the e2e reset is authorized as restart_cluster (a production change) on the instance's environment (policies/: add the action when the tool is real). L15 MA-D8's shared turn token budget (16,000 tokens, forced join at 90%) is not enforced: steps are the only ceiling in agents.topology (add with the briefs' token accounting). L16 'solo' means the only specialist dispatched in the turn (a dependent running alone after the lead does not count); SpecialistTools validates with the gate and then writes through the executor, two steps without a shared lock (the gate re-decides on current state; a change in between is caught by the read-back, not prevented). L17 ConversationReader is not registered as a tool and its characters are not charged to a shared turn budget (with L15). L18 specialist claims travel as a JSON list in a result's findings until agents.topology carries agents.contracts (W21); the merge's completed-action check is a phrase list, like the output checks' (B7). L19 PERF-01 (one reused psycopg connection per database in data.migrate.psql, for test speed) was dropped by the user on 2026-10-27: task rejected, src/data/migrate.py reverted to one docker exec psql per query; the reverted change is kept as a patch outside the repo. Tests stay slow; revisit in the sweep if speed matters. L20 admission uses fixed one-minute windows, not a continuous token bucket (a burst across a window boundary can reach twice the rate); the Upstash fallback is per process (v1 runs one worker; with several, the one-turn guarantee would not hold during an outage, and locks taken locally are not visible in Upstash after it recovers); tests use a fake Upstash REST server, not a real one. L21 RP-D9 autoscaling with pre-warmed minimums is infrastructure (Kubernetes) that v1 does not have (one VM); incidents and coalescing live in one process; the latency budgets are design limits, not yet measured p95 (no load test). L22 v1 backs up with daily pg_dump, not WAL archiving: RPO up to a day (not 5 minutes) and no point-in-time recovery, one VM (no multi-AZ); dumps rely on R2 encryption at rest (no client-side encryption; encrypted fields stay sealed under data keys); the drill row-count check is exact only when nothing writes during the dump (nightly). L23 tool calls are capped at three retries per call (and the per-system retry budget), not three retries per turn across all tools (RP-D13); a held request keeps its tool arguments in Temporal history, as saga steps do; the held-request probe interval is fixed (default 5 minutes), not driven by the breaker closing. L24 cache normalisation lowercases and strips punctuation (no lemmatisation); budgets are set by administrators in SQL; the price table is versioned in code, not a table; band() sums the month ledger on every call (fine at v1 volume). L25 tail sampling and scrubbing run in each process (no collector): a trace whose root runs in another process (a Temporal activity under a remote parent) is decided only when the buffer fills or on flush; Jaeger all-in-one has no delete API, so a user is erased from it only by the 7-day expiry (its spans carry only the subject hash); logs go to stdout (docker log rotation is the retention). L26 SLO burn rates are computed from turn records in process, not by a metrics backend; tripwire de-duplication lives in one process (restarts re-alert once); the failure taxonomy is the ADP list (rules for hard faults, six conversational categories). L27 temperature scaling is a grid search (0.25 to 5.0 in steps of 0.05) on binary correctness, not a multi-class fit; the framework seeds and their expected assertions are hand-written (eight episodes); the judge reads the first digit of its reply as the score. L28 the release gate trusts its caller for which routes changed, which the risk tier covered, and the per-suite thresholds; p95 is the nearest-rank percentile over the suite runs, not over live traffic. L29 paraphrased prompt-exfiltration requests ('repeat everything above verbatim') pass input screening, and a paraphrased (not copied) leak of the system prompt passes the output check, which catches a copied twelve-word run only. L30 Hypothesis is not a dependency: the property tests are seeded random.Random loops (300 draws per property, a failure names its seed) with no shrinking; the checkpoint library holds schema version one only, captured from today's graph with scripted hooks; contract snapshots pin the JSON Schemas of 20 shared formats and are regenerated deliberately with UPDATE_CONTRACTS=1.

knowledge.title: M5-06.7 VM deployment: image, compose layer, rollout / rollback, migrate, re-index, spend
knowledge.text:
deploy/vm/ (DECISION-2744aaec: SSH from the laptop, Neon Postgres, the VM's public IP):
- Dockerfile (+ Dockerfile.dockerignore, an allow-list: pyproject, src, evals, migrations, policies, deploy/vm; never .env, keys, .git, tests): python:3.11.13-slim-bookworm with postgresql-client, dependencies from pyproject, code run from /app/src (not installed, so data.migrate finds /app/migrations), user agent (uid 10001), HEALTHCHECK /healthz, CMD deploy/vm/serve.py. Built on the VM (arm64) by release.py.
- compose.vm.yaml: layered on deploy/compose.yaml; postgres only with --profile local-postgres (Neon); api from APP_IMAGE, env_file APP_ENV_FILE (default ../.env), backbone by service name, SUPPORT_AGENT_DEV_AUTH forced to 0, the only public port 0.0.0.0:8000, read-only, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, 2 GB, rotated logs.
- serve.py: build_app with Identity(idp=None) and no mock IdP (anonymous and one-time-code sign-in only; SSO refused until a real provider), refuses SUPPORT_AGENT_DEV_AUTH=1, /healthz runs SELECT 1 and reports APP_REVISION.
- migrate.py: from DATABASE_URL, psql to the direct endpoint (strips -pooler); creates the five application roles, the vault and key-store databases (VAULT_DATABASE / KEYS_DATABASE), applies migrations/main, vault, keys and every module SCHEMA (17 modules incl. evals.datasets) in rounds until none is pending (cross-module references), idempotent.
- release.py (host python3 3.9, stdlib only): check / rollout REF / rollback / status / attest-spend-limit USD. Rollout: preflight, detached checkout, docker build tagged support-agent-app:<commit12>, migrate in the new image, (--maintenance: reindex), compose up api, /healthz within 90 s, record in ~/.support-agent/releases.json, keep the live and previous images. Build or migration failure: the live release untouched, checkout restored. Unhealthy: the previous image put back (none: the api stopped). Rollback: the previous live release, no schema change (expand-only). Preflight refuses: uncommitted changes, MONTHLY_SPEND_CAP_USD missing or above 10, SUPPORT_AGENT_DEV_AUTH=1, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY without an attested console limit, TYPESAFE_API_KEY without a pinned Jev (unless --allow-unpinned jev, recorded), an alias Jev or untagged embedding, a changed embedding model without --maintenance, workflows running on changed workflow code (or Temporal unlistable), port 8000 held outside compose, under 3 GB free.
- models.json: tiers by alias (groq llama-3.1-8b-instant, gemini-flash-latest, claude-opus-5-5 at 4 / 20 USD per million tokens), embedding ollama nomic-embed-text:v1.5 (768), screening llama-guard3:1b, Jev null (to be pinned), monthly_cap_usd 10.
- reindex.py: in place (DL-D11): embed every chunk first (a failing or wrong-size model leaves the index untouched), then drop and rebuild each knowledge collection with Index.ensure and the same payloads; only public_knowledge_v1 and tenant_*_private_v1 collections.
- spend.py: the month's usage_ledger across tenants priced with models.json; exit 1 at or over the cap or with an unpriced model.
- setup-ol9.sh: Oracle Linux 9 (dnf Docker CE, firewalld 8000/tcp, SELinux enforcing, .env 600), backbone up, pinned Ollama models pulled, first rollout.
tests/deploy/vm/: test_release.py (30: a fake VM answering git / docker / ss / df; every preflight refusal, failure path, rollback, 3.9 / stdlib check, the real Temporal CLI listing), test_vm_image.py (11: the image built here migrates an empty database completely from inside the container and serves read-only: anonymous sign-in and a turn, /healthz, no mock SSO or header sign-in, no secrets in the image), test_vm_tools.py (17: re-index on in-memory Qdrant, spend on a real ledger, migration helpers, serve in process).
VM state 2026-10-31 (read-only probes): Oracle Linux 9.8 aarch64, 4 OCPU, 22 GiB, 9.6 GB free of 30 GB, Docker 29.9.2, SELinux enforcing, firewalld with 8000/tcp; backbone containers up on 127.0.0.1; the API is the hand-started dev server from .venv (Python 3.11) on 0.0.0.0:8000 against Neon (pooled), main at a75b5ca with uncommitted helper copies; Neon has 12 tables, 5 migrations, 1 tenant, app_owner / app_runtime roles, agent_vault and agent_keys databases. No app image exists yet. Changes made: the VM's .env set to 600; the laptop's ssh key excluded in .git/info/exclude.

knowledge.title: Open issues register (single source; update by superseding)
knowledge.text:
Consolidated 2026-10-25 from KNOWLEDGE-2114e3c6, 82aa3192, c5d19a99, 634b024b, 0bf6e556, 60b69bfa, 60b6dd3c, 630f3cc2, c60fdc50, b0d958bf, d72ef88b, fef4e96a, 97282376; v2 added M2-09.7 items (S9, B5, W9-W13, L10-L11); v3 added M2-10.7 items (B6, W14-W16, L12-L13); v4 added M2-11.7 items (B7, W17-W18, L14); v5 added M3-01.7 items (W19, L15); v6 added the M3-01.7 security review's out-of-scope items (S10, S11, W20, and a note on S3); v7 added M3-02.7 items (S12, W21, L16-L17); v8 added M3-03.7 items (W22, L18); v9 added PERF-01 items (B8, L19); v10 marked PERF-01 dropped (L19); v11 added M4-01.7 items (W23, L20) and updated L3; v12 added M4-02.7 items (W24, L21); v13 added M4-03.7 items (S13, W25, L22); v14 added M4-04.7 items (W26, L23); v15 added M4-05.7 items (W27, L24); v16 added M5-01.7 items (W28, L25) and updated W8; v17 added M5-02.7 items (W29, L26); v18 added M5-03.7 items (W30, L27); v19 added M5-04.7 items (W31, L28); v20 added M5-05.7 items (S14-S15, B9-B15, W32, L29-L30); v21 adds M5-06.7 items (S16-S17, B16-B17, W33-W37, L31-L32). Plan (user, 2026-10-25): out-of-scope issues, critical ones too, go here instead of a replan; fix all in one sweep task added with a single plan reopen after the last task (M6-03.7).










SECURITY: S1 saga path uses ApprovalGate legacy mode: caller-supplied ctx.resource and ctx.roles, gate built without roles_of / tool_authz / resource_attrs (src/tools/sagas/activities.py). S2 Executor service-account Cedar check uses caller call.resource, not a tool->Cedar rule (src/tools/execution/__init__.py). S3 generic tools.execution.calls.call_tool / ToolActivities path runs tools without the approval gate (src/tools/execution/). Note for S3: agents.topology.executor_tool also calls Executor.run without the approval gate; it is safe only because a specialist registry refuses non-read-only tools, so M3-02.7 must route specialist writes through ApprovalGate (and S2: executor_tool sends no Cedar resource, so a service-account system denies by default). S4 no resource_attrs resolver: resource owner/tenant attributes still come from the caller (needs reviewed CRM read tools). S5 tool->Cedar rules live in gate config, not next to the tool in the registry (src/tools/registry/). S6 screening does not decode Base64; a Base64-only injection passes user-message screening (src/safety/screening/; Prompt Guard via Groq or a decode pass). S7 audit log is append-only but not hash-chained (src/tools/audit.py). S8 ticket workflow (M1-05) inputs/history not audited for sensitive data in Temporal (src/workflows/). S9 ApprovalGate.grant does not pass the request id to verify_approver, so the one-item binding of a staff sign-in (ID token nonce = request id) is enforced by hitl.approval.Desk.decide, not by a direct gate.grant call (src/tools/validation/approvals.py: pass request_id to the verifier). S10 the LangGraph Postgres checkpoint tables have no tenant row-level security and no integrity seal: someone with database write access could substitute a well-formed plan or state (agents.topology.checked_plan refuses malformed or inflated plans, not a valid substitute); theoretical while the checkpoint database is trusted (core.orchestrator.statechart.postgres_checkpointer: separate role / RLS, or an HMAC over the plan). S11 tools.execution.Executor.run writes no tool audit record (tools.audit is only on the saga path), so specialist tool calls through executor_tool are not audited (src/tools/execution). S12 a specialist's identity does not reach downstream systems or the audit log: on-behalf-of tokens carry act = the one agent identity (channels.identity.service._mint_obo, AGENT), and tool_audit_records has no actor_subrole column (MA-D9, MA-ADP-04 invariant 1); agents.contracts.actor(role) is recorded only as the approval request's handler.



 S13 the erasure workflow does not yet write the erasure log (deploy/backup/pgbackup.log_erasure) when an erasure completes (memory.lifecycle.inventory close / data.erasure): until it does, restoring a dump taken before an erasure brings that user back, and the drill has nothing to replay. OpenBao (the transit key that wraps every data key) is not backed up: losing it makes all encrypted fields unreadable. S14 the output checks match credentials on the raw text, so an invisible or spacing character inside one hides it: a key with a zero-width space or word joiner inside, or with its characters spaced out, is delivered (src/safety/output/checks.py: NFKC and strip format characters, collapse single-character spacing, before matching; strict xfail tests/invariants/test_injection_set.py). S15 knowledge_tombstones holds per-tenant rows (scope = the tenant id) with no row-level security: app_runtime can read every tenant's tombstoned document ids and reasons (src/knowledge/ingest/pipeline.py; listed in NO_RLS in tests/contracts/test_policy_lints.py, which fails once it is fixed). S16 the VM's current API is the hand-started development server (python -m channels.identity serve, from .venv via deploy/start-api.sh) with its mock SSO route POST /v1/identity/mock-idp open on the public IP: anyone can mint a sign-in token for any tenant and user, MFA included (checked 2026-10-31: the route answers 422 to an empty body). Left running by the user's choice until the first deploy/vm rollout, whose deploy/vm/serve.py has no mock route and refuses header sign-in. S17 the deployed DATABASE_URL user (neondb_owner) has BYPASSRLS; tenant isolation holds only on code paths that SET LOCAL ROLE app_runtime, as with the local superuser (use a non-bypass login role for the app, keeping the owner for migrations).






BUGS: B1 output sanitiser strips <placeholder> text inside code fences ('--subnet-id <id>' -> '--subnet-id ') (src/safety/output/checks.py). B2 web/dev-server.js crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT when the API drops mid-stream (writeHead only if !headersSent, else destroy). B3 tests/deploy/test_backbone.py line 4 over 110 chars (lint). B4 app HTTPS on TLS-intercepting machines needs truststore / CA handling (only the demo has it). B5 ticket workflow waits 48 h for an approval decision (src/workflows/ticket.py approval_timeout_seconds) but HL-D9 / MAX_APPROVAL_TTL / hitl.queues cancel at 72 h. B6 hitl.queues.sweep promotes a claimed hand-off once its SLA passes (for a hand-off the SLA is the time to pick-up) and unassigns it: the conversation's specialist keeps ownership (handoffs row; the one-owner index stops a second take-over) but the item reappears in queue_senior and pages the lead; escalations also have no 'resolved' status for a finished hand-off (src/hitl/queues: skip claimed hand-offs in the promotion, add a resolved status set by hand_back). B7 the output checks only catch future promises ('we will refund', 'will be credited'); a past-tense success claim ('Your refund has been processed.') passes without a verified action (src/safety/output/checks.py PROMISES; strict xfail in tests/e2e/test_scenarios_actions.py flips when fixed). B9 the output checks' PEM private-key header pattern sits behind \b, which cannot match before '-----' after a space, a line break or punctuation, so that pattern never fires; a full key block is still blocked by the entropy rule on its body (src/safety/output/checks.py CREDENTIALS; strict xfail tests/invariants/test_invariants.py). B10 triage's llm_fallback catches only parse errors (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError): a provider outage (AllProvidersFailed, a connection error) escapes triage, so Jev and the fallback model both down crashes the turn instead of asking the customer (src/core/orchestrator/triage.py; strict xfail tests/load/test_chaos.py). B11 admission's local fallback cannot see a lock held in Upstash: during a partition a second turn on a busy conversation is admitted, even with one worker (worse than L20 says; src/reliability/admission: fail closed to BUSY for a conversation the shared store cannot confirm, or keep a local mirror of held locks; strict xfail tests/load/test_chaos.py). B12 CRITICAL channels.api streams events from a sync generator, which holds one of the server's 40 worker threads (anyio's default limiter) for the life of each open stream, and the sync POST handler needs the same pool. Measured by tests/load/test_api_load.py (mocked agent, compose Postgres): 5 and 30 concurrent customers are fine; at 60, 47 of 60 status events were lost, 58 final replies never arrived and the first status p50 was 7.2 s; at 100, first status p95 8.8 s and FAQ final p95 13.2 s. AC-13 cannot pass at release load (src/channels/api/app.py: an async stream with async psycopg or LISTEN / NOTIFY; strict xfail at 60 users). B13 the stream places its cursor when its generator first runs, not when the client connects: events published in between are never delivered (seen under B12's load; the web client connects the same way) (src/channels/api/app.py: take the cursor before returning the response, or return the event id with the POST for Last-Event-ID). B14 the stream polls the outbox once a second (create_app poll_seconds=1.0), which uses the whole 1 s first-status budget: first status p95 0.91 to 1.05 s at 5 to 30 customers with no agent load (poll every 0.2 s, or LISTEN / NOTIFY). B15 tests/evals/gate/test_gate.py (M5-04.7) and tests/hitl/gate/test_gate.py share a module name in test folders without __init__.py, so a single pytest run over the whole suite fails at collection (import file mismatch): CI runs python -m pytest -q and breaks; the batched local runs hid it (rename tests/evals/gate/test_gate.py to test_release_gate.py). B16 scripts/neon_role_bootstrap.sql is invalid SQL (its DO block lacks the $$ delimiters and the role names their quotes); the working copy is in scripts/run_neon_migrate.py and deploy/vm/migrate.py. B17 deploy/setup-vm.sh assumes Ubuntu (apt-get) and the VM is Oracle Linux 9; deploy/vm/setup-ol9.sh is the one to use.










NOT YET B8 tests/tools/validation test_property_no_financial_write_at_or_above_the_threshold_runs_without_a_second_person failed once (2026-10-26) with psycopg AdminShutdown: its Postgres connection was terminated mid-test, most likely by a concurrent Postgres restart from another session; not reproduced since (545/545 green on 2026-10-27). The test and ApprovalGate hold their own connections and do not reconnect. The test also takes ~42 s, unchanged by PERF-01 (its time is not in data.migrate.psql): profile it in the sweep.









WIRED: W1 governance require_sign_off() not in the statechart; disclose() not in the API reply path (src/safety/governance/). W2 conversation memory not wired into dispatch / context assembler; summarizer prompt is injected, none written (src/memory/conversation/). W3 facts: activation scoring for the 15% profile slot, the resolution / 24 h idle write trigger, ALLOWED_TOOL_FIELDS is an example list (src/memory/facts/). W4 no CI lint that every tool field declares sensitivity (review() runs at registration). W5 a DENY does not yet feed the turn's circuit breaker (src/core/recovery/ + turn loop). W6 tool-output blobs (tool-output/<tenant>/<case>/) not in the erasure inventory and no TTL (src/memory/lifecycle/). W7 approval card delivery to the specialist console / event stream: expected in M2-10 (the card itself is hitl.approval.Desk.card). W8 observability.tracing.LangfuseEraser exists (M5-01.7) but is not yet a store in the erasure inventory (memory.lifecycle.inventory STORES / verify). W9 hitl.queues.Queues.sweep is a function: not yet run on a schedule (Temporal schedule or cron, per tenant). W10 alert (Slack / PagerDuty) and notify (customer inbox, UA-D2) are injected callbacks with no production implementation. W11 nothing emits escalation packets yet: confidence gate hand-offs, reflexion limit, user-requested human and approval-requiring actions must call Queues.escalate (turn loop / M2-10 handoff). W12 escalations / escalation_events (tokenized packet, customer id) not in the erasure inventory or retention (src/memory/lifecycle/). W13 MS-D18 post-wait check: an approval executed more than 1 h after staging does not re-read external state against the dry-run snapshot before running (tools.validation execute / sagas). Also: staff_directory has no admin or SCIM sync path (app_owner SQL only); specialists see PII tokens, vault reveal for authorized staff not wired (console). W14 the turn loop does not yet call hitl.handoff (wants_human -> request, mode / allowed before each turn and tool call), so co-serving and the cold hand-off are not enforced in the agent yet. W15 console sign-in is an in-process MockIdP (development): the console's OIDC redirect with a per-item nonce and its deployment (Hugging Face Spaces) are not built. W16 no customer API route for cancel(); the wait estimate is published once at request time, not refreshed as the queue moves. W17 the statechart waits for approval on amount only (execute_sop: parameters.amount >= approval_threshold); an SOP whose tool needs approval for another reason (high-risk write, unreviewed tool, Cedar approval_required) has no way into AWAITING_APPROVAL; the e2e test sets the threshold to 0 for it (src/core/orchestrator/statechart.py: take needs_approval from tools.validation's decision). W18 the turn loop has no correction detection for an action waiting for approval (the e2e test asks Jev a noul question, then Handoffs.cancel + APPROVAL_DENIED + a new episode), and no slot filler (scripted in the e2e tests). W19 agents.topology.coordinator is not yet called from the statechart's DELIBERATING stage, and a handoff plan (low lead confidence or Jev down) does not yet open an escalation in hitl.queues (turn loop wiring). W20 a specialist tool failure is reduced to its code for the model, and its detail is not written to an access-controlled, redacted diagnostic log (observability, M5). W21 agents.topology does not use agents.contracts yet: briefs and results are still dicts; its registry refuses every non-read-only tool, so SpecialistTools' solo low-risk writes are unreachable from the coordinator; for_turn needs solo (the plan's single assignment), the conversation id and the masked message; a specialist's ProposedAction is not yet routed by the coordinator to ApprovalGate.request + hitl.queues (src/agents/topology). W22 agents.merge is not wired into the coordinator's join: its human outcomes (NUMERIC_DISCREPANCY, EVIDENCE_AMBIGUITY, REDIRECT, UNVERIFIED_COMPLETION, JEV_UNAVAILABLE) do not yet open a hitl.queues escalation with a discrepancy card; a REDIRECT does not re-delegate to the missing specialist; the drafting model is not wired, and the merged reply does not yet pass the output checks and the confidence gate on its way out.

 W23 reliability.admission is not wired: channels.api POST /turns does not call admit() (409 body with active_turn_id, 429 with a Retry-After header), the turn loop does not call keep_alive / finish, AWAITING_APPROVAL does not call hold_for_approval and an approval decision or the 72 h cancellation (hitl.queues.sweep) does not release it, model and Jev completions do not call record_usage, KB_ONLY is not routed to degraded_answer, and UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL / TOKEN are not read into an Upstash store.
 W24 reliability.bursts is not wired: retrieval and tool reads do not go through SingleFlight; there is no admin API (with on-call authorization and audit) to declare or clear an incident; the turn loop does not ask incident_answer before triage; turns do not run on a Deadline (first status event, skipping reranking, the route fallbacks), and nothing classifies a turn as faq / diagnostic / multi-specialist.
 W25 backups are not installed on the VM: deploy/setup-vm.sh does not install the cron file, create /var/log/support-agent or set RESTORE_DSN_BASE; there is no warm standby (RP-D15: a kept standby_ copy would also need to join the erasure fan-out); Qdrant is not snapshotted (the index can be rebuilt from the raw snapshots in R2).
 W26 reliability.hold is not wired: the turn loop does not catch a holdable ToolFailure and call start_hold; no worker for the held-requests task queue is deployed; answer() is not the drafting model yet; the hand-over packet carries identity_tier unknown and the agent as handler.
 W27 cost.cache and cost.budgets are not wired: the turn loop does not look up the cache before generating or store eligible answers after; nothing provides the kb_version (a hash of the tenant index snapshot) or the customer product_version (identity has none); erase_document does not call AnswerCache.evict_document; model and Jev completions do not call Ledger.record; band() is not consulted (soft cap -> degraded_answer + SOFT_CAP_NOTICE); there is no admin-notification channel, tenant-admin report view, monthly reconcile job or invoice import; release_gate is not in CI (it needs cost per resolved conversation per route from the evaluation harness, M5).
 W28 tracing is not wired: services do not call observability.tracing.provider / json_logging at start-up, the turn loop, model router, Jev client and tools do not create spans with turn_attributes and gen_ai.* attributes or set support.escalated / agent.risk_tier, Temporal workers are not given temporalio.contrib.opentelemetry.TracingInterceptor (trace context across workflows), and the compose Jaeger runs in memory with no 7-day retention set (deploy/compose.yaml; Langfuse retention is a project setting).
 W29 observability.alerts is not wired: no metrics backend (Prometheus / Grafana Cloud) or alert channel (PagerDuty / Slack) is set up; nothing feeds burn_alerts with turn records or the tripwires with breaker states, OAuth token lifetimes, batch results, reranker fallbacks or the financial_writes ledger; TokenCounter is not fed by completions; classify() is not run over failed or escalated conversations, its results are not stored, and residuals have no human QA queue; observability.tracing does not tag kept spans with sampling.reason (deterministic / baseline), which estimated_cost needs.
 W30 evaluation data is not wired: eval_samples is not a store in the erasure inventory; there is no back-office route to set the evaluation opt-in, and no job that harvests opted-in production conversations; no judge model or key is configured (it must be another family than the agent: the agent runs Claude / Groq Llama / Gemini, so e.g. OpenAI or Mistral); the per-route labelled validation sets and the 200 human-labelled conversations for judge acceptance are not collected; nothing feeds retrieval_deficit with live reranker scores, re-asks, feedback and citation clicks.
 W31 the evaluation suites are not in CI: no GitHub Actions job runs the smoke tier per commit or the full tier nightly and before a release; the component suites are not yet populated with real cases for every component (the tests carry examples), and the framework seed episodes are not run through the agent; shadow mode and canary routing are not wired into the live runtime or the API; live CSAT, FCR and CES are not collected (feedback signals come in M6-01). W32 the release load test (tests/load/locustfile.py, AC-13) has not run on the VM (needs M5-06's deploy) and no release job runs it or gates on its exit code; chaos runs in process only (no staging cluster or Chaos Mesh, L21). W33 no workflow supports Continue-As-New (DL-D6): deploy/vm/release.py only refuses to swap while workflows run on code the release changes; the workflows themselves (TicketWorkflow, SagaWorkflow, HeldRequestWorkflow, ErasureWorkflow) need a drain of pending signals and workflow.continue_as_new at a release boundary. W34 no worker process: each Temporal worker needs injected activities and nothing composes them, so the VM runs the api only (no worker service in deploy/vm/compose.vm.yaml) and turns are accepted but nothing runs them (create_app's no_orchestrator). W35 the model pins in deploy/vm/models.json are not read by the code: JevClient defaults to jev-latest, there is no embedding client in src (deploy/vm/reindex.py takes an Ollama embedder), and the tier models are not configured anywhere else; the Jev version is not pinned yet (null until the user supplies it). W36 OpenBao runs in dev mode (secrets in memory): the R2 credentials the backup cron reads from it vanish on every restart, and the backup cron is not installed on the VM (W25); its paths assume /opt/support-agent. W37 the VM checkout (~/Enterprise-Support-Agent, main at a75b5ca) carries uncommitted copies of the deploy helpers since committed as 48f0f85, so a rollout's preflight refuses until it is reset to a commit; deploy/vm is not on the VM until it is pushed.
ACCEPTED LIMITS / DESIGN DEBT: L1 no pgvector (nearest facts in Python). L2 legal archive: no legal holds, no General Counsel dual sign-off, Postgres not S3 Object Lock; its tokens lose their values after erasure. L3 the Redis turn lock now exists (reliability.admission) but is not wired (W23), so the Postgres PK still sequences turns; no P2 alert for pin budget; so the 72 h cancel has no mutex to release. L4 fact TTL uses valid_from as last-confirmed; old versions of a live fact stay until the lineage expires (plain FK). L5 Temporal ticket history TTL via namespace retention. L6 'prod' -> 'production' synonyms refused (agent asks). L7 non-USD money actions denied until a trusted FX source exists (DECISION-bdad33ce). L8 hazard scorer is a stub in tests/demo (Llama Guard needs a model pull). L9 SPEC FR-7 says OBO tokens last 24 h; code and UA-D9 say 15 min (doc fix). L10 a business day is counted as 24 h for significant-decision SLAs (no business calendar). L11 queue priority is Jev acuity then SLA deadline; contract tier does not affect it, and promotion to the senior queue keeps the original (breached) deadline. L12 the wait estimate uses a fixed 10-minute service time per specialist, not Erlang A or measured rates. L13 HL-D10's Jev categorisation of free-text feedback is not built: feedback is reason codes only and the edited draft text is not stored. L14 Cedar has no credential-reset action; the e2e reset is authorized as restart_cluster (a production change) on the instance's environment (policies/: add the action when the tool is real). L15 MA-D8's shared turn token budget (16,000 tokens, forced join at 90%) is not enforced: steps are the only ceiling in agents.topology (add with the briefs' token accounting). L16 'solo' means the only specialist dispatched in the turn (a dependent running alone after the lead does not count); SpecialistTools validates with the gate and then writes through the executor, two steps without a shared lock (the gate re-decides on current state; a change in between is caught by the read-back, not prevented). L17 ConversationReader is not registered as a tool and its characters are not charged to a shared turn budget (with L15). L18 specialist claims travel as a JSON list in a result's findings until agents.topology carries agents.contracts (W21); the merge's completed-action check is a phrase list, like the output checks' (B7). L19 PERF-01 (one reused psycopg connection per database in data.migrate.psql, for test speed) was dropped by the user on 2026-10-27: task rejected, src/data/migrate.py reverted to one docker exec psql per query; the reverted change is kept as a patch outside the repo. Tests stay slow; revisit in the sweep if speed matters. L20 admission uses fixed one-minute windows, not a continuous token bucket (a burst across a window boundary can reach twice the rate); the Upstash fallback is per process (v1 runs one worker; with several, the one-turn guarantee would not hold during an outage, and locks taken locally are not visible in Upstash after it recovers); tests use a fake Upstash REST server, not a real one. L21 RP-D9 autoscaling with pre-warmed minimums is infrastructure (Kubernetes) that v1 does not have (one VM); incidents and coalescing live in one process; the latency budgets are design limits, not yet measured p95 (no load test). L22 v1 backs up with daily pg_dump, not WAL archiving: RPO up to a day (not 5 minutes) and no point-in-time recovery, one VM (no multi-AZ); dumps rely on R2 encryption at rest (no client-side encryption; encrypted fields stay sealed under data keys); the drill row-count check is exact only when nothing writes during the dump (nightly). L23 tool calls are capped at three retries per call (and the per-system retry budget), not three retries per turn across all tools (RP-D13); a held request keeps its tool arguments in Temporal history, as saga steps do; the held-request probe interval is fixed (default 5 minutes), not driven by the breaker closing. L24 cache normalisation lowercases and strips punctuation (no lemmatisation); budgets are set by administrators in SQL; the price table is versioned in code, not a table; band() sums the month ledger on every call (fine at v1 volume). L25 tail sampling and scrubbing run in each process (no collector): a trace whose root runs in another process (a Temporal activity under a remote parent) is decided only when the buffer fills or on flush; Jaeger all-in-one has no delete API, so a user is erased from it only by the 7-day expiry (its spans carry only the subject hash); logs go to stdout (docker log rotation is the retention). L26 SLO burn rates are computed from turn records in process, not by a metrics backend; tripwire de-duplication lives in one process (restarts re-alert once); the failure taxonomy is the ADP list (rules for hard faults, six conversational categories). L27 temperature scaling is a grid search (0.25 to 5.0 in steps of 0.05) on binary correctness, not a multi-class fit; the framework seeds and their expected assertions are hand-written (eight episodes); the judge reads the first digit of its reply as the score. L28 the release gate trusts its caller for which routes changed, which the risk tier covered, and the per-suite thresholds; p95 is the nearest-rank percentile over the suite runs, not over live traffic. L29 paraphrased prompt-exfiltration requests ('repeat everything above verbatim') pass input screening, and a paraphrased (not copied) leak of the system prompt passes the output check, which catches a copied twelve-word run only. L30 Hypothesis is not a dependency: the property tests are seeded random.Random loops (300 draws per property, a failure names its seed) with no shrinking; the checkpoint library holds schema version one only, captured from today's graph with scripted hooks; contract snapshots pin the JSON Schemas of 20 shared formats and are regenerated deliberately with UPDATE_CONTRACTS=1. L31 the API is served over plain HTTP on the VM's public IP (DECISION-2744aaec): the HTTPS web widget on Vercel cannot call it (mixed content); the API, console and load test work; HTTPS needs a Cloudflare tunnel or a domain. L32 the app connects through Neon's pooled (PgBouncer, transaction mode) endpoint; migrations go to the direct endpoint; sessions survive only within a transaction (SET LOCAL is fine, session SET ROLE is not), and one-time codes go to the container log (no mail sender); the session signing key is generated at start, so a restart signs everyone out.

knowledge.title: M6-01.7 feedback signals, Jev triage, failure taxonomy and weekly review
knowledge.text: improvement.feedback.taxonomy: VERSION 2026-10-31.1; TREE of Node(id subsystem.failure, Jev-safe description, quadrant KK/KU/UK/UU, tier 4/2/1 with weights 100/10/1, postmortem flag on tier-4 nodes tools.wrong_target, tools.unapproved_financial_write, safety.jailbreak, safety.pii_disclosure, safety.authorization_escape) plus unclassified_anomaly; FROM_ANALYZER (observability.alerts.Failure), FROM_DRAFT (hitl.handoff.DraftFailure), FROM_REJECTION (hitl.approval.RejectReason) map every existing code onto it; node(code). improvement.feedback: schema improvement_0001_feedback.sql, table feedback_events (append-only for app_runtime: SELECT, INSERT, DELETE for erasure; RLS forced; user by subject hash; tokenized comments; taxonomy version per row). Feedback(connect, tokenizer, engine, page): thumbs, survey (CES 1-5, 1 effortless, optional comment tokenized and refused if PII is left, triaged, paged at s >= 0.80), reason_code (source rejection for actions stopped before they ran), implicit (reask, reopen, abandon), events(window), erase. triage(engine, Masked): one Jev request, choice over the tree (below 0.70 or invalid -> unclassified, severity kept) and a five-level score s = level / 4; Jev down -> unclassified, severity None. similarity / reasked (>= 0.85, lexical), reopened (within 7 days of resolution), abandoned. weekly_review(events, owners): clusters ranked by volume x weight, top 3 owned by their subsystem's owner (owners_missing listed), postmortems for postmortem nodes except rejections, high_severity, needs_person (comments with unknown severity), unclassified count. live_metrics(events, conversations, resolved): csat (thumbs-up share), ces (mean), fcr (1 - reopen rate), reask / abandonment / reopen rates, the keys evals.gate compares. Tests: 21; mutation 6 of 6 caught.

knowledge.title: Open issues register (single source; update by superseding)
knowledge.text:
Consolidated 2026-10-25 from KNOWLEDGE-2114e3c6, 82aa3192, c5d19a99, 634b024b, 0bf6e556, 60b69bfa, 60b6dd3c, 630f3cc2, c60fdc50, b0d958bf, d72ef88b, fef4e96a, 97282376; v2 added M2-09.7 items (S9, B5, W9-W13, L10-L11); v3 added M2-10.7 items (B6, W14-W16, L12-L13); v4 added M2-11.7 items (B7, W17-W18, L14); v5 added M3-01.7 items (W19, L15); v6 added the M3-01.7 security review's out-of-scope items (S10, S11, W20, and a note on S3); v7 added M3-02.7 items (S12, W21, L16-L17); v8 added M3-03.7 items (W22, L18); v9 added PERF-01 items (B8, L19); v10 marked PERF-01 dropped (L19); v11 added M4-01.7 items (W23, L20) and updated L3; v12 added M4-02.7 items (W24, L21); v13 added M4-03.7 items (S13, W25, L22); v14 added M4-04.7 items (W26, L23); v15 added M4-05.7 items (W27, L24); v16 added M5-01.7 items (W28, L25) and updated W8; v17 added M5-02.7 items (W29, L26); v18 added M5-03.7 items (W30, L27); v19 added M5-04.7 items (W31, L28); v20 added M5-05.7 items (S14-S15, B9-B15, W32, L29-L30); v21 added M5-06.7 items (S16-S17, B16-B17, W33-W37, L31-L32; M5-06.7 was then superseded by M5-06.8, same work, because its base manifest predated commit 48f0f85); v22 adds M6-01.7 items (W38, L33). Plan (user, 2026-10-25): out-of-scope issues, critical ones too, go here instead of a replan; fix all in one sweep task added with a single plan reopen after the last task (M6-03.7).










SECURITY: S1 saga path uses ApprovalGate legacy mode: caller-supplied ctx.resource and ctx.roles, gate built without roles_of / tool_authz / resource_attrs (src/tools/sagas/activities.py). S2 Executor service-account Cedar check uses caller call.resource, not a tool->Cedar rule (src/tools/execution/__init__.py). S3 generic tools.execution.calls.call_tool / ToolActivities path runs tools without the approval gate (src/tools/execution/). Note for S3: agents.topology.executor_tool also calls Executor.run without the approval gate; it is safe only because a specialist registry refuses non-read-only tools, so M3-02.7 must route specialist writes through ApprovalGate (and S2: executor_tool sends no Cedar resource, so a service-account system denies by default). S4 no resource_attrs resolver: resource owner/tenant attributes still come from the caller (needs reviewed CRM read tools). S5 tool->Cedar rules live in gate config, not next to the tool in the registry (src/tools/registry/). S6 screening does not decode Base64; a Base64-only injection passes user-message screening (src/safety/screening/; Prompt Guard via Groq or a decode pass). S7 audit log is append-only but not hash-chained (src/tools/audit.py). S8 ticket workflow (M1-05) inputs/history not audited for sensitive data in Temporal (src/workflows/). S9 ApprovalGate.grant does not pass the request id to verify_approver, so the one-item binding of a staff sign-in (ID token nonce = request id) is enforced by hitl.approval.Desk.decide, not by a direct gate.grant call (src/tools/validation/approvals.py: pass request_id to the verifier). S10 the LangGraph Postgres checkpoint tables have no tenant row-level security and no integrity seal: someone with database write access could substitute a well-formed plan or state (agents.topology.checked_plan refuses malformed or inflated plans, not a valid substitute); theoretical while the checkpoint database is trusted (core.orchestrator.statechart.postgres_checkpointer: separate role / RLS, or an HMAC over the plan). S11 tools.execution.Executor.run writes no tool audit record (tools.audit is only on the saga path), so specialist tool calls through executor_tool are not audited (src/tools/execution). S12 a specialist's identity does not reach downstream systems or the audit log: on-behalf-of tokens carry act = the one agent identity (channels.identity.service._mint_obo, AGENT), and tool_audit_records has no actor_subrole column (MA-D9, MA-ADP-04 invariant 1); agents.contracts.actor(role) is recorded only as the approval request's handler.



 S13 the erasure workflow does not yet write the erasure log (deploy/backup/pgbackup.log_erasure) when an erasure completes (memory.lifecycle.inventory close / data.erasure): until it does, restoring a dump taken before an erasure brings that user back, and the drill has nothing to replay. OpenBao (the transit key that wraps every data key) is not backed up: losing it makes all encrypted fields unreadable. S14 the output checks match credentials on the raw text, so an invisible or spacing character inside one hides it: a key with a zero-width space or word joiner inside, or with its characters spaced out, is delivered (src/safety/output/checks.py: NFKC and strip format characters, collapse single-character spacing, before matching; strict xfail tests/invariants/test_injection_set.py). S15 knowledge_tombstones holds per-tenant rows (scope = the tenant id) with no row-level security: app_runtime can read every tenant's tombstoned document ids and reasons (src/knowledge/ingest/pipeline.py; listed in NO_RLS in tests/contracts/test_policy_lints.py, which fails once it is fixed). S16 the VM's current API is the hand-started development server (python -m channels.identity serve, from .venv via deploy/start-api.sh) with its mock SSO route POST /v1/identity/mock-idp open on the public IP: anyone can mint a sign-in token for any tenant and user, MFA included (checked 2026-10-31: the route answers 422 to an empty body). Left running by the user's choice until the first deploy/vm rollout, whose deploy/vm/serve.py has no mock route and refuses header sign-in. S17 the deployed DATABASE_URL user (neondb_owner) has BYPASSRLS; tenant isolation holds only on code paths that SET LOCAL ROLE app_runtime, as with the local superuser (use a non-bypass login role for the app, keeping the owner for migrations).






BUGS: B1 output sanitiser strips <placeholder> text inside code fences ('--subnet-id <id>' -> '--subnet-id ') (src/safety/output/checks.py). B2 web/dev-server.js crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT when the API drops mid-stream (writeHead only if !headersSent, else destroy). B3 tests/deploy/test_backbone.py line 4 over 110 chars (lint). B4 app HTTPS on TLS-intercepting machines needs truststore / CA handling (only the demo has it). B5 ticket workflow waits 48 h for an approval decision (src/workflows/ticket.py approval_timeout_seconds) but HL-D9 / MAX_APPROVAL_TTL / hitl.queues cancel at 72 h. B6 hitl.queues.sweep promotes a claimed hand-off once its SLA passes (for a hand-off the SLA is the time to pick-up) and unassigns it: the conversation's specialist keeps ownership (handoffs row; the one-owner index stops a second take-over) but the item reappears in queue_senior and pages the lead; escalations also have no 'resolved' status for a finished hand-off (src/hitl/queues: skip claimed hand-offs in the promotion, add a resolved status set by hand_back). B7 the output checks only catch future promises ('we will refund', 'will be credited'); a past-tense success claim ('Your refund has been processed.') passes without a verified action (src/safety/output/checks.py PROMISES; strict xfail in tests/e2e/test_scenarios_actions.py flips when fixed). B9 the output checks' PEM private-key header pattern sits behind \b, which cannot match before '-----' after a space, a line break or punctuation, so that pattern never fires; a full key block is still blocked by the entropy rule on its body (src/safety/output/checks.py CREDENTIALS; strict xfail tests/invariants/test_invariants.py). B10 triage's llm_fallback catches only parse errors (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError): a provider outage (AllProvidersFailed, a connection error) escapes triage, so Jev and the fallback model both down crashes the turn instead of asking the customer (src/core/orchestrator/triage.py; strict xfail tests/load/test_chaos.py). B11 admission's local fallback cannot see a lock held in Upstash: during a partition a second turn on a busy conversation is admitted, even with one worker (worse than L20 says; src/reliability/admission: fail closed to BUSY for a conversation the shared store cannot confirm, or keep a local mirror of held locks; strict xfail tests/load/test_chaos.py). B12 CRITICAL channels.api streams events from a sync generator, which holds one of the server's 40 worker threads (anyio's default limiter) for the life of each open stream, and the sync POST handler needs the same pool. Measured by tests/load/test_api_load.py (mocked agent, compose Postgres): 5 and 30 concurrent customers are fine; at 60, 47 of 60 status events were lost, 58 final replies never arrived and the first status p50 was 7.2 s; at 100, first status p95 8.8 s and FAQ final p95 13.2 s. AC-13 cannot pass at release load (src/channels/api/app.py: an async stream with async psycopg or LISTEN / NOTIFY; strict xfail at 60 users). B13 the stream places its cursor when its generator first runs, not when the client connects: events published in between are never delivered (seen under B12's load; the web client connects the same way) (src/channels/api/app.py: take the cursor before returning the response, or return the event id with the POST for Last-Event-ID). B14 the stream polls the outbox once a second (create_app poll_seconds=1.0), which uses the whole 1 s first-status budget: first status p95 0.91 to 1.05 s at 5 to 30 customers with no agent load (poll every 0.2 s, or LISTEN / NOTIFY). B15 tests/evals/gate/test_gate.py (M5-04.7) and tests/hitl/gate/test_gate.py share a module name in test folders without __init__.py, so a single pytest run over the whole suite fails at collection (import file mismatch): CI runs python -m pytest -q and breaks; the batched local runs hid it (rename tests/evals/gate/test_gate.py to test_release_gate.py). B16 scripts/neon_role_bootstrap.sql is invalid SQL (its DO block lacks the $$ delimiters and the role names their quotes); the working copy is in scripts/run_neon_migrate.py and deploy/vm/migrate.py. B17 deploy/setup-vm.sh assumes Ubuntu (apt-get) and the VM is Oracle Linux 9; deploy/vm/setup-ol9.sh is the one to use.










NOT YET B8 tests/tools/validation test_property_no_financial_write_at_or_above_the_threshold_runs_without_a_second_person failed once (2026-10-26) with psycopg AdminShutdown: its Postgres connection was terminated mid-test, most likely by a concurrent Postgres restart from another session; not reproduced since (545/545 green on 2026-10-27). The test and ApprovalGate hold their own connections and do not reconnect. The test also takes ~42 s, unchanged by PERF-01 (its time is not in data.migrate.psql): profile it in the sweep.









WIRED: W1 governance require_sign_off() not in the statechart; disclose() not in the API reply path (src/safety/governance/). W2 conversation memory not wired into dispatch / context assembler; summarizer prompt is injected, none written (src/memory/conversation/). W3 facts: activation scoring for the 15% profile slot, the resolution / 24 h idle write trigger, ALLOWED_TOOL_FIELDS is an example list (src/memory/facts/). W4 no CI lint that every tool field declares sensitivity (review() runs at registration). W5 a DENY does not yet feed the turn's circuit breaker (src/core/recovery/ + turn loop). W6 tool-output blobs (tool-output/<tenant>/<case>/) not in the erasure inventory and no TTL (src/memory/lifecycle/). W7 approval card delivery to the specialist console / event stream: expected in M2-10 (the card itself is hitl.approval.Desk.card). W8 observability.tracing.LangfuseEraser exists (M5-01.7) but is not yet a store in the erasure inventory (memory.lifecycle.inventory STORES / verify). W9 hitl.queues.Queues.sweep is a function: not yet run on a schedule (Temporal schedule or cron, per tenant). W10 alert (Slack / PagerDuty) and notify (customer inbox, UA-D2) are injected callbacks with no production implementation. W11 nothing emits escalation packets yet: confidence gate hand-offs, reflexion limit, user-requested human and approval-requiring actions must call Queues.escalate (turn loop / M2-10 handoff). W12 escalations / escalation_events (tokenized packet, customer id) not in the erasure inventory or retention (src/memory/lifecycle/). W13 MS-D18 post-wait check: an approval executed more than 1 h after staging does not re-read external state against the dry-run snapshot before running (tools.validation execute / sagas). Also: staff_directory has no admin or SCIM sync path (app_owner SQL only); specialists see PII tokens, vault reveal for authorized staff not wired (console). W14 the turn loop does not yet call hitl.handoff (wants_human -> request, mode / allowed before each turn and tool call), so co-serving and the cold hand-off are not enforced in the agent yet. W15 console sign-in is an in-process MockIdP (development): the console's OIDC redirect with a per-item nonce and its deployment (Hugging Face Spaces) are not built. W16 no customer API route for cancel(); the wait estimate is published once at request time, not refreshed as the queue moves. W17 the statechart waits for approval on amount only (execute_sop: parameters.amount >= approval_threshold); an SOP whose tool needs approval for another reason (high-risk write, unreviewed tool, Cedar approval_required) has no way into AWAITING_APPROVAL; the e2e test sets the threshold to 0 for it (src/core/orchestrator/statechart.py: take needs_approval from tools.validation's decision). W18 the turn loop has no correction detection for an action waiting for approval (the e2e test asks Jev a noul question, then Handoffs.cancel + APPROVAL_DENIED + a new episode), and no slot filler (scripted in the e2e tests). W19 agents.topology.coordinator is not yet called from the statechart's DELIBERATING stage, and a handoff plan (low lead confidence or Jev down) does not yet open an escalation in hitl.queues (turn loop wiring). W20 a specialist tool failure is reduced to its code for the model, and its detail is not written to an access-controlled, redacted diagnostic log (observability, M5). W21 agents.topology does not use agents.contracts yet: briefs and results are still dicts; its registry refuses every non-read-only tool, so SpecialistTools' solo low-risk writes are unreachable from the coordinator; for_turn needs solo (the plan's single assignment), the conversation id and the masked message; a specialist's ProposedAction is not yet routed by the coordinator to ApprovalGate.request + hitl.queues (src/agents/topology). W22 agents.merge is not wired into the coordinator's join: its human outcomes (NUMERIC_DISCREPANCY, EVIDENCE_AMBIGUITY, REDIRECT, UNVERIFIED_COMPLETION, JEV_UNAVAILABLE) do not yet open a hitl.queues escalation with a discrepancy card; a REDIRECT does not re-delegate to the missing specialist; the drafting model is not wired, and the merged reply does not yet pass the output checks and the confidence gate on its way out.

 W23 reliability.admission is not wired: channels.api POST /turns does not call admit() (409 body with active_turn_id, 429 with a Retry-After header), the turn loop does not call keep_alive / finish, AWAITING_APPROVAL does not call hold_for_approval and an approval decision or the 72 h cancellation (hitl.queues.sweep) does not release it, model and Jev completions do not call record_usage, KB_ONLY is not routed to degraded_answer, and UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL / TOKEN are not read into an Upstash store.
 W24 reliability.bursts is not wired: retrieval and tool reads do not go through SingleFlight; there is no admin API (with on-call authorization and audit) to declare or clear an incident; the turn loop does not ask incident_answer before triage; turns do not run on a Deadline (first status event, skipping reranking, the route fallbacks), and nothing classifies a turn as faq / diagnostic / multi-specialist.
 W25 backups are not installed on the VM: deploy/setup-vm.sh does not install the cron file, create /var/log/support-agent or set RESTORE_DSN_BASE; there is no warm standby (RP-D15: a kept standby_ copy would also need to join the erasure fan-out); Qdrant is not snapshotted (the index can be rebuilt from the raw snapshots in R2).
 W26 reliability.hold is not wired: the turn loop does not catch a holdable ToolFailure and call start_hold; no worker for the held-requests task queue is deployed; answer() is not the drafting model yet; the hand-over packet carries identity_tier unknown and the agent as handler.
 W27 cost.cache and cost.budgets are not wired: the turn loop does not look up the cache before generating or store eligible answers after; nothing provides the kb_version (a hash of the tenant index snapshot) or the customer product_version (identity has none); erase_document does not call AnswerCache.evict_document; model and Jev completions do not call Ledger.record; band() is not consulted (soft cap -> degraded_answer + SOFT_CAP_NOTICE); there is no admin-notification channel, tenant-admin report view, monthly reconcile job or invoice import; release_gate is not in CI (it needs cost per resolved conversation per route from the evaluation harness, M5).
 W28 tracing is not wired: services do not call observability.tracing.provider / json_logging at start-up, the turn loop, model router, Jev client and tools do not create spans with turn_attributes and gen_ai.* attributes or set support.escalated / agent.risk_tier, Temporal workers are not given temporalio.contrib.opentelemetry.TracingInterceptor (trace context across workflows), and the compose Jaeger runs in memory with no 7-day retention set (deploy/compose.yaml; Langfuse retention is a project setting).
 W29 observability.alerts is not wired: no metrics backend (Prometheus / Grafana Cloud) or alert channel (PagerDuty / Slack) is set up; nothing feeds burn_alerts with turn records or the tripwires with breaker states, OAuth token lifetimes, batch results, reranker fallbacks or the financial_writes ledger; TokenCounter is not fed by completions; classify() is not run over failed or escalated conversations, its results are not stored, and residuals have no human QA queue; observability.tracing does not tag kept spans with sampling.reason (deterministic / baseline), which estimated_cost needs.
 W30 evaluation data is not wired: eval_samples is not a store in the erasure inventory; there is no back-office route to set the evaluation opt-in, and no job that harvests opted-in production conversations; no judge model or key is configured (it must be another family than the agent: the agent runs Claude / Groq Llama / Gemini, so e.g. OpenAI or Mistral); the per-route labelled validation sets and the 200 human-labelled conversations for judge acceptance are not collected; nothing feeds retrieval_deficit with live reranker scores, re-asks, feedback and citation clicks.
 W31 the evaluation suites are not in CI: no GitHub Actions job runs the smoke tier per commit or the full tier nightly and before a release; the component suites are not yet populated with real cases for every component (the tests carry examples), and the framework seed episodes are not run through the agent; shadow mode and canary routing are not wired into the live runtime or the API; live CSAT, FCR and CES are not collected (feedback signals come in M6-01). W32 the release load test (tests/load/locustfile.py, AC-13) has not run on the VM (needs M5-06's deploy) and no release job runs it or gates on its exit code; chaos runs in process only (no staging cluster or Chaos Mesh, L21). W33 no workflow supports Continue-As-New (DL-D6): deploy/vm/release.py only refuses to swap while workflows run on code the release changes; the workflows themselves (TicketWorkflow, SagaWorkflow, HeldRequestWorkflow, ErasureWorkflow) need a drain of pending signals and workflow.continue_as_new at a release boundary. W34 no worker process: each Temporal worker needs injected activities and nothing composes them, so the VM runs the api only (no worker service in deploy/vm/compose.vm.yaml) and turns are accepted but nothing runs them (create_app's no_orchestrator). W35 the model pins in deploy/vm/models.json are not read by the code: JevClient defaults to jev-latest, there is no embedding client in src (deploy/vm/reindex.py takes an Ollama embedder), and the tier models are not configured anywhere else; the Jev version is not pinned yet (null until the user supplies it). W36 OpenBao runs in dev mode (secrets in memory): the R2 credentials the backup cron reads from it vanish on every restart, and the backup cron is not installed on the VM (W25); its paths assume /opt/support-agent. W37 the VM checkout (~/Enterprise-Support-Agent, main at a75b5ca) carries uncommitted copies of the deploy helpers since committed as 48f0f85, so a rollout's preflight refuses until it is reset to a commit; deploy/vm is not on the VM until it is pushed. W38 improvement.feedback is not wired: no API route takes a thumbs, the survey card is not in the web widget, the turn loop does not emit re-ask / abandonment / reopen signals, hitl.handoff draft verdicts and hitl.approval rejections do not call Feedback.reason_code, the pager is an injected callback (W10), feedback_events is not a store in the erasure inventory, the weekly review and live_metrics are not scheduled or fed to the release gate (W31), and observability.alerts.classify still returns its own Failure enum (mapped by taxonomy.FROM_ANALYZER, not replaced).
ACCEPTED LIMITS / DESIGN DEBT: L1 no pgvector (nearest facts in Python). L2 legal archive: no legal holds, no General Counsel dual sign-off, Postgres not S3 Object Lock; its tokens lose their values after erasure. L3 the Redis turn lock now exists (reliability.admission) but is not wired (W23), so the Postgres PK still sequences turns; no P2 alert for pin budget; so the 72 h cancel has no mutex to release. L4 fact TTL uses valid_from as last-confirmed; old versions of a live fact stay until the lineage expires (plain FK). L5 Temporal ticket history TTL via namespace retention. L6 'prod' -> 'production' synonyms refused (agent asks). L7 non-USD money actions denied until a trusted FX source exists (DECISION-bdad33ce). L8 hazard scorer is a stub in tests/demo (Llama Guard needs a model pull). L9 SPEC FR-7 says OBO tokens last 24 h; code and UA-D9 say 15 min (doc fix). L10 a business day is counted as 24 h for significant-decision SLAs (no business calendar). L11 queue priority is Jev acuity then SLA deadline; contract tier does not affect it, and promotion to the senior queue keeps the original (breached) deadline. L12 the wait estimate uses a fixed 10-minute service time per specialist, not Erlang A or measured rates. L13 HL-D10's Jev categorisation of free-text feedback is not built: feedback is reason codes only and the edited draft text is not stored. L14 Cedar has no credential-reset action; the e2e reset is authorized as restart_cluster (a production change) on the instance's environment (policies/: add the action when the tool is real). L15 MA-D8's shared turn token budget (16,000 tokens, forced join at 90%) is not enforced: steps are the only ceiling in agents.topology (add with the briefs' token accounting). L16 'solo' means the only specialist dispatched in the turn (a dependent running alone after the lead does not count); SpecialistTools validates with the gate and then writes through the executor, two steps without a shared lock (the gate re-decides on current state; a change in between is caught by the read-back, not prevented). L17 ConversationReader is not registered as a tool and its characters are not charged to a shared turn budget (with L15). L18 specialist claims travel as a JSON list in a result's findings until agents.topology carries agents.contracts (W21); the merge's completed-action check is a phrase list, like the output checks' (B7). L19 PERF-01 (one reused psycopg connection per database in data.migrate.psql, for test speed) was dropped by the user on 2026-10-27: task rejected, src/data/migrate.py reverted to one docker exec psql per query; the reverted change is kept as a patch outside the repo. Tests stay slow; revisit in the sweep if speed matters. L20 admission uses fixed one-minute windows, not a continuous token bucket (a burst across a window boundary can reach twice the rate); the Upstash fallback is per process (v1 runs one worker; with several, the one-turn guarantee would not hold during an outage, and locks taken locally are not visible in Upstash after it recovers); tests use a fake Upstash REST server, not a real one. L21 RP-D9 autoscaling with pre-warmed minimums is infrastructure (Kubernetes) that v1 does not have (one VM); incidents and coalescing live in one process; the latency budgets are design limits, not yet measured p95 (no load test).
